News.title: The one baby name that experts say nobody is using - but totally needs to
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Finding the perfect name for a baby can be stressful for parents during pregnancy - but one expert says a name is being unused and you should totally snatch it up.

Colleen Slagen is a baby name expert who is known on Instagram as “namingbebe.” She is now pushing for the name that ranks 6,250th in popularity to move up the list.

It’s Mamie.

“It’s a name that I feel should be amongst the top 100 popular names. I could totally see this name being mainstream, and yet it’s insanely uncommon,” Slagen told the Today Show’s webpage.

In her video, Slagen notes the name ranked 6,250th on the U.S. Social Security Administration list of baby names in 2025. Only 19 families chose to name their kid Mamie.

A baby name expert is arguing for one name to skyrocket up the list of most popular ( AFP via Getty Images )

“Historically, it was a nickname for Mary or Margaret, or Mary-Margaret, and it means pearl. Could also be a nickname for Marie, Marian, Marguerite, or something like Matilda Marie, Maeve Margaret,” she says.

While some might note that Mamie is the word for grandma in French, Slagen argues other names used for grandmas, such as Poppy and Gigi, are still used for kids.

“Guarantee if you start hearing this out and about, you're gonna have name envy,” she says.

Slagen revealed she started thinking about the name because Merlyn Steep’s daughter used Mamie despite her real name being Mary Willa.

“This name has big first lady energy, Mamie Eisenhower. I would use this name, but it pretty much rhymes with my first daughter's name,” Slagen notes in her video.

News.title: Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card
News.content:
Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

News.title: Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury
News.content:
This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”

News.title: Wallabies humiliated in ‘unacceptable’ thrashing by New Zealand
News.content:
New Zealand blew Australia off the field in an extraordinary first-half display in Sydney as they claimed a 13th successive win against the Wallabies and completed a 2-0 Bledisloe Cup clean sweep.

The annual series had already gone New Zealand’s way for a 24th successive year at Eden Park last weekend, but Australia did enough in a highly competitive first half in Auckland to suggest they could give the All Blacks a game on their home turf. And in a breathless opening six minutes in Sydney, it looked as if they might.

The ball-in-play time during that opening spell was incredible as both teams committed to fast, attacking rugby, offloading from everywhere. Like two heavyweights going toe-to-toe in the opening round of a boxing contest, throwing haymakers to see who would get knocked out first.

Ryan Lonergan produced an excellent turnover for the Wallabies to trigger an Australia counter, and the irrepressible Peter Lakai responded with one for the visitors, as the ball travelled from one end of the pitch to the other in one long unbroken spell.

But after New Zealand wing Josh Moorby finally crossed the whitewash, it was Australia who found themselves out on their feet, punch drunk.

News.title: England’s Rugby League World Cup hopes in tatters after Tonga defeat
News.content:
McDermott was full of credit. “They’re a big team, a strong team,” he said. “They’ve got some tremendous players in there, and I thought we stuck toe-to-toe with them for nearly all the game.

“They scored some tries through kicks, which are always hard to defend, and then towards the back-end of the game we made some errors chasing the scoreboard.”

It should be factored in that this was McDermott’s first match in charge and strides have clearly been made since England were woeful in losing the Ashes 3-0 last year.

“I thought we opened up Tonga in that first 20,” McDermott added. “Whether we went through the middle or the edge, we found ourselves in a good ball position, but we had some scrappy finishes to the good ball sets. It was too erratic. We wanted to put a load of fatigue into Tonga, but credit to them. I thought they were terrific defensively.”

Having been beaten by Samoa in the World Cup four years ago, England must face up to the burgeoning conviction that they are no longer among the top three countries in international rugby league. There was the palpable sense of the old order being changed in a stadium packed with the red shirts of Tonga.

As Williams said in the build-up, this is a “mad” format, with only the top two from the combined six-team group of Pool B and C going through to the semi-finals, but now it is very simple as far as England are concerned. They must beat France and Papua New Guinea in their remaining two matches, and do so heavily, then pray that Tonga can beat Samoa in the last match of the pool stage. However, Samoa thumped France 78-4 on Friday, so even that potential avenue appears blocked. McDermott has no other option but to look ahead.

“We know what’s in front of us now, we’ve got to win the next two games and improve on the things we need to improve on,” he said. “But I’ve seen enough tonight that is telling me we’re heading in the right direction.

“It would be tremendously disrespectful to either France or PNG to suggest we’re going to rack up points. I can start looking at points difference and start working out our strategies, but the road will lead us back to winning those two games, and winning them in a strong way.”

Team details

England Radley, Pearce-Paul, Nsemba (King 62), Thompson (Harvard 29, Currie 69), O’Neill (Litten 58); Brimson (Nsemba 79), Young, Savala, Farnworth, Eckersley, Williams, Smith, King (Walters 33, Thompson 76).

Tonga Frizell (Vaimauga 28, Taumalolo 64), Wong (Olakau’atu 41), Olakau’atu (Fonua-Blake 38, Utoikamanu 66), Taumalolo (Halasima 31), Foketi; Hopoate, Watene-Zelezniak, Koula, Toia, Fifita, Fainu (Lolohea 17), Katoa, Fonua-Blake (Utoikamanu 21, Wong 52).

Referee Gerard Sutton (Australia).

England’s Rugby League World Cup challenge could well be over, just 80 minutes after it started.

Brian McDermott’s hopes of qualifying for the semi-finals were all but shattered in his side’s first pool match in a brutal encounter in which Pacific Island physicality and passion ultimately earned Tonga a famous victory.

England displayed huge attacking courage with their offload strategy – in all, they made 26 – but their adventurous intent could not find the finishing touch and was not enough to topple a ferocious opposition defence in Perth. Despite excellent performances from captain George Williams and Dom Young, they were ultimately blown off HBF Park.

On their seventh attempt, this was Tonga’s first win over England and although this intense contest was for, so long, much closer than the scoreboard finally showed, there can be no doubting the excellence of Kristian Woolf’s team and the ruthlessness they displayed in the last quarter in which they never stopped tackling refused to stop coming.

News.title: ‘The boats don’t stop’: The deadly coastline that has become a trafficking superhighway
News.content:
The dangers were illustrated earlier this month, when a boat carrying more than 300 migrants sank near Obock on its way to Yemen. At least 139 people drowned, including 15 children. There were 700 drownings or people lost at sea on the route in 2025.

“The boats don’t stop, day or night,” the local coastguard chief told the Telegraph as he looked out at the waterway, walkie-talkie in hand, one day earlier this month.

The chief, who declined to be named, pointed to skiffs and fishing boats moored in a lagoon outside his outpost, that he had confiscated from smugglers and traffickers.

The world has become familiar with the 18-mile-wide Bab el-Mandeb strait as one of the globe’s most congested and strategically important maritime choke points.

Sitting to the south of the Suez Canal, the East-West artery flowing through the strait carries approximately 12 to 15 percent of global maritime trade.

What is less well known is that there is also a migration superhighway running across the strait, linking Africa via Djibouti to Yemen and the Gulf beyond.

Many tens of thousands of people cross the waterway each year and while Yemeni refugees fleeing the Houthi offensive have made headlines in recent weeks, the majority of those braving the waterway are heading the other way.

This maritime migrant route out of Africa has recently been busier than all the crossings across the Mediterranean into Europe, according to the International Organisation for Migration (IOM).

The IOM estimates there were nearly 64,000 crossings across the Bab el-Mandeb in the first four months of 2026, compared with a total of just over 23,000 across the Western, Eastern and central routes of the Med.

The vast majority heading east are Ethiopians so desperate to find work in the Gulf that they are prepared to trek through war-torn Yemen, which has been tipped into a humanitarian crisis by its civil war.

The IOM recorded some 202,000 migrant trips into Djibouti from Ethiopia in 2025 and by early October, the figure for 2026 had already hit 177,000.

The reignited war in Ethiopia’s Tigray region is expected to increase the numbers wanting to leave, yet the exodus is also being held up by escalating fighting along Yemen’s coast between Houthis and the government.

Fewer are now able to get across the strait, leaving them stranded on the western side, or forced to take more dangerous routes.

News.title: Asia’s vaccine self-sufficiency drive gets $650m boost
News.content:
An “innovative” partnership to boost vaccine security across Southeast Asia will inject up to $650 million into regional manufacturing, in a bid to reduce reliance on imported shots.

The five-year initiative, announced at the annual meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund in Bangkok on Friday, will see major lenders, non-profits, and the private sector come together to invest in the region’s vaccine industry.

Currently Southeast Asia’s production base remains limited and exposed. The majority of shots are imported, and any capacity the region does have is highly concentrated – one analysis this year estimates 60 to 90 per cent sits with a single vaccine manufacturer.

Even before Covid-19 hit, this vulnerability was recognised. The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), a regional bloc of 11 countries, endorsed a vaccine security and self-reliance initiative in 2019, driven by Thailand’s National Vaccine Institute (NVI).

These concerns have mounted since the pandemic, but up until now investment as well as political will has been lacking. The partnership announced on Friday, led by NVI, hopes to remedy this, and develop a model that can be copied worldwide.

​​“If we can do it here in Asia, then that really provides a model for the world,” said Aurélia Nguyen, deputy CEO of the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi), a a vaccine research non-profit. “We can build it out in Africa, in Latin America, and that really gives us the resilience that we want the next time we have a major epidemic.”

Cepi has committed up to $20 million of “catalytic funding” for the programme, which is backed by the World Bank as well as organisations like the Singapore-based AVPN investment network.

In all, the package of loans and grants will include at least $174m in public financing, and up to $460m in private capital mobilisation for regional vaccine manufacturing. Further details, including recipients, have not yet been announced.

But Paschal Donohoe, the managing director and chief knowledge officer of the World Bank Group, told a panel in the Thai capital that “we believe this has the ability over time to mobilise up to $650m of finance”.

He added that the group would use public loans and grants alongside investments by its private-sector arm, the IFC, while its guarantee arm, MIGA, would help cover investors against risk.

“It’s really important because each element of the World Bank Group is involved in it,” Donohoe said. “We’re not just talking the talk, but walking the walk.”

Speaking to the Telegraph after the event, Nguyen added: “Innovative models and partnerships like this, where we’re each bringing a piece to de-risk scientific technology, [allow us] to leverage larger quantities of capital.

“But I think what’s also helpful in this model is, beyond the financing, [we] have a sort of coordinating umbrella through Asean,” she said. “So you can be smart and [avoid] duplicating investments, which brings commercial sustainability and resilience for health systems.”

Nakorn Premsri, the director of NVI, added that the investment model will help “build a more sustainable and resilient regional vaccine ecosystem, to meet both routine needs and the demands of health emergencies”.

News.title: Bank tax would raise mortgage costs, warns UBS
News.content:
Bank stocks have fallen on fears that John Healey will launch a tax raid on the sector in the Budget.

NatWest and Lloyds Banking Group shares were both down more than 2pc in early trading on the London Stock Exchange as investors responded to news the Chancellor is poised to raise taxes on the industry.

The banking sector has come into Mr Healey’s focus after their earnings were boosted by higher interest rates caused by the Iran war.

He is understood to be planning to target lenders despite praising banks at an International Monetary Fund (IMF) event in Bangkok on Thursday.

He said: “They’re a big contributor to the economy.

“They’re an important part of our business. They’re a part of the jewel, if you like, in the British economic crown.” Here is what you need to know.

5) Cult London cinema beloved by Tarantino saved from closure | The Prince Charles Cinema secures its future with 25-year lease after bitter landlord dispute

What happened overnight

Asian shares mostly rose a day after a tech sell-off dragged stocks lower.

South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index jumped 3.6pc, after tumbling 7.6pc on Thursday. Samsung Electronics was up 4.2pc, while memory chipmaker SK Hynix added 3.5pc.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 1.9pc to 65,658.59, after falling 4.9pc a day earlier. OpenAI investor SoftBank climbed 1.7pc. Chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron was 2.8pc higher and memory chipmaker Kioxia advanced 3.2pc.

The Asian technology stocks traded higher after losses in AI shares moderated in the US.

Kevin Warsh, the chairman of the US Federal Reserve, said Friday at the IMF and World Bank gathering in ⁠Bangkok that AI could bring about positive impacts to global economies.

He said: “I’d say, the advent of this new technology is probably the most consequential change to the U.S. and the global economy in my lifetime.

“There really is, I think, a huge benefit to the global economy, the US economy, over the horizon.”

Taiwan’s Taiex, which also benefited from the AI frenzy, was up 0.6pc. But shares of TSMC, or Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, were 0.4pc lower even as it posted record quarterly profits on Thursday and said AI demand remained very strong.

In Indonesia, the Jakarta Composite index fell more than 10pc, the lowest in years, after MSCI said Indonesia’s continued classification as an emerging market would be “no longer appropriate.”

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng gained 1.2pc to 24,353.69. The Shanghai Composite index rose 1pc to 3,742.66.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 was 1.1pc higher at 8,812.90.

India’s Sensex edged up 0.2pc.

News.title: Are my smart home devices always watching me? How to stay safe (and private) in a connected house
News.content:
The past decade has seen a huge rise in the number of smart devices in the home, from video doorbells to robot vacuum cleaners.

Smart connectivity offers many useful upsides, from letting us keep an eye on package deliveries to streamlining household chores. However, concerns remain about whether these devices are safe from hackers and how they might impinge on our privacy.

As a technology journalist for almost 20 years, I have reviewed many smart appliances and have lots of connected devices in my own home, so I’m an experienced user. To find out more about their potential downsides, and how to keep yourself protected, I’ve also spoken to an expert from cybersecurity firm Kaspersky, a board member at the Connected Standards Alliance (CSA) – which promotes openness and safety within smart-device networks – as well as other leading brands in the space.

What is a smart appliance?

A smart appliance connects to your home network, often via Wi-Fi, to allow for a wider range of interactions. That might be a washing machine that notifies you when it’s finished, or a fridge-freezer such as the Samsung Family Hub with a screen and voice controls.

But smart appliances don’t have to be huge: connected lightbulbs, baby monitors, smart plugs and more can all link up with your home network, in many cases integrating with voice assistants such as Amazon’s Alexa or Apple’s Siri.

Sports.title: Ex-Ukraine national footballer killed in war with Russia as body found 20 months after heartbreaking last call to wife
Sports.content:
Next

A FORMER Ukrainian national team footballer has been killed while fighting against Russia – 20 months after he first went missing.

Roman Maksymyuk made a heartbreaking final call to his wife on January 30, 2025 before disappearing from the frontline.



Now, a DNA match with his daughter Daria has confirmed the soldier’s death in Vladimir Putin’s bloodthirsty war.

Roman previously played as a midfielder for Ukrainian clubs Dynamo Kyiv, Dnipro, Volyn, Chornomorets and Prykarpattia.



Between 1998 and 2002 he played five matches for Ukraine’s national team before retiring in 2011.

After Putin invaded Ukraine in 2022 the former footballer joined the war effort as a gunner in the 25th Sicheslav Airborne Brigade.

He was last seen trying to break out of an encirclement in the embattled Donetsk region – the site of severe bloodshed over the last four years.

Roman was 50 years old when he went missing in action.

In what would become his last phonecall with his wife Vera, he told her that he was heading into the dangerous Pokrovsk area in Donetsk and that he may not make contact for a long time.

Tragically, his loved ones never heard from him again.



Family and friends hoped he had managed to escape the meatgrinder frontline – but devastating DNA test results confirmed his body was a match with daughter Daria.

In June last year the Ukrainian national team wore Roman’s jersey and military jacket in tribute to their fallen player in a friendly against Canada.

It comes after Putin last night blitzed 15 sites across Ukraine, killing nine and wounding a further 90.



It marked one of Putin’s largest attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukraine with a barrage of missiles and more than 300 drones.

Ukraine have also been ramping up their attacks – and recently unveiled a lethal new “Thor Hammer” strike drone.

The mid-range weapon can carry warheads of up to 50kg and blitz through the skies at breakneck speeds of up to 180km/h.

On Friday Volodymyr Zelensky’s forces launched a devastating blitz on one of Vladimir Putin’s key chemical hubs.

Swarms of drones pummelled the chemical plant – which lay more than 3,000km behind the frontline – and sparked a huge inferno.



Brit-made sea drones also exploded a Russian port in a fresh blow to Putin’s trade routes across the Black Sea.

Extraordinary footage showed K3 Scout speedboats hurtling towards Vladimir Putin‘s forces during a combat operation last month.

The Ukrainian president initially halted attacks on Russia’s oil hubs – before the US president struck a deal with Putin to buy off millions of tonnes of diesel.

Sports.title: LaLiga sides set to play 67 minutes of clash behind closed doors after postponement controversy
Sports.content:
Next

RAYO VALLECANO have been ordered to play the rest of their abandoned clash against Athletic Bilbao behind closed doors – after fans repeatedly launched projectiles.

The LaLiga sides were still looking to break the deadlock when their clash at the Estadio de Vallecas descended into chaos last weekend.



Furious Rayo fans threw paper aeroplanes onto the pitch in protest against owner and president Raul Martin Presa.

And both sets of players were dragged off the pitch by referee Jose Maria Sanchez Martinez.



When the showdown restarted, following Rayo stars Oscar Valentin and Isi Palazon’s decision to speak to ultras, more objects were tossed from the stands.

It led to the clash being postponed – following advice from police – and the hosts have now been slapped with huge sanctions.

LaLiga chiefs have controversially ruled the remaining 67 minutes of the contest must be played behind closed doors.

And Rayo are also being forced to cover all travel and accommodation expenses for Athletic Bilbao as preparations are made for the rearranged fixture.

If both clubs cannot reach a private alternative agreement, the visitors will submit their invoices to the judge.

LaLiga bigwigs insist their decision to lock fans out of the Estadio de Vallecas is a preventative measure to stop the encounter being suspended again.

Sports.title: Haaland and Semenyo seen limping after Man City win over Ipswich amid fears FIVE stars could be ruled out
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER CITY have been dealt a double injury scare after Erling Haaland and Antoine Semenyo were both spotted limping following their victory over Ipswich Town.

Enzo Maresca‘s side secured another important win against the Tractor Boys but the celebrations were overshadowed by concerns over two of their attacking stars.



Haaland was seen walking with a heavy limp as he left the pitch at full-time, having suffered a painful knock to his foot during the game.

The Norwegian striker scored twice in the game to help his side to a 3-2 win and ensured they continued their perfect start to the season.



And there was further concern for Maresca as Semenyo was also spotted limping off the pitch after the final whistle, raising fears of another potential injury setback.

On top of the three players who finished the game limping, Mateo Kovacic, Matheus Nunes and Nico O’Reilly were all substituted after picking up knocks.



The worrying injury concerns threaten to take the shine off City’s hard-fought victory over Ipswich.

Maresca was forced to shuffle his pack during the contest as his players struggled with a series of fitness problems.

And the sight of several stars struggling physically will be particularly concerning for the City boss as the fixtures continue to pile up.

The Italian now faces an anxious wait to discover the extent of the injuries, with his medical team expected to assess the affected players.

Losing Haaland and Semenyo would be a particularly frustrating blow, given their importance to City’s attacking options.

The games are coming thick and fast.

City face AEK Athens in the Champions League on Tuesday evening.

And with a crucial clash against Aston Villa looming next Saturday, Maresca will be desperate to have as many of his key players available as possible.

Sports.title: Brentford 1 Liverpool 2: Isak bags winner as Reds battle to crucial victory over nine-man Bees
Sports.content:
Next

LIVERPOOL’s £400million Fab Four attack has finally clicked into gear as Alexander Isak sealed a comeback win over nine-man Brentford.

For only the second time in this season’s Premier League, boss Andoni Iraola was able to field the formidable quartet of Isak (£125million), Bradley Barcola (£123million), Florian Wirtz (£100million) and Victor Munoz (£35.5million).



And though that unit were goalless at home to Fulham last month, they combined superbly in the red-and-white half of West London.

Though the Bees had led thanks to Keane Lewis-Potter’s first-half header, the dismissal of Yehor Yarmoliuk before half-time impacted them significantly as they played with 10 men until Vitaly Janelt went off in the 91st minute.



And then Liverpool scored twice in eight second-half minutes, with all four men getting involved, to put their Prem season back on track.

First it was Wirtz to Munoz for the equaliser on 62 minutes and then Barcola to match-winner Isak – his fifth goal of the season – as Brentford suffered their first loss at the Gtech Community Stadium since February 21.



Barcola is undoubtedly a quality player – he is, after all, a two-time Champions League and a France first-teamer – but that assist aside, he has yet to really show English fans what he is capable of.

The former PSG winger scored a hat-trick in last Wednesday’s crazy 6-3 win over Austrian side LASK but he fluffed his big moment here.

And assuming he has a reasonable grasp of English, he would not have been amused by chants of “what a waste of money” from cruel Brentford fans in the West Stand.

Twenty minutes into the first half, on a cold and blustering autumnal afternoon, and Barcola cleverly took advantage of Janelt’s careless header towards his own goal.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Having outpaced Yarmoliuk, Barcola only had Bees goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher, a former Liverpool player, to beat for his first Prem goal.

The Frenchman’s finish, however, was regrettable as he scooped his attempt wide and then Lewis-Potter screamed in his face to emphasise what a squandered moment that was.

With minutes of the first half left, Liverpool were awarded a penalty by referee John Brooks but slow motion replays showed it was the wrong call.

It was, in fact, a fantastic challenge as Brentford’s Dango Ouattara managed to nick the ball with his right heel away from Alexis Mac Allister.

And this is where VAR works best – anyone who saw that incident again would have realised it was NOT a penalty, and Brooks changed his mind once he had viewed a pitchside monitor.



Things got even worse for Liverpool moments later when Lewis-Potter, the smallest man on the pitch, scored with a magnificent header that fizzed past Brazilian goalkeeper Alisson Becker.

Thiago delivered the chipped cross and the Liverpool defence, which has been vulnerable throughout this season, switched off completely as the 5ft 7in full-back attacked the delivery.

Brentford just needed to see out the first half but in a lengthy stoppage-time period, Yarmoliuk was sent off for violent conduct.

It might have been tame and Liverpool centre-back Jeremy Jacquet did not exactly need a trip to A&E but Brooks brandished the red card because the Brentford man had “committed a headbutting action”.

There was no penalty, of course, because the ball was not in play at that point of the incident.



The second half brought better news for visiting supporters and Wirtz – subject of much criticism in recent weeks – showed why he is well considered in Germany with a smart pass for Munoz.

And the Spaniard, once he had checked on to his weaker left foot, found the net with a cute finish.

On 70 minutes, club-record signing Isak celebrated just his ninth goal since moving to Merseyside for big money from Newcastle when he latched on to Barcola’s knockdown.



It was a feather in the cap for Iraola, who had never beaten Brentford in six attempts as Bournemouth boss.

Yet his medical team had a busy afternoon as Hungarian Dominik Szoboszlai, back in the starting line-up following a hamstring strain, hobbled off after 32 minutes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And Jeremie Frimpong lasted just SEVEN minutes of the second half before he returned to the dressing room.

Brentford manager Keith Andrews, a Liverpool fan growing up in Ireland, was not amused that his captain Janelt was shown a second yellow card when he tripped 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha outside the box.

Sports.title: Fulham 1 Hull 0: Alex Iwobi nets only goal to earn under-fire Arbeloa huge win amid sack fears
Sports.content:
Next

ALVARO ARBELOA tasted his first victory as a Premier League boss and eased the pressure on his future job prospects.

A deflected first half goal from forward Alex Iwobi made the numerical difference, but Fulham were applauded off their home pitch by their picky fans as they celebrated a much deserved – and overdue – win.



Not even an added time sending off for sub Ryan Sessegnon dampened the mood as drizzle fell on Craven Cottage.

Arbeloa has been under increasing pressure over his team selection and substitutions with his team sitting last place in the table.



He has also faced accusations that his players switch off when they get their noses in front.

But the shy Spaniard answered all those questions as Fulham threatened to overwhelm Hull City, whose inspiring start to the season following promotion is slowly running out of steam following a second defeat in four league games.

Arbeloa has endured a sticky start to relations with the fans for not acknowledging them at the end of games. He says it is not in his character but applauded the Hammersmith End at the final whistle along with his players.

In addition to Iwobi’s winner, Fulham hit the bar through striker Gonzalo Garcia and created a string of chances via lively forwards Josh King, Iwobi and Oscar Bobb.

Hull were lucky to keep it down to one thanks to two stunning one-footed saves from keeper Konstantinos Tzalakis.

It was all Fulham from the off but then again they have not had a problem with getting their noses in front this season, seeing games out has been the issue.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Lively front three Alex Iwobi, Josh King and Oscar Bobb were filling their boots in a one-sided match.

Their overwhelming superiority triggered the solitary goal when City defender Brooke Norton-Cuffy hit an underwhelming defensive pass under pressure straight to midfielder Sander Berge.

He laid off for Iwobi to drill a shot home from 15 yards out.

Arbeloa’s team were in control from start to finish, only losing it momentarily when sub Sessegnon launched himself at City sub Robinio Vaz to earn a straight red card.

Sports.title: Man City 3 Ipswich 2: Haaland nets brace as City maintain 100 per cent record in front of thousands of bananas
Sports.content:
Next

EVERYONE in the Premier League is waiting for the answer of Manchester City’s appeal against their widescale breaches of financial rules.

But no top-flight side has an answer to Erling Haaland.



The great goalscoring entertainer is proving that no matter what trouble his club might be in off the pitch, he’s still as prolific on it.

His double downed Ipswich to take his red-hot form to 12 goals in his last eight City games in all competitions.



And the only thing that might stop the Norwegian colossus is the sight of him limping off down the Etihad tunnel at full-time.

What always felt like an inevitable double from him, plus Phil Foden’s opener, means Enzo Maresca now holds the record of being the first manager in the Prem era to win SEVEN successive opening games.

Only an offside ruling robbed the Norwegian of a hat-trick.

Maresca made that new mark having rested £340million-worth of stars in Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo from the start.

Those demanding the downfall of the Abu Dhabi Etihad empire might be forgiven for thinking the Italian was thumbing his nose at them with that selection.

All that expense sitting on the bench representing the kind of talent most of City’s rivals – and the visiting Tractor Boys – would give their eye teeth for.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Certainly the massed home ranks, sporting thousands of former player Imre Varadi’s bright yellow inflatables, showed they don’t give a Fyffe about what the greater football public may think of their club.

Bile poured down from all but the dark blue visiting section as the Prem anthem was played before kick-off – while those from East Anglia spouted: “Same old City, always cheating.”

Maresca had predicted that Foden would score on his return from the three-match ban he suffered for his controversial red card against Manchester United.

The Italian got it spot-on, and so did the playmaker with the smoothest of left-foot finishes.

Just 60 seconds before that strike Jeremy Doku slid over a pass from which Ruben Dias forced a fine fingertip save from Christian Walton.



The Belgian left winger went into repeat mode to find Foden in the 18th minute.

City, as the midweek 4-2 Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain showed are a more unpredictable and edgier side since Maresca replaced Pep Guardiola.

That can leave them more open at the back and three minutes after Foden’s opener Marc Guehi was left completely exposed to Daizen Maeda’s charge down the right flank from Abdul Ouatarra’s fine pass.



The Japanese attacker brushed past the defender’s challenge and gave Gianluigi Donnarumma no chance with a stunning shot.

By the 29th minute Haaland had restored the lead, moving on to a perfect cross from Mato Kovacic and powering home.

The Norwegian goal machine was signed from Borussia Dortmund in 2022 for £51.4m so cannot be lumped into the sham shame that lasted nine years until 2018.

Yet cynics would be entitled to ask whether the striker – one of the most wanted in world football – would have chosen City were it not for the dominance they had created by cooking the books for so long.

The bread-and-butter finish made it 173 goals in 208 appearances.



With the quality of the players at his disposal Maresca clearly has a great opportunity of landing his first Prem title, with Kovacic replaced by £125m Fernandez just after the break.

Now that is a luxury but one that had to be put to use for as Ipswich boss Gary O’Neill had promised, his side didn’t arrive just to make up the numbers.

But in the end City’s numbers just proved too much for them, and Haaland’s numbers just keep going up.



He claimed his second of the game in the 69th minute after Iliman Ndiaye, who had worked relentlessly down the right flank, set off on another drive.

Haaland read his intentions perfectly, timing his run to meet the low cross and he bullied his way past Ouatarra to smash home.

And yes, those City fans who will not accept they support the club seen as the biggest cheats ever in the game, went bananas as the ball hit the net.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sub Zian Flemming smacked home a 90th-minute penalty after Guehi dumped Abdul Fatawu in a game that referee Farai Hallam decreed should have a dozen minutes added on.

Suddenly Ipswich now had hope when all seemed gone. But Maresca’s machine just motored on.

Sports.title: Premier League trio including Man City star refuse to take knee as initiative returns
Sports.content:
Premier League trio including Man City star refuse to take knee as initiative returns

Premier League matches have seen the reintroduction of taking the knee, but several players opted to stand while the anti-racism gesture was being observed before kick-off on Saturday

View 2 Images The taking the knee initiative has returned in October

A trio of Premier League players, including Manchester City's Marc Guehi, refused to take the knee on Saturday as the 'No Room For Racism' month of action began.

‌



‌



The England defender chose to remain standing before their clash with Ipswich at the Etihad, whilst on the opposing team fellow defender Issa Diop also refused to take the knee.

‌



Earlier in the afternoon, prior to Everton's loss to Chelsea, Ainsley Maitland-Niles refused to kneel despite everyone else on the pitch doing so.

‌



Neither of them have spoken out but it is well documented that several players believe the gesture, which began in the aftermath of the Covid lockdown, has lost its value.

‌



Players and staff have the opportunity to perform the pre-match gesture for the next two weeks in October. The Premier League have maintained their "commitment to tackling discrimination and highlight the importance of diversity in football".

Ahead of the 2021/22 season, Luton stated that they would not be taking the knee and instead all stood in the centre circle. That was at a time when players were still taking the knee before every game, but that idea came to an end in August 2022.

A decision was then made to limit the gesture so that it only took place during match rounds that fall during the No Room For Racism initiative. It was agreed by Premier League captains ahead of the season that they would continue to perform the gesture twice per season.

‌



View 2 Images Ainsley Maitland-Niles stood whilst others took the knee during the lunchtime kick-off (Image: TNT Sports)

In 2021 ex-Crystal Palace star Wilfried Zaha described kneeling as "degrading" and then Brentford frontman Ivan Toney said: "We are kind of being used as puppets, in my eyes; take the knee and the people at the top can rest for a while now, which is pretty silly and pretty pointless. Nothing is changing."

The move started in the UK in 2020 following the death in US police custody of George Floyd, which sparked the Black Lives Matter movement.

FIFA quietly dish out two punishments to World Cup winners Spain

Spain handed double FIFA punishment following Islamophobic chanting during Egypt friendly

FIFA have fined Spain $20,000 (£15,000) and ordered a partial stadium closure following Islamophobic chanting during their friendly against Egypt in March. The chants were heard during the first half and again at the start of the second period.

‌



‌



A section of supporters were reportedly heard singing: "Bote, bote, bote, musulman el que no bote," which translates as "Jump, jump, jump, whoever doesn’t jump is a Muslim."

‌



An anti-discrimination message was subsequently displayed inside the stadium condemning 'Islamophobic and xenophobic' chanting. FIFA launched disciplinary proceedings against the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) following the incident, with Spain manager Luis de la Fuente among those to condemn the behaviour.

‌

Sports.title: Chelsea address poor record to end Everton's unbeaten start as horror injury overshadows win
Sports.content:
Chelsea ended Everton's unbeaten start to the season as they won for the first time on the road since the opening weekend in a game that was overshadowed by a serious injury to Emi Martinez.

The Blues, since seeing off Fulham, had been beaten at Arsenal and Brentford but produced a perfect away day performance to secure three points at Everton.

David Moyes' side had won two and drawn four of their six games heading into the lunchtime kick-off, but Pedro Neto's brace saw the Blues secure a victory that sees them jump into the top four, at least temporarily.

Martinez and Jarrad Branthwaite clashed as they both went for an Everton set piece, with the concern immediately evident on the faces of those nearby. The Everton defender was able to stand up and continue after some prolonger treatment.

‌

The Argentine goalkeeper though remained laying on the ground with several medical staff tending to him. He was eventually taken off on a stretcher with Mike Prenders coming on for the first 15 minutes. Martinez was carried off to a round of applause.

In a first-half that lacked in quality it was Moises Caicedo who was centimetres away producing a Goal of the Season contender. The midfielder was the target of a corner, floated to the back post, before he volleyed it first time, only to see his effort hammer the bar. Up the other end Emi Martinez needed to be alert to tip over a Jack Grealish effort.

‌



But Chelsea needed only 44 seconds on the second-half to take the lead, Jorrel Hato driving into the Everton box before his cross found Petro Neto. The Portuguese's effort into the bottom corner beat Jordan Pickford, who could only get a hand to it.

Joao Pedro missed a major chance to double the Chelsea lead in the latter stages as the Blues broke on the Everton goal, but Pickford was on hand to deny the Brazilian.

View 3 Images Emi Martinez was taken off on a stretcher after a serious collision

However Neto was on hand to score his second of the afternoon as the clock hit 90 minutes. The wing-back coming up with an opportunistic strike having reacted quickest to a blocked free-kick.

‌



Fast starts continue

We've been accustomed to seeing Chelsea take the lead in the early stages. In their first four games they were ahead inside ten minutes. Against Arsenal and Fulham they needed only two minutes to get themselves in front.

At Everton the game was slow to get going, but the Blues showcased their ability to get going fast once the whistle for the second-half blew. They were able to catch their opponents napping and a combination of a smart Morgan Rogers back heel, Hato's driving run and pass and Neto's finish handed Chelsea the game's opening goal.

View 3 Images Moises Caicedo was so close to a stunning first-half strike

From then on they didn't need to press the agenda. In more recent games they've seemingly operated on a 'we'll outscore you' plan. Seeing off Fulham 3-2 and Brighton 4-3. But this time they showed a more measured approach.

‌



It also ended Chelsea's horror recent record on the blue half of Merseyside. Coming into Saturday's contest they'd won just one of their last nine visits to Everton, the majority of those coming at Goodison Park.

They were beaten 3-0 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium only seven months ago during Liam Rosenior's short-lived reign, but made efforts to atone for that loss as Xabi Alonso's side got back on track with his side registering a first clean sheet in nine months.

Chelsea's Emi Martinez forced off on stretcher after huge collision and lengthy delay

The goalkeeper has been stretchered off during Chelsea's Premier League clash with Everton following a clash of heads with Jarrad Branthwaite

Emiliano Martinez was stretchered off during Chelsea's clash with Everton following a nasty collision with defender Jarrad Branthwaite. The incident occurred around the hour mark, with play halted for a lengthy period as medical staff attended to both players.

The incident followed a free-kick for the hosts, with Martinez and Branthwaite both challenging for the ball before colliding heads. Both players received medical attention on the pitch, but Martinez was ultimately stretchered off.

Manchester United are tracking Real Betis forward Troy Parrott, who has a £67.5m release clause, with scouts sent to watch the Republic of Ireland international in action

Manchester United are weighing up a stunning move for ex-Tottenham forward Troy Parrott, with the club said to have 'sent officials' to Spain to watch him in action for Real Betis.

‌



‌



Parrott, 24, departed Spurs in 2024 to sign for Dutch outfit AZ Alkmaar in a £6.7million permanent deal. During his spell in the Netherlands, the Republic of Ireland international put up some eye-catching goalscoring figures, netting 51 times in 97 appearances across all competitions.

‌



Those numbers, combined with a consistent scoring record for Ireland, earned him a £17m switch to Betis over the summer. Since arriving in Spain, Parrott has continued to impress, chipping in with two goals and one assist in seven matches this season.

‌

Speculation has been mounting that Tottenham could look to lure Parrott back to north London, as Roberto De Zerbi seeks to bolster his attacking options. However, Spurs are far from the only Premier League side thought to be circling.

‌



According to Fichero, Parrott's displays have 'sparked serious interest' from the English top-flight, with United believed to be firmly in the running. It is understood the Red Devils are on the hunt for a No.9 with potential who can hit the ground running, having opted against signing a new centre-forward during the summer transfer window. This is where Parrott would enter the frame with his 'link-up play, physical strength, and clinical finishing'.

View 2 Images Troy Parrott (Image: Mandatory Credit ©INPHO/Ryan Byrne)

United are monitoring his development closely and have dispatched scouts to observe him in action for Betis in both La Liga and the Champions League. Manuel Pellegrini's outfit have been in exceptional form this season, collecting 19 points from a possible 24 in the league and a perfect six from six in Europe's premier club tournament.

However, while Michael Carrick's squad are believed to hold an interest in Parrott, there is no suggestion, at present, of United pursuing further moves for the striker. He is tied down until 2031 with a release clause set at £67.5million, a sum that may deter prospective buyers, United included.

Benjamin Sesko remains the primary striker at United, though he has battled with injuries and continues to be sidelined. At present, there are legitimate worries about when the Slovenian international might return to fitness.

United chose not to recruit a deputy for Sesko during the summer and kept Joshua Zirkzee as their alternative option despite it appearing the Dutch forward would depart on transfer deadline day, a choice that certain fans regard as misguided.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Points deduction size emerges as Premier League rivals 'fuming'
Sports.content:
Football finance expert Kieran Maguire has claimed Manchester City must be deduced "multiple double figures of points" after breaching Premier League financial rules.

Maguire said: "The redacted report sets out year by year how much the sham contracts contributed to the artificial commercial revenue. Over the rolling three-year period, in some years we could be talking about a £350million difference. That would shatter all records for PSR compliance.

"Everton and Nottingham Forest's deductions covered a single breach in a single year, an overspend of no more than £20million. So is there a ceiling on what can be deducted? And the sanctions hearing could already have taken place. Because City are appealing and everyone has NDAs, we might not know the sanction until the appeal result. But it has to be multiple double figures of points, before you start the calculations.

"I worked out that if you add up nine years of Champions League non-participation for individual clubs at an average of £50million a time, around £20million for the Europa League, plus potential claims from players who missed bonuses, the Premier League's legal fees and a fine, we're talking in excess of a billion pounds regardless of the points deduction.

When asked about the possibility of City being kicked out of the Premier League, Maguire responded: "I think it would be a very unusual vote. We did see Bury get expelled from League Two some time ago but I think that the other clubs would have to bear in mind that Manchester City would probably take legal redress and that could prove to be very expensive if they are expelled without the verdict being held and without the appeal. So it's a risky path to tread, but the strength of feeling does vary from club to club.

"Certainly some of the other elite clubs are very unhappy with the delay in the situation because they feel it has an impact upon their ability to qualify for the Champions League. I think some of the more mid-tier clubs who don't see Manchester City as a threat, their main concern is, is this going to further increase the already sky-high legal costs that have been incurred by the Premier League and they don't want any part of it.

"So, they want a quick resolution and then they can get on with the rest of their season and focus on their own clubs."

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd star lifts lid on crippling addiction that plagued playing career
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd star lifts lid on crippling addiction that plagued playing career

Ex-Manchester United and Sunderland striker Fraizer Campbell has discussed his addiction to snus, the tobacco product, which has become increasingly used by footballers

View 2 Images Fraizer Campbell has discussed his addiction, which came when he was at Crystal Palace

Former Premier League striker Fraizer Campbell has opened up about how he was addicted to snus throughout his playing career, later struggling to deal with the impact of it.

‌



‌



Campbell made 446 appearances for the likes of Manchester United, Sunderland, Hull and Crystal Palace before retiring in 2022. It was during his three-year stint at Selhurst Park that he admits he was addicted to the nicotine product.

‌



Snus is a smokeless tobacco product made from ground or pulverised leaves, packaged similar to a teabag sachet, which an individual would place under their top lip.

‌



Campbell says he originally took it to wind down after games, but he continued taking it after retirement and that's when he began struggling to deal with some of its effects.

‌



He said on The Sports Agents podcast: “I felt relaxed, and it just chilled me out more than anything. It was after a game as well, and after a game, it’s one of those things that it’s quite hard to relax after.”

Campbell would concede he became addicted, which the product itself warns of, but always stayed away from them on matchdays in fear of becoming too relaxed. “Well, yeah. I definitely was addicted," he confessed.

"But obviously, when I had more time on my hands when I retired, I had more time to have the snus. So obviously, in the morning, while I was playing, I might have one in the morning or two in the morning and then for the next couple of hours I’d be out on the training pitch.

‌



View 2 Images The striker came through the ranks at Man Utd

“I would never have them on a match day because it chilled me out too much, and I was someone that… I’m a pretty chill person as it is. If I was more chilled, I’d struggle to get into a jog.”

Campbell, who says he's now clean, concedes: “It got a lot worse after I finished playing football, but I didn’t really see the negative side of it while I was playing."

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Real Madrid deal transfer blow as secret meeting comes to light
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Real Madrid deal transfer blow as secret meeting comes to light

A look at the latest headlines surrounding Arsenal as they gear up for a trip to Nottingham Forest in the Premier League

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has suffered a setback in the transfer market concerning one prominent Arsenal target (Image: David Price, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Premier League champions Arsenal travel to Nottingham Forest on Sunday for the latest examination of their title credentials. The Gunners have started strongly in their bid for back-to-back crowns but it's Manchester City who are out in front.

‌



‌



Mikel Arteta's side have started this season much as they ended the last and are well in the hunt for multiple pieces of silverware. That being said, the manager and other backroom star will have eyes on the transfer market to assess how to improve the squad.

‌



One target in particular may not be on their way to the Emirates next year, however, following disappointing news this week. Mirror Football covers all the latest news around Arsenal as the club looks to continue their recent reign of prosperity.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Guler won't be a Gooner

Arda Guler seemingly won't be on his way to north London anytime soon after reportedly agreeing to fresh terms with Real Madrid. The attacker has been linked with the Gunners for a number of years but is purportedly on the verge of signing a two-year extension at the Bernabeu.

Arsenal eye shock transfer for Bayern Munich flop with backroom figure leading the charge READ MORE :

Guler, whose current contract is due to expire in 2029, was previously subject to concerns over his playing time under Jose Mourinho. However, those appear to have been put to bed after he's pitched in with one goal and five assists in nine appearances this season, setting up two goals in Wednesday's narrow Champions League win over Roma.

‌



It's a potential blow for Arsenal if the English giants had indeed planned to make their own move on the player. That will be effectively unfeasible if he puts pen to paper on a new deal that won't expire for another four-and-a-half years.

The Gunners are well-stocked for wing options as things stand, especially on the right flank where Guler often operates. Bukayo Saka looks likely to have that area locked down for years to come and Guler is too talented to play a back-up role.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The same may not be said for the No. 10 role, however, where Martin Odegaard has functioned for most of this season. The Norway captain continues to deliver but has had injury issues in past seasons, while Arsenal will want to plan for the post-Odegaard era.

A new contract is Guler's reward for worming his way into Real's XI, a project that first started when Arteta's friend Xabi Alonso was in charge. That progress has only continued under Mourinho, who appears adamant on ensuring the Turkey international stays put.

Merino reveals 'secret meeting'

View 2 Images Mikel Merino has opened up about the secret player meeting he feels sealed last season's Premier League title for Arsenal (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Mikel Merino has revealed how a secret meeting among Arsenal's squad got their Premier League title push over the line. Merino spent a large portion of the title-winning campaign injured but still had some key moments in a historic season.

The Gunners unnerved fans with certain results, including blowing a 2-0 lead to draw against Wolves in January, as well as losing to Manchester City and Bournemouth in April. However, Merino opened up about how the players took it upon themselves to ensure they were mentally prepared to end the club's 22-year drought.

"One slip, and all we heard was ‘same old Arsenal’. To be honest, there were doubts inside the team too," he wrote for the Players Tribune. "Giving away a 2–0 lead should never happen. But the day after the game, the players had a meeting inside the dressing room, without the boss. Everyone spoke up.

‌



"Nobody talked about tactics. This was about how a group of human beings handle adversity together. I spoke about how I saw the team from the outside, and I said that this was something we as players had to handle, because the boss couldn’t do everything for us.

"When one person has so many tasks at one club, you need leaders who can figure things out on their own. Well, at this club, we do.

"In my view, that was the day we won the title. Even when we lost to Bournemouth and City, that meeting kept us together. We decided to use all the criticism as fuel, and thanks to social media we saw everything."

Sports.title: Kartal hails mentality after 'dream come true' run to Wuhan Open final
Sports.content:
Britain's Sonay Kartal says making her maiden WTA 1000 final at the Wuhan Open is a "dream come true," adding that the mental side of sport is "one of my strongest assets."

Kartal became only the second British woman, after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019), to reach a WTA 1000 final with a stunning 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory over Jelena Ostapenko.

The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, saved multiple set points to punish Ostapenko, despite the Latvian hitting an astonishing 50 winners in the match.

Kartal will take on Maja Chwalinska in Sunday's final, live on Sky Sports Tennis from 11.30am, after the French Open finalist upset fellow Pole and former world No 1 Iga Swiatek 7-5 6-1.

"Today was a dream come true," Kartal told media.

"I've been shooting to get this far in one of these events for a very long time and to be able to do it this fast after so long out, is special.

"I think for me to have had in my box today all the people that got me feeling fit and ready to go and injury-free, it's a special moment for me and a special moment for the rest of my team."

Currently 170th in the WTA rankings, Kartal - the lowest-ranked player to reach the final in Wuhan - will break inside the top 50 and become the new British No 1

Since the format's introduction in 1990, Kartal has become just the second player to defeat five former finalists en route to a WTA-1000 final, after Naomi Osaka in Montreal in 2005.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kartal described reaching her first ever WTA 1000 final as a huge milestone after beating Jelena Ostapenko to make the Wuhan Open last two

'I've been underdog in every match here'

Her victory over Ostapenko extended a remarkable series of wins against former Olympic champion Belinda Bencic, ex-Wimbledon finalist Jasmine Paolini, and world No 6 Elina Svitolina.

"I think in every match, I've kind of been the underdog in this event," she added. "So I think the only pressure is kind of the pressure that I'm putting on myself.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Wuhan Open quarter-final between Elina Svitolina and Kartal

"Regardless of how long I spent out, I still expect to offer a good performance and I'm very proud of what I've managed to achieve this week.

"There's a lot of first-time things that I've managed to do. So with each match, I've grown in confidence, and the atmosphere today was amazing.

"It's a special feeling to walk out onto that court. The battle was a true battle, it's what I expected. And I'm very proud of just how I handled the occasion and everything that was going on in the match."

'The mental side of sport one of my strongest assets'

After reaching the fourth round of Indian Wells in March, Kartal missed three of this year's four Grand Slams, including Wimbledon after six months out with a stress fracture in her back, returning last month at the Billie Jean King Cup Finals.

Previously ranked as high as No 44 in the world, she showed positive signs by reaching the third round in Beijing earlier this month, but scarcely could have expected such a level of success so soon.

"I think mentally, it is one of my biggest assets on the tennis court. I think I managed to stay very calm in a lot of situations that can probably get a little heated and you can get frustrated with.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kartal discussed her back injury after reaching the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open and whether she will get a celebratory tattoo if she wins

"I just really try and use that to my advantage. I can maybe see her getting a bit upset and emotional on the other side, so I know at that point it's time for me to just knuckle down and not let her distract me.

"But yeah, I've been lucky mentally, I think a lot of players have to work on it, but for me, it's just something that's always been ingrained in me.

"I think also having no pressure this week has obviously helped, and with each win, you just gain more confidence. I think this week there's been an accumulation of a lot of good things that have helped me keep my composure."

Fleming: Kartal playing the tennis of her life

Sky Sports Tennis' Colin Fleming on Sonay Kartal:

"Her ability to stay in the present got her through. She kept cool to ultimately outlast Ostapenko, who hit 50 winners past her and still couldn't win a set.

"Just a brilliant achievement and the run doesn't stop here. She's playing the tennis of her life and she's got every chance of getting her hands on the title.

"It's just so impressive the way she takes it all in her stride. Fascinating to hear her say this was a win for her mentality because it did carry her across the line in both sets when Ostapenko was losing it really.

"Kartal was there, composed, and ready to take her chances when it came. Every reason for me to think she's going to play a good match in the final. I'm not saying she's going to win but that's exciting to know.

"I have full confidence she's going to handle that occasion, play her tennis, which has been exceptional this week, and assuming she does that she'll give herself every chance."

Sports.title: Kiltie double helps Kilmarnock beat fellow-strugglers Motherwell
Sports.content:
Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom of the Scottish Premiership with a 3-2 victory over Motherwell.

Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann's side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point off bottom-placed Hibernian.

Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie's second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head.

But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.

Given their run, Motherwell fans would have feared the worst when their team gifted Kilmarnock a goal with little over 60 seconds on the clock.

Goalkeeper Alex Paulsen misplaced a short pass into central midfield and Kiltie ultimately converted after some desperate defending.

Worse almost followed several moments later when Well centre-back Martin Moorman lost possession midway inside his own half, but Joe Hugill dragged his shot wide.

But the visitors levelled in the 17th minute when Lukas Fadinger sent Emmanual Longelo down the left wing. Calum Ferrie made a great stop after Palmer-Houlden got on the end of the left-back's low cross but Lowry kept his composure to fire the rebound into the bottom corner.

Motherwell took control as Killie struggled to keep possession inside their own half. Maswanshise hit the post from 25 yards and scuffed a decent chance wide, and Ibrahim Said forced a good save from Ferrie.

Neil McCann brought on Jamie Brandon for on-loan Hearts right-back MJ Kamson-Kamara in the 33rd minute in a bid to deal with the twin threat of Longelo and Said. He was forced into another change two minutes later when the injured Bailey Rice went off for Aaron Tshibola.

The hosts improved towards the end of the half. Paulsen got down well to stop a John-Jules drive after Motherwell failed to deal with a long ball and the unmarked Tom Lowery volleyed well over.

Killie were grateful for a VAR intervention after referee Calum Scott sent George Stanger off for a high boot on Lowry. The punishment was downgraded to a yellow card after a trip to the monitor.

Motherwell were soon in front in the 56th minute after a low cross from Said. Palmer-Houlden was denied at close range by Ferrie but the ball ricocheted in off the centre-forward.

The visitors' lead only lasted two minutes. Two Motherwell defenders were barged off the ball as Brandon headed the ball back into the box after a half-cleared corner and John-Jules produced an emphatic finish.

Brandon delivered another assist when his crossfield pass played in Kiltie, who again slotted into the far corner.

Paulsen made saves from substitute Ieuan Owen and Hugill to keep Motherwell in it.

Alfred Johansson's side struggled to create chances though, and Ferrie saved from Johnny Koutroumbis deep in stoppage time when the substitute found himself in a good position.

Sports.title: Murrell scores two as Falkirk claim Edinburgh double by beating Hibs
Sports.content:
Falkirk registered a stunning Edinburgh double as they put Hibs to the sword with a 2-1 win in an entertaining Scottish Premiership clash at Easter Road.

The Bairns' only other league victory this term was against Hearts in September.

In a game that went from end to end in the cold Edinburgh sunshine, Jacob Murrell had Falkirk 2-0 ahead inside 37 minutes, before Hibs struck back with an Owen Elding goal. Hibs dominated the second half, but couldn't bag an equaliser.

Hibs boss Marink Reedijk made three changes from their 1-0 defeat at Dundee United last weekend, with Azeem Abdulai, Adam Mayor and Martin Boyle replacing Jack Iredale, Callum Wright and Ante Suto.

John McGlynn made a single change from Falkirk's defeat at home to Dundee, with Scott Tanser in for Leon McCann.

Hibs created a chance after four minutes when Tanser's corner from the right fell to Felix Passlack and when his shot was blocked, the rebound was sliced wide of the right post by Thibault Klidje.

But Falkirk took the lead after 13 minutes when Ryan Strain played a superb ball forward for Murrell to latch on to and thunder a shot past goalkeeper Raphael Sallinger into the right corner.

Strain's low shot was then comfortably saved by Sallinger after 23 minutes before Hibs' best chance fell to Boyle on the half-hour, but he was denied by the feet of Scott Bain.

Klidje fired high and wide of the left post 60 seconds later, and Mayor let fly with a shot from distance that cleared the bar 36 minutes in.

But more slack play by Hibs let Falkirk in for their second goal after 37 minutes.

Klidje's back-heel pass in the right corner let in Ethan Ross, and his cross was whipped past Sallinger by Murrell for his fourth goal of the season.

Hibs pulled a goal back on 41 minutes when Passlack's cross from the right was chested in by Elding, with VAR clearing a hand-ball check.

Image: Hibernian's Owen Elding scored to make it 2-1

Falkirk thought they had scored a third on the stroke of half-time, but Finley Barbrook was flagged offside before his header hit the net.

Abdulai was sent through on the right on 47 minutes, but sliced high and wide of the left post. Elding was through on goal two minutes later, but Bain slid out superbly to whip the ball off his toes.

Hibs were awarded a penalty on 53 minutes when Liam Henderson was adjudged to have pulled down Klidje, which VAR reduced to a free-kick just outside the box, which was fired over by Boyle.

Barbrook nearly set up a third on 80 minutes, but Owen Eames' shot was cleared off the line. At the other end, Jamie McGrath forced a terrific save from Bain to keep Falkirk ahead.

Sports.title: Improved second-half display helps Aberdeen beat St Mirren
Sports.content:
Aberdeen returned to winning ways in the Scottish Premiership as a 3-1 victory over St Mirren moved them above their opponents, who have now lost five straight matches.

Brad Lyons gave the hosts the lead in spectacular fashion after just two minutes, but the Buddies went on to dominate the first half and levelled through Eseosa Sule.

A much-improved second-half display saw strikes from Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua earn the Dons three points.

Lyons opened the scoring when he drove forward from Conor Ronan's pass and unleashed a spectacular 22-yard effort into the top corner, clipping the crossbar on the way in.

Dons goalkeeper Marius Muller had to be alert to save from Killian Phillips after a Declan John cutback, with Mats Knoester sliding in to block the former Aberdeen loanee's rebound effort.

A Luke Thomas cross saw Muller save again from Sule's header, before Aberdeen finally showed signs of growing back into the game - Nisbet was presented with two headed opportunities in the space of three minutes.

But St Mirren were the more dangerous, and while Muller once again denied Phillips from a curling effort, Saints were level three minutes before the break.

Marcus Fraser's superb switch to the far side saw Thomas hold the ball up for Phillips, whose cut-back was swept home at the far post by Sule.

Aberdeen made two substitutions and a change of formation at the break as they looked to gain a foothold, with Tony Yogane flashing an effort over the crossbar before fellow replacement Stuart Armstrong saw an effort ruled out for offside.

But they were back in front before the hour.

Paul Nsio hauled down Yogane on the edge of the area, and although referee John Beaton initially awarded a free-kick, a VAR review upgraded the call to a penalty.

Image: Aberdeen's Kevin Nisbet (L) celebrates scoring to make it 2-1

Nisbet's initial effort was weak and well saved by Jacob Chapman, but the goalkeeper could not hold on to the ball and the Dons captain drilled home at the second attempt.

They extended their lead after 72 minutes as Mouloua, barely on the park for 60 seconds, latched onto Afeez Aremu's quick free-kick to beat the St Mirren line and curl the ball into the bottom-right corner.
