Sports.title: Ombudsman simply supreme in Champion Stakes
Sports.content:
Ombudsman exacted Qatar Racing Champion Stakes revenge on Calandagan to come out on top with a show-stopping performance at Ascot.

It was Francis-Henri Graffard's French raider who took home the spoils 12 months ago, but this time around there was a decisive verdict in favour of John and Thady Gosden's home favourite, who obliged as the 5-4 market leader.

With the six-strong field heading into the home straight grouped tightly, the stage was set for Ombudsman to demonstrate the blistering turn of foot that has often been a hallmark of his career.

When William Buick asked him to quicken, he scorched past eventual third Bay City Roller before seeing off Calandagan to banish Juddmonte International disappointment and prove he is truly one of the best middle-distance horses on the planet.

John Gosden said: "I thought William was riding him very confidently in the straight and I thought, 'when are you going to go?'. He showed that turn of foot.

"The ground today is on the slow side of good, he can handle that, at York he just spun his wheels, but today it was back to seeing what he is.

"We set nice, even fractions - Rab (Havlin) on Devil's Advocate - there was no plan to go fast, slow, pull it up, we talked about that before, solid even fractions. A special performance from a special horse.

"We got a little too far back in this race last year, way back, 10, 11 lengths off it, so we thought we're not going to do that again.

"This time the race went perfectly, he rode him just how he wanted to and he's a top-class horse when we get it right. I think we got the tactics a little faulty last year, but don't take anything away from Calandagan, he won well."

On whether Ombudsman runs again, Gosden said: "Either he will go to stud or I will discuss with His Highness Sheikh Mohammed if he would like to consider putting him in the Breeders' Cup Turf, that's the only other option now.

"Golden Horn didn't enjoy it at Keeneland because it was like a sandpit when he ran and it rained three inches, but this horse, he'd handle it well, he's quick, he's agile, he could have sat on the lead if he'd wanted to today.

"He's the right type of horse and I think the track would suit him so it's a possibility; we don't have to make a rapid decision.

"The best mile-and-a-quarter horse (I've trained), definitely. I don't know if he's the best, he's going to stud so I'd better say yes hadn't I because that helps sell the nominations!"

Thady Gosden said: "To have a horse of this calibre winning on a day like today is fantastic.

"The race at York just didn't pan out for him, it was nobody's fault and we can't control the weather. He just had a nice freshen up after it and came here in good form.

"He's a year older than last year, still retains his enthusiasm and is always full of it.

"To beat a horse like Calandagan takes some doing, we found that out last year and he went all around the world proving it, but today was our turn."

Buick said: "They are two great racehorses, him and Calandgan, they produced a great race last year and it was our turn today.

"I don't think he'd have any problems going to America, obviously it would be his first time at a mile and a half but I'd leave that up to John and Thady and the team.

"It's difficult to rate his performances, you've got to remember he's been very good in winning the Prince of Wales' twice, but he was very good here today. You could pick a lot of his performances, this being certainly one."

Sports.title: Wrexham thump four past dismal Preston
Sports.content:
Wrexham eased the pressure on Phil Parkinson with a 4-1 Sky Bet Championship win over rock-bottom Preston.

Joe Worrall scored his first goal in more than two years and, after Alfie Devine briefly brought Preston level, former Lilywhites midfielder Ben Whiteman struck next to score his first goal in Wrexham colours.

Sam Smith gave the hosts breathing space just before the hour and Kieffer Moore killed it off moments later.

In a week that had seen former Liverpool skipper Steven Gerrard linked with the manager's job, Wrexham's third league win of the season was a vital one as they moved up to 14th.

But Preston remain stuck on four points from 11 games, with Graham Alexander having lost his first three games in charge.

Parkinson got a big show of support from the home fans before kick-off but his side started on the back foot, with Worrall heading Odel Offiah's lobbed effort off the line before Andrew Hughes headed narrowly wide.

Parkinson had made four changes, bringing in Smith to add more firepower, but it took some time for them to start to put any pressure on struggling Preston.

Callum O'Hare's stabbed effort was pushed around the post by Daniel Iversen and Smith had a low shot saved before the breakthrough came from an unlikely source.

Worrall, a summer signing from Burnley, had not scored since a late winner for Besiktas against Rizespor in May 2024, but the big defender rose highest to head in Danny Imray's curled cross on his home debut.

That was a little bit of unwanted history for Preston, who equalled a club record set in 1969-70 for the longest run of league matches without a clean sheet at 26.

But Wrexham have been struggling at the back themselves this term, with their only clean sheet coming in a goalless draw with Swansea, and five minutes later the visitors were level.

Moore lost possession in midfield and Preston quickly worked it wide to Johnny Kenny. His angled shot was deflected but the ball fell for Devine who made no mistake for his first goal since March - and Preston's first since Alexander took over last month.

Wrexham's second was a painful one for the visitors. Imray's cross was only half-cleared and fell for former Preston man Whiteman to hit a low shot which left Iversen wrong-footed and the midfielder almost apologetically celebrating.

O'Hare might have killed it in first-half stoppage time as he burst into the box but his close-range shot was blocked.

Preston had chances to get back into it early in the second half but Brad Potts, just on as a substitute, missed the target at the end of a sweeping counter.

That quickly proved costly as Smith headed in Whiteman's corner moments later, with Moore then ending the contest as he flicked in Callum Doyle's low free-kick.

The managers

Wrexham's Phil Parkinson:

"I thought the lads stood up and were counted today individually and collectively.

"A lot of really solid performances from the lads.

"It was great to get back in with the lads on Thursday, galvanise the group, and look at the detail of where we needed to improve, and I thought the lads implemented (it) so well.

"I could go through a lot of individuals who I'm so pleased with, because we showed character, we showed mentality. It's an important win for us."

Preston's Graham Alexander:

"We just conceded goals that we shouldn't. And I think if you look at the opportunities we had, certainly at the start of the second half when it was 2-1, if we take one of those it's potentially a different game.

"But we've got a little bit of a soft spot at the moment that gets exposed at this level and we have to work out how to fix it.

"I haven't got magic dust. We have to work. But I still think there's improvements and I have to look at whether I'm asking too much of the players at this moment considering where we are."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Sorry Derby beaten at home by Stoke
Sports.content:
Luke Graham scored his first goal for Stoke as they won 1-0 at Pride Park to pile more pressure on struggling Derby.

The Scotland defender headed in a free-kick early in the second half and that was enough to settle a scrappy contest.

Derby, who are missing a number of key players, battled away and nearly snatched a point when David Ozoh's shot was superbly saved by goalkeeper Viktor Johansson.

The win keeps Stoke in the top eight and leaves Derby in the bottom three still searching for a first home win of an increasingly difficult season.

Stoke had the first chance of a sunny but chilly afternoon when Lamine Cisse broke forward and pulled the ball to Jack McGlynn but his low shot lacked the power to trouble Josh Vickers.

Carlton Morris looked to have got away from Bosun Lawal who appeared to trip the Derby striker but referee Oliver Langford waved away protests.

The game became increasingly scrappy but the Rams ended the first half with a corner that fell to Sammie Szmodics but his goalbound shot was blocked by a defender.

Stoke had failed to build on a promising start and had been guilty of giving the ball away, so boss Mark Robins would have been expecting a big improvement in the second half.

His players responded by taking the lead in the 49th minute through Graham who met Ethan Galbraith's free-kick with a header that Vickers got a hand to but the ball went in off his left post.

Derby responded with Ozoh getting the better of Lawal but he hesitated and his shot was blocked.

They had another chance in the 63rd minute when Rhian Brewster shot narrowly wide from the edge of the area and for the first time in the match, Derby were putting Stoke under pressure.

But the visitors almost got a second on the break in the 84th minute with Ben Johnson sliding a pass across to Justin Devenny who could not get a strong enough contact on his shot.

It nearly proved costly because Derby were denied an equaliser by a brilliant save from Johansson who plunged to his right to keep out Ozoh's low drive in the 89th minute.

The managers

Derby's John Eustace:

"We asked for a reaction after Wednesday's first 45 minutes and we certainly got that.

"I was very proud of the effort of the group today, we battled against a very good team and limited them to next to nothing. We created some decent chances ourselves, so to lose the game is frustrating.

"It is what it is at the moment, we're not getting much luck. It's a frustrating period for us but this is the Championship, teams go through periods like this and I think we've got a valid reason why it's been difficult.

"We've got six or seven starters (missing) who would come into the team and make us stronger, but with the effort of the group up to now we could easily have got a couple more wins so it's important we keep believing in the process.

"The injuries haven't helped, we're going through a difficult period but we'll come through it. Also, it's my job to win games, there's no excuses. My head's on the door and I understand we haven't won enough games at the moment and it's my responsibility."

Stoke's Mark Robins:

"We gave the ball away too often and in one or two areas we looked tired but we dug out another three points.

"They threw everything at us but we defended really well, we got blocks in, we stopped crosses and broke things up and started counter-attacks, but we gave the ball away too cheaply in really poor areas which gave them momentum, hope and belief.

"It wasn't a game for the purists by any stretch of the imagination, but it was one that you can learn an awful lot from and an awful lot about your players.

"I think we'd have gone under last year but we didn't, we found the resilience to see the game out and that was really pleasing on the back of a three-game week. You can't underestimate how difficult that is."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Sheff Utd battle to narrow win at Bristol City
Sports.content:
Oliver Arblaster's early strike and a strong defensive display saw Sheffield United take all three points from a 1-0 Championship victory over Bristol City at Ashton Gate.

The visitors took a fifth-minute lead when a headed clearance fell to Arblaster, who connected with a sweet right-footed volley from just outside the box which gave City goalkeeper Sam Tickle no chance.

It proved enough to settle a contest high on endeavour but low on entertainment from which the Blades emerged worthy winners.

For the Robins it meant a second home defeat in the space of four days without scoring a goal and their fans were quick to signal their frustration after nine minutes of stoppage time.

Image: Oliver Arblaster celebrates after giving Sheffield United an early lead at Bristol City

City midfielder Luke McNally made his first start in a home game since February 2025 when he sustained a serious knee ligament injury.

Yu Hirakawa and Rio Cardines also came in, while Blades manager Chris Wilder made five changes, bringing in Arblaster, Mark McGuinness, Harrison Burrows, Kalvin Phillips and Jordan Ayew.

The first half might have been a different story had Hirakawa capitalised on a golden opportunity to put City in front after four minutes. The winger broke clear, but with the goal gaping miscued his shot straight at United goalkeeper Michael Cooper.

The miss was made to look more costly when Arblaster fired United in front a minute later and they went on to look the better side in the opening period, winning most of the physical battles and easily nullifying City's predictable attacks.

Hirakawa did break away again in the 13th minute, this time going down under challenge inside the box but referee Ben Speedie waved away his penalty appeals.

Tom Cannon volleyed wide for United and Liam Kitching was unlucky to see a 27th-minute effort blocked for a corner as the Blades looked the more threatening outfit. The half-time whistle brought loud booing from City supporters.

Home boss Michael Skubala made two attacking changes at the start of the second half, sending on Elijah Adebayo and Jed Wallace for Scott Twine and George Tanner, but still his team failed to create much until two chances in quick succession in the 65th minute.

A Wallace shot was blocked by Burrows and from the resulting corner Dom Ballard headed over at the near post.

Soon United were pressing at the other end and Tickle did well to smother a Japhet Tanganga header on his line.

It was the visitors who looked more likely to score in the closing stages, Cannon having a shot blocked into the path of substitute Ryan One, who fired over from the rebound and also sent a late header wide.

City remained toothless and could have no complaints over the result.

The managers

Bristol City's Michael Skubala:

"We weren't good enough today. We got bullied a bit.

"But we also had the best scoring opportunity of the game before they scored and had we taken it we would have seen a totally different game.

"When you are through on goal, you have to score. That's a problem for us at the moment. If you don't take your big chances and fail to keep clean sheets you are not going to win games.

"If you score early at home the opposition have to come out and play differently. But today they were too physical for us having gone in front.

"Today we started too slowly, lost too many duels and our clearances were not strong enough. We have a lot of work to do and it's good to have a free midweek coming up."

Sheffield United's Chris Wilder:

"That goal will do Ollie's confidence the world of good. When you suffer a serious knee injury and spend over a year out, the first thing you tick off is a return to training.

"Then comes a return to playing and after that a return to top form. It has been an up and down struggle for Oli to reach that stage.

"Today, he and Kalvin Phillips were brilliant in midfield. We all know how highly Oli was rated among young midfielders before the injury and what he is capable of achieving.

"We have had a lot chucked at us recently with the timing of the goals we have conceded and the quality of them, but today our game management was spot on.

"I was particularly pleased with our first-half performance. But we expected a reaction from Bristol City in the second half and dealt with a lot of balls into our box very strongly.

"The group is high on team spirit. I'm delighted to get a clean sheet and a solid away victory from a typical Championship game, which ebbed and flowed."

What the result means and next fixtures...

3h ago 11.00 EDT Louise Taylor Newcastle’s latest attempt to play vertical football left Matthias Jaissle’s side horizontal at Coventry on Monday night. That 4-1 defeat has prompted quite an inquest on Tyneside, where Jaissle could do without his players falling flat on their faces once more when Aston Villa visit St James’ Park. Jaissle maintains that his vertical football is the brand of high-octane, aggressive attacking that Newcastle’s hierarchy believes should become the club’s default, and is the way fans want to see the team play. That argument is not without validity but it is also worth remembering that, less than a decade ago, under Rafael Benítez’s charge, Newcastle often played a low block bolstered by three at the back, rarely took unnecessary risks and improved steadily. Admittedly resources were thinner then but the fans almost universally adored Benítez and were heartbroken when he eventually tired of Mike Ashley’s ownership and resigned. Quite apart from making his dislike for chaotic football plain, the Spaniard was a realist who knew a gung-ho approach would spell relegation. Granted, tactical fashions have changed, but Jaissle could do worse than slow things down a bit and search for his inner Rafa against Villa. Sports.title: Haaland helps Maresca achieve record start as Manchester City defeat Ipswich
Sports.content:
There have been few winners in Manchester City’s guilty verdict, except highly paid lawyers and the inflatable fruit industry. The fans have suffered, being forced to question everything they have been told, while being labelled “cheats” but they were able to forget the cacophony of noise around the club as Enzo Maresca became the first manager to win his first seven games in charge of a team.

Ipswich were the latest victims, but they put up a fight in City’s first home Premier League game since being found to have breached financial rules. Defiance has fortified most of the City fanbase, who were able to see local boy Phil Foden instigate the triumph with a kiss of the badge, before an emblem of their wealth, Erling Haaland, secured the points to move six clear of the nearest challengers with a clinical double, albeit with a few scares between.

If City have felt like it has been their backs against the wall for the past few weeks, it was Ipswich’s turn on Saturday. Gary O’Neil put 11 men behind the ball whenever the hosts ventured over the halfway line as City enjoyed 90% possession in the opening quarter hour, but without truly threatening as they struggled to find space in the lowest of blocks, expertly organised and fully disciplined.

Maresca had made six changes to refresh the side and it took time to understand one another’s rhythm, with Ayyoub Bouaddi the one creating it from defensive midfield in another mature performance from the teenager.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City fans have gone back to more innocent times with their inflatable bananas. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

Rúben Dias was the first to provide a distraction from the banana waving and gallows humour chants when he thrashed a shot from 30 yards towards the top corner, only for Christian Walton to palm clear. It was inevitable what was coming as there was irrefutable evidence that City were dominant. As at Anfield, Jérémy Doku was a key instigator, showing mesmeric skill on the left of the area before finding Foden to sweep home for his first goal since mid-December.

There was an element of pantomime around the ground with the booing of the Premier League anthem, the sing-alongs and inflatables. It was fitting Marc Guéhi did not know Daizen Maeda was behind him, allowing the Ipswich man to latch on to a sublime curved through ball from Abdoul Ouattara and slot in an equaliser two minutes after the opener.

With the home fans deflated, the match reverted to the attack v defence training scenarios, with City pondering how to get the previously anonymous Haaland into the game, with banana inspiration Imre Varadi watching from the stands. Foden, buoyed up by his goal, showed skill and precision with neat footwork and a pass for the Norwegian who flashed a shot from inside the area, which was deflected over.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca has guided Manchester City a record seven-match winning start in the Premier League. Photograph: Michael Steele/Getty Images

An optimistic metaphor for the club, Haaland showed it is possible to get a better result second time around, making the most of Mateo Kovacic becoming an auxiliary winger. The header lacked power, but Walton could not keep it out, palming the ball from one hand to the other and into the net before Haaland was serenaded with the clap of bananas.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Ipswich came out after the break with greater ambition, eager to show they had thrust to add to solidity. They produced fine interplay and should have levelled when Gianluigi Donnarumma completely misjudged a corner, but was relieved to see Emersonn head against the back of a defender with the goalkeeper nowhere to be seen.

City found themselves stuck in a lull, unable to prise open Ipswich, instead having to bide their time with sideways passing. It was a test of patience and a sweeping move upfield concluded with a precision pass from Iliman Ndiaye and an aggressive finish from the striker who was later denied a hat-trick by the VAR.

The video assistants became busy late on, calling Farai Hallam over to review footage of Guéhi taking out Abdul Fatawu in the area and Zian Flemming did the rest in the 90th minute. City were left to complain about a Premier League official’s decision when 12 minutes was added on, with few knowing why, but this one concluded with a result that will not be questioned.

Sports.title: Isak completes Liverpool’s comeback win as Brentford finish with nine
Sports.content:
If this truly was the turning point for Liverpool’s spluttering forwards then they will owe a big debt of gratitude to Yehor Yarmolyuk. Brentford were 1-0 up when their midfielder saw red for a butt on Jérémy Jacquet just before half-time.

While Andoni Iraola will hope surviving one of the toughest tests the Premier League has to offer is a sign his methods are starting to take hold, the Spaniard will know it was very different contest once his side had a numerical advantage to exploit.

Brentford, whose unbeaten start to the season is over, raged at the officiating. They finished with nine men after losing Vitaly Janelt late on. John Brooks walked off to boos at full-time, although Brentford had only themselves to blame. They pressed the self-destruct button when they had Liverpool on the ropes. Yarmolyuk was foolish and Liverpool punished him.

An attack worth close to £400m rose to the occasion in the second half. Florian Wirtz, who has struggled since his £116m move from Bayer Leverkusen last year, collected his second assist of the season when he made Victor Muñoz’s equaliser.

Muñoz finished well and his strike was followed by a first assist in Liverpool colours for Bradley Barcola, whose header teed up Alexander Isak to complete the turnaround in the 70th minute and lift ILiverpool into fifth place.

There was not much between the sides before Yarmolyuk’s rush of blood to the head. Liverpool had Isak back after injury ruled him out of last week’s defeat by Manchester City and they shaded the early openings. Isak nodded over from a good position and when Janelt made an error Barcola missed a chance to build on his midweek hat-trick against LASK.

Brentford responded with a series of fast breaks. Liverpool had to be strong. They looked readier for the threat posed by Brentford than when they folded in this fixture under Arne Slot 12 months ago. Jacquet, quietly impressive in central defence, made a crucial tackle to deny Igor Thiago. The initial problem for Iraola was more that the expensive parts at his disposal in attack were not gelling.

At least Barcola was willing to look for the ball and test Michael Kayode on the left, but Wirtz was not on Isak’s wavelength during the first half. Muñoz was struggling to make an impact against Keane Lewis-Potter and Liverpool’s worries grew when they lost Dominik Szoboszlai to injury.

View image in fullscreen Yehor Yarmolyuk leaves the pitch after being shown the red card. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

With Ryan Gravenberch suspended, Iraola was light on midfield options. Trey Nyoni replaced Szoboszlai and the 19-year-old’s introduction was followed by a whirlwind spell, sparked by Liverpool having a penalty overturned when Brooks checked the pitchside monitor and realised Dango Ouattara had touched the ball first when he slid in to stop Alexis Mac Allister from running on to Isak’s cutback.

Brentford were pumped up after the video assistant referee intervention and soon had Liverpool ruing a failure to clear their lines. The ball came back at the visitors too easily. Mac Allister backed off Thiago, who crossed for Lewis-Potter to run in from left-back and direct a fine header into the top corner.

Brentford will wonder what might have been if they had kept 11 on the pitch. Instead they imploded while trying to hold out for six added minutes. There was a tussle in the area before a Liverpool corner on the left and when Jacquet went down holding his face the replays showed Yarmolyuk had taken the physicality too far.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Brentford midfielder could not complain about his dismissal. Liverpool, though, took a while to adjust in the second half. They encountered further complications when injury forced Jeremie Frimpong off seven minutes after he replaced Ronald Araújo at right-back.

Brentford were holding firm and Keith Andrews made adjustments of his own. Kevin Schade was one of two half-time changes. Mamadou Sangaré, the other player to come on, drew an important save from Alisson Becker.

Liverpool grasped for inspiration. Mac Allister let fly from distance, but Caoimhín Kelleher saved. Rio Ngumoha, on for Frimpong, produced a teasing cross for Virgil van Dijk to volley wide.

Quick Guide Brentford 1-2 Liverpool key facts Show • Florian Wirtz is the first player to create nine or more chances from open play in a Premier League game since Sadio Mané against Burnley in January 2021 (9), also for Liverpool, and first in an away match since Samir Nasri for Manchester City v Spurs in August 2011 (10). Victor Muñoz (pictured centre, with Wirtz and Trey Nyoni) scored from one of them. • Liverpool’s Alexander Isak has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford (5 goals); only Erling Haaland v Crystal Palace (6) has a better 100% rate in the competition. • Brentford received two red cards in the same league game for the first time since April 2013 against Sheffield United in League One. Opta Photograph: Peter Cziborra/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Brentford began to wobble and they were caught after committing too many players forward in the 62nd minute. Wirtz dropped back, swivelled and played a clever pass inside Lewis-Potter. Muñoz was away and this time the cheapest of Liverpool’s front four provided incision, cutting past Lewis-Potter before using his left foot to thread a low shot beyond Kelleher.

The change in mood was dramatic. Barcola sliced a volley just wide, but the second goal arrived with 20 minutes left. Wirtz combined with Mac Allister, Barcola headed the Argentina midfielder’s cross down and Isak came alive, fastening on to the ball and driving home an emphatic shot.

Brentford remained defiant. They threatened an equaliser through Thiago after Jaidon Anthony broke through on the left. They wanted a penalty when Jacquet tangled with Thiago, but it was not their day. Their unbeaten run was over when Janelt, already on a booking, picked up a second yellow for a foul on Ngumoha.

Sports.title: Pressure on Arbeloa lifted after Alex Iwobi sinks Hull for Fulham’s first win
Sports.content:
After such a dominant performance against a team so blunt going forward, it almost felt inevitable that Álvaro Arbeloa was going to be denied his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach in similar fashion as the weeks and games before. After all their chances and possession, Craven Cottage should not have been a place of nerves when Mohamed Belloumi lined up a free-kick as three minutes of stoppage time were shown.

When the Hull winger blazed that free-kick over the bar – the closest Hull had come to scoring throughout the second half – the tension was released that little bit more. Despite Ryan Sessegnon’s late red card, the full-time whistle brought a first victory of the season, courtesy of Alex Iwobi’s first-half strike, and a release from the burden of being the Premier League’s basement club.

Arbeloa’s appointment was designed to move Fulham on from Marco Silva’s pragmatic system to a more expansive style – the Spaniard brought five members of staff with him from Real Madrid and three players. This was a dominant display, with plenty of creativity, especially from the wingers Iwobi and Oscar Bobb. They started fast, with Iwobi sending a curling shot on to the roof of the net from the left and Bobb a constant threat on the right.

It was from an attack down the right that Fulham produced their goal. Hull’s left wing-back, Brooke Norton-Cuffy, held off Josh King, but failed to clear and Sander Berge poked the ball into Iwobi’s path. His first-time shot should not have troubled the goalkeeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis, but it squirmed under his rolling dive at the near post after coming through a crowd of bodies, almost in the way you would let your child score past you in the garden.

Arbeloa remained a stern presence on the touchline. Fulham had conceded late in their two previous games, against Ipswich last wSaturday and Manchester United here before the international break, with five points out of six dropped from the 88th minute onwards.

The hosts doubled down against Hull and pushed for a second before the break, with Calvin Bassey heading over and King flashing a shot across goal that Tzolakis kept out with his foot.

It was Sergej Jakirovic who needed to find answers at half-time. He replaced the 19-year-old centre-back Lucas Herrington, who had been booked for one of his fouls on the elusive King, with the midfielder Tim Iroegbunam. After a bright breakthrough season in the first team under Silva, the 19-year-old King is expected to push on under Arbeloa. He was allowed to roam against Hull’s low block and after neatly combining with Shea Charles should have doubled their lead, but his low shot was too close to Tzolakis’s feet again.

View image in fullscreen Referee Chris Kavanagh shows a red card to Ryan Sessegnon (left) of Fulham after his foul on Robinio Vaz. Photograph: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images

Tzolakis kept Hull in the game. Another smart turn from King, this time away from Semi Ajayi, preceded a chance that Iwobi, with time and the whole goal to aim at, should have buried, but he telegraphed his low effort for Tzolakis to read and smother.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

When Iwobi curled another shot wide from the edge of the area with 20 minutes to go, Arbeloa continued to wear a pensive face – and with good reason. Gonzalo García, the £40m striker who has not scored in the league since the opening weekend, somehow headed Iwobi’s cross against the bar from six yards out.

Arbeloa was criticised for his substitutions before Ipswich’s late comeback, which included the introduction of the former Real Madrid youngster Manuel Ángel for his Premier League debut. With 10 minutes to go here and defending the same 1-0 lead, he opted to bring on Fulham stalwarts Tom Cairney and Ryan Sessegnon.

Cairney almost added a second in added time while Sessegnon was sent off for planting his studs on the achilles of the Hull substitute Robinio Vaz. He exited to a standing ovation and the cheers went on long after the full-time whistle.

Sports.title: Boos for Arsenal as draw with Birmingham extends winless WSL run
Sports.content:
An equaliser from Olivia Smith averted defeat for Arsenal, but a home draw with Birmingham did little to calm fears for Renée Slegers’s future as Gunners coach. Boos accompanied the final whistle at the Emirates Stadium, as the result left Arsenal on six points from six matches and without a win in five Women’s Super League matches, the club’s longest winless run in WSL history. They are eighth in the table, nine points behind the leaders, Manchester City, who have played one game fewer.

Birmingham opened the scoring at the start of the second half when Océane Hurtré coolly tapped in after her run from the halfway line went unchecked. Alessia Russo had hit the woodwork in the first half with a diving header, among a slew of Arsenal chances as Sophie Baggaley was kept the busier of the goalkeepers.

“I don’t think we created enough in the first half,” said Slegers. “Second half is different. There was one player we needed to stop and that was Hurtré. But she came through in a fast break and a counter, we don’t defend that well enough.”

After Smith’s spectacular strike, in the 66th minute, curled from outside the area, Arsenal would not find the winning goal that might ease pressure on Slegers. Baggaley’s goalkeeping and slack finishing meant Birmingham secured their point. “We are in a scenario we’ve had too many times season,” said Slegers.

Next week for Arsenal is a north London derby with Tottenham, who kick off at Chelsea in fourth on Sunday. Slegers said: “The next game is always the next opportunity. [It’s good] we always keep going and we rise after setbacks.

“We just need to put ourselves in better positions earlier so that’s not necessary every time because it takes energy from the team having to play those scenarios. But yes, the team has been brilliant. The urgency, the willingness, the desire in the second half was really good.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Despite those boos at the final whistle, Smith said of the home fans: “They always bring out great support, [we’re] so happy to have them here. Again, disappointed not to get the result, must be frustrating for them, but they stay with us and support us.”

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Kiltie double sinks Motherwell to lift Kilmarnock
Sports.content:
Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom with a 3-2 home victory over Motherwell. Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann’s side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point above bottom-placed Hibernian.

Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie’s second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head. But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.

Falkirk secured an entertaining 2-1 win at Hibernian. Their only other league victory this term was at home to Hearts in September.

In a game that went from end to end, Jacob Murrell put Falkirk 2-0 ahead inside 37 minutes, before Hibs struck back with an Owen Elding goal. The home side dominated the second half, but could not bag an equaliser.

Aberdeen returned to winning ways as a 3-1 victory over St Mirren moved them above their opponents, who have now lost five straight matches. Brad Lyons gave the hosts the lead in spectacular fashion after two minutes, but the Buddies went on to dominate the first half and levelled through Eseosa Sule. In a much-improved second-half display strikes from Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua gave the Dons three points. Aberdeen are seventh.

Lyall Cameron’s 79th-minute strike earned Dundee United a 1-1 draw at St Johnstone. United trailed at half-time to a Josh Fowler goal, the striker’s sixth of the Premiership campaign. The league’s top scorer did not make it out for the second half due to illness and Simo Valakari’s side were unable to repeat the trick of last Sunday in Aberdeen when they successfully defended a 1-0 lead.

Jim Goodwin had too many creative and attacking options to throw at their hosts and despite a decent defensive stand from the hosts, Cameron struck the second goal of his impressive loan spell from Rangers. The clubs are locked together on 12 points in the top half of the table after encouraging starts to the campaign, with the Saints in fifth on goal difference.

Later on Saturday, second-placed Rangers can go top overnight with a win at Dundee, who are fourth. Celtic, the leaders, are at home to Hearts on Sunday.

Sports.title: Neto double at Everton leads Chelsea to victory marred by Martínez head injury
Sports.content:
Chelsea have returned from the international break with a spirit, authority and resilience that augurs well for Xabi Alonso. Their troubles at Everton, not a happy hunting ground in recent years, were confined to the seven minutes Emi Martínez needed treatment for a head injury as Pedro Neto’s double delivered a deserved victory in the Merseyside sunshine.

The Argentina goalkeeper was taken to hospital for tests after an accidental collision with Jarrad Branthwaite left him with suspected concussion. “When he left the stadium he was conscious,” Alonso said. “Hopefully it is not too bad but we need to wait.” A first Premier League clean sheet since January, and a second successive win since losing at Brentford before the Nations League break, were otherwise secured with a minimum of fuss in a commanding second-half performance.

“It’s one day,” the Chelsea manager replied when asked whether victory, built on a feisty first-half display and mature second, provided evidence of the mentality he craves at Stamford Bridge. “We need to repeat it again and again and again to know for sure but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it’s not about playing nice but playing good football, winning many second balls and being efficient. We need a game like this. The feeling at Brentford was that it was not enough. Today has been better but it’s just one. When it’s 10 clean sheets …”

There were goalkeeping problems at both ends of the field, with Jordan Pickford unconvincing for the second week in a row for Everton. David Moyes’s side edged the first half and could have legitimate complaints about Morgan Rogers avoiding a second yellow card moments before the break. But from Pickford’s weak attempt to stop Neto’s opener to Thierno Barry missing their one big chance of the contest, there were self-inflicted wounds in Everton’s first defeat of the season.

“It wasn’t that we played that badly overall,” said Moyes. “We just didn’t create enough which meant if we did anything wrong defensively it would count against us.” So it proved.

There was more needle than quality in the first half and Rogers, already booked, was extremely fortunate to avoid a second yellow card from the referee, Paul Tierney, when leaping into a challenge with James Garner. The Chelsea forward caught the ball and the man. The tackle could be considered just as reckless as the one that brought an earlier booking for Harrison Armstrong.

Barry wasted Everton’s best chance when heading a Jack Grealish cross straight at Martínez from close range. Another big miss from Barry was one of several recurring themes that undermined Everton’s afternoon.

View image in fullscreen Pedro Neto shows his delight after giving Chelsea the lead. Photograph: Molly Darlington/Getty Images

Chelsea began to contain the hosts and turn the tide as the interval approached. They were inches away from taking the lead in spectacular fashion. Moisés Caicedo pulled away to the back post for a Jordan Henderson corner that arrived exactly where the training ground routine required. His thunderous volley flew past Pickford but smacked the crossbar, leaving it shaking for several seconds.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Neto forced a decent save from the Everton keeper from distance in first-half stoppage time and beat him from much closer range 44 seconds after the restart. As in the draw at Hull last weekend, Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Pickford were found wanting defensively. Rogers was somewhat inevitably involved when releasing Jorrel Hato, Alonso’s one enforced change from the 5-1 defeat of Bournemouth, away from Maitland-Niles down the Chelsea left. Hato’s cross took a fortunate touch off James Tarkowski en route to Neto, whose shot beat Pickford’s weak attempt to save low to his left.

Goalkeeping worries took on a far more serious complexion when Branthwaite collided with Martínez as they challenged for a Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall free-kick. The Chelsea keeper required lengthy treatment before being carried away with his neck in a brace and to the uncomfortable sound of Evertonian boos. Thankfully he gave a thumbs up to Branthwaite when the concerned Everton defender waited to wish him well.

Martínez’s replacement, Mike Penders on his Premier League debut, was not seriously tested as the Everton threat petered out and Chelsea maintained control of the second half. Victory was sealed in the final minute of normal time when Henderson’s free-kick struck the head of Barry, rebounded off the Everton substitute Tyrique George and Vitalii Mykolenko, before dropping to Neto. The Chelsea winger rolled a confident finish past Pickford’s despairing dive into the bottom corner.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: West Ham go second; Norwich beaten again
Sports.content:
West Ham ended Swansea’s four-match winning streak with a 1-0 away victory that reduced the gap at the top of the Championship to a single point.

Divine Mukasa’s calm first-half finish proved the difference, with the result putting the Hammers second, within a point of Swansea, who lost at home for the first time since April. Swansea had made their best start since 1923 by winning seven and drawing two of their opening 10 games.

Kim Hellberg defended his decision to rest Will Lankshear against Cardiff after the division’s top scorer came off the bench to rescue a point for Middlesbrough. Lankshear, who took his tally to 10 for the season in all competitions midweek, was rested him for the visit of the Bluebirds.

View image in fullscreen Will Lankshear’s goal saved a point for Middlesbrough. Photograph: Richard Sellers/PA

That selection backfired as Cardiff stunned Boro with two first-half goals from Jack Moylan and Ollie Tanner. Lankshear was then introduced at half-time and inspired a fightback, levelling for Boro with his 11th goal of the campaign after Tommy Conway had halved the deficit.

“You need to manage your players in this league and look into numbers,” said Hellberg. “We have a lot of players that have no pre-season. Will is one of those who came late and has been doing a lot of good things. He’s been absolutely brilliant and sometimes you need to also protect him.”

Liam Millar scored twice as Birmingham beat QPR 3-0 at St Andrew’s. Millar swung the game Birmingham’s way in the 27th minute and then doubled their advantage just after the break. On both occasions he was assisted by Tomoki Iwata while Demarai Gray added the gloss in the first minute of stoppage time by hammering a pull-back by fellow substitute Luis Vázquez into the top corner.

Quick Guide League One roundup: Bradford go top; Plymouth lose Show Bradford moved top of League One with their first home win under Michael Duff, as Plymouth slipped up against Huddersfield. The Bantams, who appointed Duff as manager earlier this month following the departure of Graham Alexander, claimed a 2-0 home win over Stevenage thanks to goals inside the last 11 minutes from Antoni Sarcevic and substitute Will Swan. That proved enough to put them a point clear at the top, with previous front-runners Plymouth going down 2-0 at home to Huddersfield and dropping to fourth in the process. The Terriers climbed above their opponents into third after strikes from Derensili Sanches Fernandez and Bojan Radulovic. Stockport climbed to second, edging out Bromley 1-0 with Kyle Wootton on target, while Robbie Savage’s first home league game in charge of Peterborough ended in a 2-2 draw with Burton. It looked as if Gbemi Arubi’s 89th-minute wonderstrike had earned Albion their first win in three, but Matt Garbett responded with a 96th minute leveller to snatch his side a point. Savage started his time at London Road with a 3-1 win at Leicester last Saturday. Aaron Collins scored the winner as MK Dons beat Luton 2-1 to claim a first league victory of the season. Alex Gilbey fired the Dons ahead with a fine strike before Jordan Clark equalised for the visitors. But Collins’s penalty won the match to condemn Luton to a third defeat in their past four games. Under-pressure Leicester manager Russell Martin celebrated a badly needed win, seeing off visiting Doncaster 2-1 – with Warren O’Hara’s 84th-minute own-goal causing some late tension. Cambridge kept pace with the promotion hopefuls after Shayne Lavery grabbed the winner in added time to leave Barnsley with a 2-1 win, while Sheffield Wednesday eased to a 5-0 win over AFC Wimbledon – Davis Keillor-Dunn with a double. Bottom club Wigan registered a first league win since 2 September, Scott Hogan with the only goal against Reading. Notts County lost 2-0 at Wycombe and Leyton Orient beat Blackpool 2-0. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Luke Graham scored his first goal for Stoke as they won 1-0 at Pride Park to pile more pressure on struggling Derby. The Scotland defender headed in a free-kick early in the second half and that was enough to settle a scrappy contest. Derby, who are missing a number of key players, battled away and nearly snatched a point when David Ozoh’s shot was superbly saved by goalkeeper Viktor Johansson.

West Brom completed a stunning comeback after conceding two early goals as they beat Blackburn 3-2. Andri Gudjohnsen had Rovers two up before the break, before Barney Stewart pulled a goal back for Albion. Isaac Price’s penalty levelled it up before substitute Felix Horn Myhre netted a dramatic winner for the home side a minute from time.

James Bree, Lewis Dobbin and Leo Scienza all squandered chances as Southampton dropped points at home for the first time this season with a 0-0 draw against Bolton. The trio all wasted tap-ins, while Saints were also left bereft by a penalty not being given for a Rúben Rodrigues handball.

View image in fullscreen Luca Kjerrumgaard enjoys his crucial opener for Watford against Charlton. Photograph: Ben Peters/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Watford lifted the pressure on Alessio Dionisi and quelled their supporters’ rebellion against the owner, Gino Pozzo, with a deserved 2-0 win against a sluggish Charlton. After shipping nine goals in defeats by Burnley and Cardiff, Watford had slumped into the bottom three and the fans had turned their anger on Pozzo. But goals from Luca Kjerrumgaard and the substitute Jordan Zemura extended Charlton’s worrying run to eight games without a win as they were booed off at Vicarage Road.

Dionisi said later his team was “not yet strong enough for the Championship but it’s possible to improve. I’ve been a coach for 14 years and I know when my team stays near my idea. This result is important and tonight I will drink a glass of red wine.”

Portsmouth piled on the misery for struggling Norwich as they made it back-to-back Championships victories with a 1-0 win at Carrow Road. Pompey followed up their midweek victory against Sheffield United with a hard-fought success in East Anglia, with a 51st-minute penalty from striker Marezi settling the issue.

It was a sixth successive league defeat for the hosts and there were calls for sporting director Ben Knapper to go from frustrated supporters at the final whistle.

Norwich’s head coach, Philippe Clement, had no complaints with his side’s effort – but felt they sometimes failed to see the bigger picture on the pitch.

“I am very disappointed, very frustrated”, he said. “I saw a lot of passion out there, a lot of effort, but not enough overview. We had some good possession but at important moments we would make the wrong pass, or try a shot from 30 yards. It’s about getting the balance right between their hearts and their brains. I understand the frustration of our fans with our results and all I can say is that I will work even harder than I did last season to turn it around.”

View image in fullscreen Portsmouth’s Marezi celebrates on another bleak day for Norwich. Photograph: Stephen Pond/Getty Images

Jake Cooper’s scrambled equaliser rescued a point for Millwall as they came from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Lincoln. The visitors looked on course to put Wednesday’s 6-0 home thrashing against West Ham behind them in style when goals from Andrei Coubiș and Rob Street put them in a strong position after 33 minutes at the Den. But Millwall were able to prevent back-to-back home defeats with a much-improved second-half performance, and the visitors were hanging on for a share of the spoils after having Deji Elerewe sent off soon after Cooper’s leveller. Kyrell Lisbie had scored Millwall’s first.

Quick Guide League Two roundup: Salford make it five in a row Show League Two pacesetters Salford made it five wins in a row in the fourth tier as Macaulay Langstaff scored twice in a 2-1 success over bottom side Crawley. Barnet and Crewe remain close by just a point further back. Barnet came from behind to beat Tranmere 2-1, Kabongo Tshimanga scoring both, and Crewe defeated Rochdale 3-2. York were held to a 1-1 draw at Newport after going down to 10 men but Shrewsbury held on 1-0 against Bristol Rovers despite two red cards in the last 10 minutes. Ian Holloway’s Swindon are now eight games without a win in all competitions after a 1-1 draw with Walsall, Oldham eased to a 4-1 result against Cheltenham and Port Vale edged Chesterfield 1-0. Ten-man Grimsby went down 2-0 to Northampton, Accrington took a 3-1 win over Gillingham, strugglers Rotherham lost 2-0 at Fleetwood and there was a goalless draw between Colchester and Exeter. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Oliver Arblaster’s early strike and a strong defensive display saw Sheffield United take all three points from a 1-0 victory over Bristol City at Ashton Gate. The visitors took a fifth-minute lead when a headed clearance fell to Arblaster, who connected with a sweet right-footed volley from just outside the box which gave City goalkeeper Sam Tickle no chance. It proved enough to settle a contest high on endeavour but low on entertainment from which the Blades emerged worthy winners.

Wrexham eased the pressure on Phil Parkinson with a 4-1 win over rock-bottom Preston. Joe Worrall scored his first goal in more than two years and, after Alfie Devine briefly brought Preston level, the former Lilywhites midfielder Ben Whiteman struck next to score his first goal in Wrexham colours. Sam Smith gave the hosts breathing space just before the hour and Kieffer Moore killed it off moments later.

In a week that had seen former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard linked with the manager’s job, Wrexham’s third league win of the season was a vital one as they moved up to 14th. But Preston remain stuck on four points from 11 games, with Graham Alexander having lost his first three games in charge.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca’s eerie prediction comes true as Man City boss makes Premier League history
Sports.content:
Phil Foden helped Enzo Maresca create Premier League history after the Manchester City boss correctly backed him to break his goal drought.

Foden made an instant impact on his return to action following a three-match suspension by scoring his first competitive goal since last December in Saturday's 3-2 win over Ipswich.

4 Phil Foden ended his barren spell in front of goal with City's opener against Ipswich Credit: Getty

The 26-year-old opened the scoring for the Citizens from close range in the 19th minute following great work by Jeremy Doku.

It was a welcome strike for Foden, who has struggled to reach the levels he set in the 2023/24 season when he was crowned PFA Player of the Year after scoring 19 top-flight goals - 27 in all competitions.

While many wouldn't have tipped Foden to get on the score sheet against the Tractor Boys, Maresca was in no doubt that his player would end his barren spell.

Speaking in his pre-match press conference on Friday, the Italian boldly predicted that Foden’s quality in front of goals would soon shine through.

What did Maresca say about Foden?

“He will score tomorrow!,” Maresca boldly predicted.

“We just try to work with him day by day.

“The international break and since the red card against United has been quite long.

“But he has been training well, he’s doing well since we made a very positive start, very good.

“We need to decide if he starts tomorrow or not and if he does, no doubt he will give us something.”

Foden’s goal would have delighted Maresca as his side continued their 100 per cent start to the season.

4 Maresca's side bounced back following their 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday night

What Premier League record has Maresca created?

The victory gave Maresca a little taste of history by becoming the first manager in Premier League to win his first seven matches in charge of a club.

Erling Haaland scored twice to take his tally to eight goals in seven league games.

But there was concern for Maresca after the Norwegian was seen limping down the tunnel after the final whistle after taking a knock to his foot.

Haaland was expected to be rested for Tuesday’s Champions League clash with AEK Athens. with Maresca to now be hoping the striker is available for next weekend’s trip to Aston Villa.

But the injury concerns do not stop there for the Manchester City boss with a further four players picking up knocks.

Antoine Semenyo and Iliman Ndiaye were both seen limping after the match, while Mateo Kovacic and Matheus Nunes went off with knocks.

4 Erlign Haaland appeared in discomfort as he made his way down the tunnel at full time Credit: AFP

What did Foden say after ending his goal drought?

With his goal drought now over, Foden has declared his strike against Ipswich will be the catalyst for more in the ner future.

He told BBC Radio Manchester: "I set such high standards of myself to always try and score goals, assist, and because I hadn't scored for a long time I've just been trying to practice as much as I can in training and hopefully it paid off.

"Today it finally did. I'm really happy. The first one is always the hardest to score."

Foden also stated: "It's been such a hard time.

"It's been over a month I couldn't play [due to suspension and international break], so it's been quite annoying. I've had to be patient, train on my own sometimes, it's not been easy.

"But today, to get out there and score and get three points, it's what I've been thinking about for a long time."

4 Foden will now be looking to reach double digits for goals for a seventh successive season Credit: Getty

Foden was also pressed for his opinion regarding the ongoing guilty verdict shrouding the club.

To which he said: "We just try to not listen to anything.

"The noise going around, we try to just stick to our football, take it game by game, and I think you can see that it's not affecting us one bit.

"We're still 100 per cent focussed on winning football games, and I think that's how it has to be.

"The main focus is doing our job, and that's all we can do."

Sports.title: Erling Haaland one of FIVE Man City injury fears as Enzo Maresca issues update
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland one of FIVE Man City injury fears as Enzo Maresca issues update

Manchester City picked up five injury concerns during their dramatic 3-2 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday.

The Citizens maintained their 100 per cent Premier League record with a hard-fought victory at the Etihad to make it seven wins from seven.

1 Haaland was one of five players to pick up an injury for City in their home win over Ipswich Credit: AFP

However, Erling Haaland, who scored two and had a hat-trick goal ruled out for offside, has given them a cause of concern.

At the full-time whistle, the Norwegian striker was first down the tunnel and appeared to be in discomfort.

Antoine Semenyo also looked uncomfortable at the end and clutched his leg and his departed, with Iliman Ndiaye also struggling.

City lost Mateo Kovacic and Matheus Nunes to injuries earlier in the second half, with the quintet of injuries overshadowing their victory.

"We'll see," Enzo Maresca said of his players afterwards. "Erling is inside, Antoine is inside. We'll see. We need to wait."

Seven in seven for City, but only just

A 3-0 win at Liverpool last weekend cemented City's status as one of the candidates for this season's Premier League title.

It was their first match since it was announced that an independent commission found them guilty on all charges of financial breaches.

They were smashed 4-2 by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League earlier this week, but bounced back against Ipswich.

Phil Foden drove into the area and fired in the opening goal for the hosts on 19 minutes.

Ipswich equalised moments later via Daizen Maeda, but Haaland was there to head in second for City before the break.

He then slotted in on the break midway through the second half and looked to have bagged a treble to make it 4-1.

But Enzo Fernandez, who provided the assist for the goal, was in an offside position beforehand.

City were given a late scare when Zian Flemming scored a penalty in the 90th minute to offer Ipswich hope of a huge late draw.

However, even with 12 minutes of added time, they couldn't grab a third and earn a point.

Still on the Premier League summit, City have a six-point gap over reigning champions Arsenal, who face Nottingham Forest on Sunday.

However, the outcome of their cases regarding numerous financial rule breaches is expected in early 2027 and, if their appeal fails, they could face a heavy points deduction.

Sports.title: Richarlison takes aim at Roberto De Zerbi on social media in fresh swipe at Tottenham boss
Sports.content:
Richarlison takes aim at Roberto De Zerbi on social media in fresh swipe at Tottenham boss

Richarlison has risked further tension with Roberto De Zerbi after taking aim at the Tottenham boss on social media.

The 29-year-old has been frozen out at Spurs having been omitted from the De Zerbi's Premier League squad.



3 Richarlison, who has been on Tottenham's books since 2022, is in the final year of his contract Credit: AFP

The decision came after the Brazilian started in the north London outfit's opening game of the top-flight campaign - a 3-0 defeat away at Brentford.

A move back to Everton then fell through in the closing stages of the summer transfer window.

Richarlison has already taken to social media to express his pain over his continued exile.



And he has now taken to his Instagram to respond to comments made by Everton icon Duncan Ferguson - who coached him at Goodison Park.

What did Duncan Ferguson say about Richarlison?

Speaking on the Overlap Daily, the Scotsman stressed the forward doesn't deserve the treatment he has been subject to.



He remarked: "I don’t know what the manager [De Zerbi] at Tottenham’s done, I don’t know if they’ve had a massive fall-out, and knowing Richy they probably have.

"But you’ve got to put your arm around him and say, ‘Come on, Richy,’ and get him back in.



"You don’t leave a player like that out (of the squad) unless there’s been a real murder - he’s chinned him, or there’s been a proper scrap on the training ground.

"Richarlison’s a good player, and Tottenham are not that great, are they?

"It’s all hands-on deck. You need all your assets out there. The manager knows what he’s doing, he’s on the ground, but Richarlison’s a great player and I enjoyed working with him.”

3 Richarlison agreed with Ferguson's view that he has been unfairly treated by De Zerbi Credit: Instagram



How did Richarlison hit out at De Zerbi?

A shortened segment of Ferguson's words were posted on X, with Richarlison sharing the snippet on his Instagram story.

Issuing a brief six-word statement, he agreed that he has been unfairly treated by De Zerbi.

He simply said: "Thanks Duncan Ferguson, you are right."

What's next for Richarlison?

With Spurs already dumped out of the Carabao Cup and not competing in Europe, the earliest Richarlison could feature for the club would be in the FA Cup in January.

But with his contract to expire at the end of the season, he may have already played his last game for Spurs.



After being denied a move to Everton, a transfer to return to his homeland to join Vasco de Gama then failed to come to fruition.

3 Richarlison finished as Spurs' top scorer last season with 12 goals, but was deemed as surplus to requirements by De Zerbi Credit: Getty

The ex-Watford man failed to agree terms with the Brazilian outfit, who had agreed a deal in principle to sign him.

And in an attempt to force through a move away from Spurs, Richarlison approached FIFA last month in an attempt to terminate his contract.



It now remains to be seen whether he will secure a switch away from Tottenham when the window reopens in the New Year.

Sports.title: Liverpool suffer cruel double injury blow in cagey Brentford clash
Sports.content:
Liverpool had to substitute two players with injuries during their 2-1 win at Brentford.

Dominik Szoboszlai missed the 3-0 Premier League defeat to Manchester City on Sunday afternoon due to a hamstring problem.



2 Szoboszlai appears to have had a recurrence of his hamstring injury against Brentford and was substituted Credit: AFP

Szoboszlai was also absent from their midweek 6-3 win over LASK in the Champions League.

He was named in the starting XI at Brentford on Saturday, but unable to see out the first half for Liverpool.

The Hungarian international went down off the ball and appeared to be affected by his hamstring once again.



Szoboszlai looked visibly upset as he walked straight down the tunnel at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Liverpool were awarded a penalty moments later but, after a quick VAR review, it was overturned as replays showed Dango Ouattara winning the ball rather than fouling Alexis Mac Allister.



Brentford then scored the opener on 44 minutes as Keane Lewis-Potter headed in from an excellent Igor Thiago cross.

However, they went down to ten men moments before the break as Yehor Yarmoliuk was sent off for violent conduct on Jeremy Jacquet.



"After review, the Brentford No.6 commits a headbutting action. The final decision is a red card," referee John Brooks said.

To capitalise one their one-man advantage, Liverpool brought on Jeremie Frimpong for Ronald Araujo at the start of the second half.

But he was replaced by Rio Ngumoha only six minutes later as he also picked up an injury.

2 Szoboszlai returned to the Liverpool starting XI after missing their last two fixtures, but could be sidelined yet again Credit: AFP



Despite their double injury blow, Liverpool managed to find their way back into the match with an hour played.

Victor Munoz found the back of the net with a composed finish in what is his second Premier League goal.

They then went ahead in west London through Alexander Isak as he smashed the ball into the bottom corner from inside the area.

Brentford went down to nine men in stoppage time when Vitaly Janelt was shown a second yellow card.



The Bees' unbeaten run in the league has now come to an end.

Liverpool have overtaken them in the table and now sit fifth.

Sports.title: Duncan Ferguson set to land new job in league’s biggest ever managerial appointment
Sports.content:
Duncan Ferguson set to land new job in league’s biggest ever managerial appointment

Ex-Everton striker Duncan Ferguson is reportedly set to become the new manager of Irish League club Glentoran.

The 54-year-old is expected to take the reins at the BetMcLean Oval in what is being described as the league’s biggest-ever managerial appointment.

3 Duncan Ferguson is set to make his return to the dugout after two years away Credit: Getty

The former Everton, Rangers and Scotland striker has been away from management for two years following his spell with Inverness Caledonian Thistle.

Ferguson has previously managed Forest Green Rovers and had a brief role as interim manager at Everton after working on the coaching staff under Carlo Ancelotti.

According to the Belfast Telegraph, which claims 'Big Dunc' has landed the Glentoran job, the Scot was the leading candidate amid a thorough recruitment process to fill the void left by former boss Declan Devine.

Glentoran opted not to officially advertise the managerial vacancy following Devine’s exit with Jim Magilton and Ian Baraclough both reportedly in the frame.

Despite that, candidates got wind of the vacancy with the club receiving a host of applications from around the world.

"There has been so much interest in the job and we did not advertise this position at all. After Deccy (Devine) left and word got out from there we were inundated with applications and agents calling us and ex-players calling us," club owner Ali Pour explained.

"Very quickly we had lots of CVs sent to us and while some were okay many were from amazing highly qualified managers."

Former Celtic star Paddy McCourt has filled in as the NIFL Premiership club’s interim manager since Devine’s sacking in September.

McCourt has made a huge impact having led Glentoran to a four-game unbeaten run prior to the midweek cup defeat against Cliftonville.

What has Ferguson done since his last job?

The Everton legend recently worked as an ITV pundit at this summer’s World Cup, casting an expert eye over Scotland’s fortunes.

3 Ferguson worked alongside Carlo Ancelotti during their time together at Everton Credit: Getty

He has also featured in episodes of The Overlap fronted by Gary Neville.

Quizzed about the opportunity of a return to the dugout, Ferguson said: “I want to get back into management.

“I’ve made a couple of crazy decisions in my career in management, but that’s because I was desperate to get in.

“When you’re working every minute of the day as a coach, and you work for Everton and you’re in there 24/7, when you leave and you’re out to football for a week or a month – you think it’s a year because you’ve been working every day.

“It feels like a month’s a year and I went in too quickly and I took the wrong job, especially the first one. I took the wrong job.

“I should never have taken it. I didn’t even know where they were in the league. And then my last job, Inverness went into administration.

3 Ferguson will be tasked with ended the club's 17-year title drought Credit: Getty

“So how’s your luck? I think I’ve got a lot to offer. I look back and I think I should give myself a good shake. Hopefully an opportunity will come along soon because I know I’ve got so much to offer.”

Sports.title: Why Man City fans are waving inflatable bananas amid club chaos
Sports.content:
Manchester City fans are responding to their critics in a unique way - with inflatable bananas!

City kept up their tradition of displaying blow-up yellow fruit before kick-off in Saturday's home clash with Ipswich, a week after flooding the Anfield away end with them in their 3-0 win over Liverpool.

3 Man City have won all their Premier League games this season and are preparing to play PSG in the Champions League mid-week Credit: Getty

The City supporters are adopting a tradition that calls back to the 1980s to try and find a positive message amid the chaos at the club.

Enzo Maresca's men were playing in their first Premier League match since it was officially ruled that the club had breached financial rules between 2009 and 2018 and were charged on 115 offences.

The Etihad hierarchy have launched an appeal against the verdict and insist they have 'irrefutable evidence' to support their position.

The atmosphere on Merseyside was hostile, with City players heavily booed every time they touched the ball during the opening minutes.

The City fans applauded their players and waved giant blow-up bananas, reviving a iconic fan culture tradition from decades past.

The idea was suggested by supporters' group 1894, and the gesture was designed to bring humor back to the matchday experience amid the club's ongoing disputes with football authorities.

It was during a time in English football when clubs were banned from European competition.

The fan group posted on X last week following the charges being annnounced, and said: "The message – this fan base has always been on a rollercoaster."

The trend supposedly originated in 1987, when Man City supporter Frank Newton brought a five-foot blow-up banana to Maine Road for a match against Plymouth Argyle.

Newton referred to former Man City striker Imre Varadi as 'Imre Banana', then more people adopted the trend and brought various versions throughout the year.

3 Following Ryan Gravenberch's red card, City dominated and scored three goals against the Reds Credit: Getty

Hostility outside and inside

City were found guilty of inflating their revenues by £900million, using disguised funding schemes.

Liverpool were beaten into second place during the 2013/14 season and the fans voiced their anger at City during Sunday's fixture.

Outside the stadium, there was merchandise being sold which displayed the words 'guilty' and 'cheats' on flags and banners.

Liverpool supporters lined the streets prior to the 4:30pm kick-off to greet the team buses.

Songs were sung about Manchester City 'going down, going down, going down' and that the club were 'cheating b*******'.

3 Manchester City fans waved hundreds of inflatable bananas in the air, while Liverpool fans also made their voices heard Credit: Getty

Additionally, Merseyside Police flew drones and had an increased presence of officers around the ground to maintain order.

Liverpool’s team bus arrived but City opted for a quieter, alternative route to the stadium to avoid the crowds.

However, inside the stadium, the players were met with a chorus of boos as they came onto the pitch.

Meanwhile, the Reds displayed a banner in Anfield which read 'a generation of supporters cheated'.

More bananas to come?

City fans will now likely adopt their banana celebrations for the rest of the season.

City take on Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday, live on talkSPORT, in their first home game since the new broke.

They then host Ipswich in the top-flight on Saturday before welcoming AEK Athens to the Etihad in Europe again next week.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso gives update on Emi Martinez after Chelsea goalkeeper knocked unconscious and rushed to hospital
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso gives update on Emi Martinez after Chelsea goalkeeper knocked unconscious and rushed to hospital

Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is conscious in hospital after a sickening collision during the 2-0 win at Everton.

The Argentina star was knocked out cold after attempting to punch a Toffees free-kick in the second-half.



4 Martinez came off worse in a sickening collision with Branthwaite Credit: AFP

4 There was immediate concern for the goalkeeper as players frantically motioned for medical assistance Credit: AFP

4 The goalkeeper had regained consciousness by the time he was carried off Credit: Getty

Speaking to talkSPORT after, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso confirmed that Martinez regained consciousness before leaving the Hill Dickinson Stadium.



He is undergoing precautionary tests after being taken to hospital.

What happened to Martinez?

Martinez collided with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite before lying motionless on the turf.

Medical staff from both teams rushed onto the pitch as St John's Ambulance paramedics joined the response.



Branthwaite was quickly deemed OK to continue after concussion protocol but Martinez was clearly in a bad way.

The match was delayed for more than ten minutes before a heavily-strapped Martinez was stretchered off.



He could be seen moving his arms and gesturing to teammates as he was taken off the pitch.

Belgian goalkeeper Mike Penders was brought on by Chelsea to replace Martinez, who was sent straight to hospital, in what was his Premier League debut.

Chelsea end clean sheet wait at Everton

Pedro Neto was the star of the show as he scored both goals to win it for Chelsea.

He opened the scoring with less than a minute played in the second half with a well-taken finish from a Jorrel Hato cross.



4 A double from Neto ensured Chelsea left Everton with all three points Credit: Getty

Martinez went down with his injury shortly after the hour mark and the break in play meant there would be plenty of added minutes at the end of the half.

Neto then bagged his second of the day shortly before stoppage time began as he coolly slotted into the bottom corner.

"A shame for Emi, but we wish him all the best. This win is for him," Neto told TNT Sports at full-time.



The result has ended Everton's unbeaten run in the Premier League, and Chelsea's wait for a clean sheet.

A 2-0 win at home against Brentford in January was the most recent time that the Blues managed to not concede a goal in the top flight.

Chelsea have also won a Premier League away match while keeping a clean sheet for the first time since a 2-0 win over Burnely last November.

Sports.title: Everton player refuses to take the knee before Chelsea clash
Sports.content:
Everton player refuses to take the knee before Chelsea clash

Everton defender Ainsley Maitland-Niles refused to take the knee prior to the Premier League clash with Chelsea.

The Toffees star abstained from the pre-match gesture which is part of the Premier League’s ‘No Room For Racism' initiative.

4 Ainsley Maitland-Niles refused to take the knee before kick off on Saturday Credit: TNT Sport

4 Other players from both sides did participate in taking the knee Credit: Getty

Taking the knee reverted from a weekly ritual between 2020 and 2022 to a targeted gesture reserved for specific fixtures.

It is unclear as to why Maitland-Niles refused to take the knee, although some stars have publicly argued that the move has lost its impact.

Before it became a part-time initiative, former Brentford captain Ivan Toney explained why the Bees stopped participating.

He said: "We are kind of being used as puppets, in my eyes; take the knee and the people at the top can rest for a while now, which is pretty silly and pretty pointless. Nothing is changing."

Players will perform the gesture for the next two gameweeks as part of the Premier League's commitment to tackling discrimination in football.

In 2022, the Premier League opted to stop taking the knee before every match after dialogue with players.

A decision was then taken to introduce the gesture on specific match rounds to promote the initiative.

Lionesses refusal to kneel

During the 2025 Women’s Euros, the Lionesses chose not to take the knee before their semi-final clash with Italy following online racist abuse directed at defender Jess Carter.

It was followed by teammate Lucy Bronze claiming the anti-racism message is not 'as strong as it used to be'.

Carter subsequently stepped back from social media platforms for the rest of the campaign.

4 Jess Carter was subjected to abhorrent online abuse during Euro 2025 Credit: Getty

4 The Lionesses stood in solidarity with teammate Carter before their semi-final win over Italy Credit: Getty

Bronze said: “It was driven by the group… obviously certain individuals more than others.

“I think it was just the fact that we feel as a collective, is the message as strong as it used to be? Is the message really hitting hard?

“Because to us it feels like it's not if these things are still happening to our players in the biggest tournaments of their lives.

“It's about putting another statement out there to say, it's something that still is a problem, it's something that still needs to be put right.

“More needs to be done in football, more needs to be done in society. What that is right now as an individual, I don't exactly know.”

The decision received backing from anti-discrimination group Kick It Out, which joined the players in calling for social media companies and authorities to take stronger, more concrete action rather than relying on symbolic gestures.
