Sports.title: Alvaro Arbeloa secures first Premier League win as Fulham boss and saves job for now: Fulham 1-0 Hull City
Sports.content:
Fulham finally got over the line to win their first match under Alvaro Arbeloa, earning precious breathing space for their under-pressure boss.

Arbeloa was facing serious questions over whether he was cut out for the role after six Premier League games without a win.

Yet this was a confident performance that eased the pressure, with Fulham dominating Hull, who had lost just once before travelling to Craven Cottage.

In fact, the performance was best encapsulated by Hull manager Sergej Jokanovic: ‘It was men v boys out there. They ate us alive.'

Jokanovic was right. This was a transformative Fulham performance, a far cry from the team that has lacked balance and looked fragile.

Fulham did not give Hull a sniff. They dominated possession, enjoying 76 per cent of the ball.

Throughout the season, they have been caught in transition and overcommitted but that evaporated - limiting Hull to eight touches in their penalty area and denying them a shot on target or an attempt inside the box.

That said, there is a caveat: Hull did not offer much. Yes, Fulham were brilliant and outclassed their opponents but it is worth being cautious about hailing their defensive display because Hull were so sloppy.

There is reason to be concerned in attack. Although Fulham were free-flowing and registered 18 shots, they lacked a clinical edge and missed four big chances.

Gonzalo Garcia, in particular, should have scored when Alex Iwobi put a delicious ball on a plate for him in the 74th minute but his header struck the crossbar from eight yards.

'I’ve seen this movie before,' Arbeloa replied when asked what he was thinking as Fulham squandered their chances. 'I never felt like we were in danger, but in football you never know. One moment and a goal can be scored.

'It was so important to see the players' commitment. For the players on the bench, not on the bench, they are so important for us, working for the group. We need to keep working, it's going to be a long season.

'I am happy because I think we deserved victories in games before, we lost some games where I didn't think the team was better than us. Today, was a perfect day where we dominated. We were almost perfect, I can't believe the game finished 1-0.'

Alex Iwobi scored a scruffy goal in the 33rd minute to alleviate the pressure on Alvaro Arbeloa

On the whole, this was a drastic improvement from Arbeloa’s side and seems to have saved his job for now. He must now find a way to knit together the defensive and attacking performances.

Fulham played entertaining football with a strong defensive platform but if they do not take their chances, games like last weekend’s will continue to haunt them. Against Ipswich, they conceded twice in four minutes, throwing away three points having squandered three big chances.

After all, the matchwinner was comical. Brooke Norton-Cuffy’s lazy clearance fell to Oscar Bobb before eventually landing with Sander Berge, who spotted Alex Iwobi on the edge of the box and played the ball into his path.

Iwobi’s first-time effort rifled into the bottom corner and underneath goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis. Meanwhile, they failed to take the chances they are expected to put away.

That winner, though, was scored with over an hour remaining. Fulham had previously cracked in winning positions, dropping eight points. But this demonstrated they do have the required mentality.

With Arbeloa’s job on the line, this was an encouraging response.

Sports.title: Liverpool's victory at nine-man Brentford leaves more questions than answers as Florian Wirtz struggles again and Bradley Barcola fails to hit Champions League heights, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
It was not a classic head butt that put Jeremy Jacquet down deep into time added on at the end of the first half. In other cultures, in other eras, it might have been interpreted as a nod of recognition from Yehor Yarmoliuk. But it was foolish and it was enough to seal his fate and cost his team. VAR intervened, Yarmoliuk was sent off and the game was changed.

Until then, Liverpool had struggled to assert themselves, even with a front line that cost more than £400m. Bradley Barcola had missed a gilt-edged chance, Florian Wirtz had spent another half fretting at the margins and Andoni Iraola’s team were soon to suffer two injury blows when both Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong were forced off.

But Brentford going down to 10 men wiped all Liverpool’s misfortunes away. By the time the dismissal of Vitaly Janelt reduced the home team to nine men in second half stoppage time, Liverpool were 2-1 up and heading towards fifth place in the table.

The statistics said that Wirtz had created nine chances, including the assist for Liverpool’s equaliser, more than any player in the Premier League this season. That flattered his overall performance but it was something to build on. There was time for one more glaring miss from Barcola but by then it didn’t matter.

It was hardly an emphatic victory. The questions about Wirtz are still getting louder. Barcola may have scored a hat-trick in the Champions League in midweek but he looks desperately short of confidence in the more testing conditions of the Premier League.

Liverpool will have been buoyed by the fact it was Alexander Isak who scored the winner after Victor Munoz had dragged them back into the game with a fine equaliser but even though Liverpool have only lost once in their opening seven league games, they are still searching for something.

Alexander Isak scored the winner on his return as Liverpool came from behind to beat Brentford

Victor Munoz had equalised; Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola provided the assists

‘He is disappointed,’ Brentford manager Keith Andrews said of Yarmoliuk and his indiscretion after the game. ‘He is an amazing young man. He will learn from this. We need to look at ourselves. They were cute and clever but he needs to do better.’

Andrews is as impressive a communicator as there is in the Premier League and his reaction fitted that pattern.

The game had got off to a slow start, notable only for Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister blazing shots over the bar. But it suddenly came to life midway through the first half when a neat interchange between Michael Kayode and Dango Ouattara ended with Ouattara’s goal-bound shot being deflected wide by Jacquet.

A minute later, Liverpool should have scored. Brentford played themselves into trouble on the half-way line and Barcola, who cost £123m when he arrived from PSG in the summer, stole the ball away from Yarmoliuk and raced clear. Barcola lifted the ball over Caoimhin Kelleher but pulled it wide of the right-hand post. ‘What a waste of money,’ Brentford’s fans sang.

A fine challenge by Jacquet prevented Igor Thiago putting the home side ahead but Liverpool had other issues to deal with, too. Barcola was shown a yellow card for pulling back an opponent and then Szoboszlai had to be substituted with what looked like a recurrence of his hamstring injury.

The Hungary forward was distraught. He hammered his hand into the turf in frustration. Szoboszlai has been Liverpool’s most influential player for some time so his loss was a big blow. He marched straight down the tunnel, his expression set in a stony grimace.

Keane Lewis-Potter had put Brentford ahead not long before half-time with a header

The game changed going into half-time when Yehor Yarmolyuk was sent off for a headbutt

One misfortune followed another. Liverpool won a penalty five minutes before half time when Mac Allister fell under a challenge from Ouattara but VAR intervened and replays showed Ouattara had touched the ball before the Liverpool midfielder tumbled to the floor.

Two minutes later, Brentford took the lead. Igor Thiago curled in an inviting ball from the right and Keane Lewis-Potter ran on to it and leapt to power a brilliant header past the dive of Alisson.

Deep in injury time at the end of the half, though, Brentford indulged in an act of self-sabotage. In the routine jostling that takes place before a corner, Yarmoliuk bumped chests with Jacquet and then moved his head towards the Liverpool centre half. VAR intervened again and Yarmoliuk was shown a red card for violent conduct.

It was a classic ‘soft’ decision. In the press room at half time, I asked Ray Houghton if that would have counted as a head-butt in his day. ‘That would have been a friendly hello,’ he said with a smile. He was right, of course, but in today’s top-flight culture, Yarmoliuk moved his head towards Jacquet and opened himself up to the censure that followed.

More injury woes afflicted Liverpool after the break. Frimpong had come on at half-time but lasted five minutes before he was led off the pitch, limping. Liverpool’s frustrations grew. Jacquet was shown a yellow card for a foul. Mac Allister was booked for dissent.

Mac Allister brought a fine save out of Kelleher before Virgil Van Dijk drove a volley into the ground and watched it bounce just wide. Victor Munoz was involved in an altercation with Kevin Schade that saw Schade booked. The clash spurred Munoz on.

A couple of minutes after it, he escaped down the right and sprinted into the area. He turned inside Lewis-Potter and bent a low left-foot shot around Kelleher and into the Brentford goal to bring Liverpool level.

Liverpool finally looked as if they had the belief to win and eight minutes later they were ahead. Mac Allister lifted a deep cross to the back post, Barcola nodded it down and Isak got in front of his man, took one touch to control it and then rifled the ball past Kelleher. Lewis-Potter was on the line but he could only deflect it into the net.

Barcola hit the bar with delicate chip but when he had a chance to put the game out of reach in the dying minutes, he hesitated, tried to play in Lewis Koumas instead and the chance was gone. It was a good win for Liverpool but it still left more questions than answers.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland gives Man City an injury scare after starring in Ipswich victory and Enzo Maresca makes history as club keep winning in face of guilty verdict, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca is statistically the best coach in Premier League history. Over seven games, anyway. Nobody has ever won their first seven in charge. Not Ancelotti, not Mourinho, not Wenger.

They’ll probably want that accolade wiped from the record books too, given how the conversation around City’s indiscretions is being shaped. Irrespective, it talks to a near-flawless few months to life at the Etihad Stadium for an Italian whose credentials were being written off before formally accepting the job and then again after a meaningless Community Shield defeat by Arsenal with an unfit team.

The public face of the guilty verdicts and the only management employee talking on record about ramifications and the club’s stance, this is a job far more difficult than merely succeeding the best to have ever done it. He’s passing everything with flying colours for City’s hierarchy, both on and off the pitch.

Six points is the gap between the leaders and Arsenal before the champions go to Nottingham Forest on Sunday. More strikingly, it is eight from Chelsea and nine down to Liverpool.

This, you have to say, is as awkward as it gets for Richard Masters and the Premier League board. As the world waits for the next stage of this bitter legal case, an appeal that is likely to bring down the grand old house of English football either which way, City just keep winning. Keep winning games with a load of jeopardy attached to them, nip and tuck, chances at both ends right until the end.

Ironically, they are dispatching the more established clubs with more ease than the upstarts, and Maresca keeps smiling in the face of ire. They are scoring heaps, giving up plenty of opportunities for the opposition with a daring style, and are eminently more watchable than anybody else in this division. To illustrate that, Gary O’Neil feels that Ipswich Town deserved far more from this and will have more than a few agreeing with him.

Erling Haaland netted twice for Manchester City as they beat Ipswich 3-2 on Saturday

The win means Enzo Maresca is the best manager in Premier League history, with no boss ever winning their first seven matches in charge before

Another Erling Haaland brace – four for the campaign – against a promoted team who are posing serious questions in this league and wasted decent chances at 2-1 just after the break, notably when Emersonn headed wide after Gianluigi Donnarumma flapped at a corner.

Haaland seemingly cannot stop – although went straight down the tunnel at full-time with what looks a knee injury having appeared as if he was unwell in the Mancunian cold – and the general merriment in the stands continued from Anfield last week. Maresca, though, seemed to suggest he was fine afterwards.

Some will instead label the merriment as defiance and others will ask what on earth do City supporters have to be defiant over. What is definitely the case is that the past few weeks have provoked a reaction from a fanbase that has been asked to swot up on matters no avid follower of any sport should have to.

And then there were the bananas. Eleven thousand of them hung over seats and many more sold outside. Word at the back end of the week was that chief executive Ferran Soriano had hoped to order in 60,000 to fill the stadium, only for constraints on supply putting paid to that.

Funnily enough, ex-striker Imre Varadi owns a business that trades in the sale of inflatable fruit. While not being the reason for the 1980s craze, Varadi is synonymous with it and City now do their banana business with him. He was invited into a box for the day to see them waved as each goal went in.

None more so than when Haaland thought he’d completed his hat-trick late on, callously volleying into the roof of Christian Walton’s net, only for Enzo Fernandez to have been ruled offside in the build-up, cleared up by VAR.

Marc Guehi has a tough game - and Gary O'Neil felt his Ipswich side deserved more

Former director Txiki Begiristain (left) was in attendance to show support for his old club

Then the game turned heading into stoppage time. Marc Guehi – who had been culpable for Ipswich’s earlier equaliser, when Daizen Maeda wriggled clear from a routine ball in behind – was caught wrong side of Abdul Fatawu. Guehi nicked the winger’s calf as he strode towards goal. Referee Farai Hallam waved away the appeals when the decision seemed clear and needed calling back by VAR again to overturn it.

Zian Flemming hammered the penalty down the middle, Ipswich now within a goal and Hallam – who became exceptionally unpopular in a game against Wolves here last January – then somehow ruling 12 minutes of injury time to incredulity.

Still end to end, still City desperate to find a fourth and not hold what they had. Donnarumma tangled in his own netting while punching away a corner. Sharp intakes of breath, more gasps.

Maresca loves this entertainment but doubtless wants a tad more of the control with which this club had become accustomed. Former director of football Txiki Begiristain, sat next to Hugo Viana as another show of support for the club from the old guard, will not have seen much of this helter-skelter stuff under the previous incumbent.

Begiristain witnessed a positive afternoon for Phil Foden, sweeping in the 19th-minute opener beautifully from Jeremy Doku’s pass in a way we have seen so often down the years. He went off to a standing ovation and with a huge grin for the first time in a long time. Maheda struck back two minutes later before Haaland’s powerful header proved too hot for Walton just after the half hour.

It prompted ‘Dave from Liverpool’ to send a message into the BBC’s live text service to suggest that ‘City are just a midtable team without Haaland,’ which feels indicative of the collective loss of perspective in recent weeks. As it was, the goal was greeted by chants of ‘we are staying up’ before they completed fine renditions of a future spent travelling to Stockport County for league fixtures. That should stir some enthusiasm given the bounty of ale choices behind Edgeley Park’s Cheadle End and the town’s general upturn. It’s a pretty strong away day.

Haaland’s second – 12 for the season – saw him muscle Ouattara out of the way from the industrious Iliman Ndiaye’s pass and appeared to put the game beyond doubt, only for Ipswich to wrestle back in for what became a ridiculously nervous final passage. Say what you like about City but they are certainly not boring.

Sports.title: The fact Man United cannot drop Lisandro Martinez after his outburst just goes to show he was spot on about Sir Jim Ratcliffe's politburo of under-qualified, over-protected advisors, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez will be in the Manchester United squad when they face Leeds on Sunday. And of course he will, because he was right about that shambling wreck of a club. If he was wrong, and United were indeed a functional, intelligent organisation, he wouldn’t be anywhere near the bus for Elland Road. Not after what he said the other night. A proper recruitment system would have meant there was enough defensive cover to drop a dissenting voice in questionable form. But United don’t have that. Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s politburo of under-qualified, over-protected advisors messed up another transfer window, so kicking Martinez into the long grass wasn’t an option. In other words, if Jason Wilcox was better at his job then Martinez would have lost his and here’s a little list to support the point: Cristiano Ronaldo, Jadon Sancho, Marcus Rashford. In the past few years, all of them have spoken out about those above them at United. And with the exception of Rashford, their feet didn’t touch the ground. Straight red. Rashford got put in the freezer for 18 months. Martinez’s comments were slightly different, of course. He didn’t go after his manager, like Ronaldo and Sancho, and he didn’t turn up late and then flash some leg to potential suitors, like Rashford. But he did sing a similar song by tearing strips off the regime in public. That used to be a hard no-no at Old Trafford, irrespective of how much truth was in the pudding. We know that everything Martinez said about Wilcox and the club’s lack of ambition was accurate. We also know that his performance at the microphone was better than anything he has shown on the pitch in quite some time. No one could score points off him for accuracy, only his wisdom in stating the obvious and his reliability as a witness. Michael Carrick says the club have moved on from Lisandro Martinez's comments after the defeat by Atletico Madrid on Tuesday night Sir Jim Ratcliffe brought in Jason Wilcox from Southampton in 2024 Michael Carrick’s position in all of this is quite interesting. Unlike Wilcox, he has to answer questions about rogue speakers, limited options and poor results and the links between them. When the Martinez situation was put to him on Friday, he dealt with it the way he used to play, by taking the least fussy option – he managed upwards by not slapping his bosses and he limited his criticisms of Martinez to saying he made a ‘mistake’. Pinned into a tight space, he found a sensible pass. Carrick couldn’t have done much better in that no-win scenario. But on some level, and in thoughts best kept to himself, he might even wish to thank Martinez. Because who else in-house has pinned United’s difficulties to the lapels of those who are largely responsible for this mess? It won’t count for much in the long run, as it’s always the manager who carries the can. And some of the flak he has drawn in recent weeks is justified, of course. Same goes for the players. But it is inconceivable to think Carrick, a smart man, would have supported the thinking behind a summer window in which United prepared for a return to a European workload by signing three midfielders and a back-up goalkeeper. A window that offered no cover for a left-back in Luke Shaw, who has managed 25-plus Premier League games in four of his 12 seasons at United. A window that left Martinez and Harry Maguire as the first-choice centre-back pairing. A window that marked two years since they last signed a senior defender, the entirety of which has been spent under the watch of Wilcox, the director of directionless football. Those are the decisions that shape seasons and what we are seeing from United is no surprise. We all called it a mile off. And we can all see Carrick’s points of exposure when Leeds are in the opposite corner. Wilcox brought in Carlos Baleba from Brighton to complete United's transfer business this summer - he was the third midfielder they signed, after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans In many ways, they are the last thing he needs right now. They are a club that, for a number of reasons, highlight his shortcomings and those of United’s executive tier. I was at their game against Arsenal and left with three main thoughts – Leeds dominated the champions for an hour, they are brilliantly organised by Daniel Farke and they know the value of a good defender. Leeds didn’t have a spectacular window, but it was key to the building of a backline that is jointly the best in the Premier League so far. Nico Elvedi has been a good signing and Tarik Muharemovic an exceptional one; between them, they cost roughly the same as Youri Tielemans, with the difference being that Farke had a clear idea of how to use them. It’s possible that Carrick will crack that code on Sunday – his team are good for attacking moments, if nothing else. But it is also possible that Elland Road will prove the worst possible place for him to be, because so many of the areas where his side have under-performed are those where Farke has excelled. A solid, physical midfield, a reliable defence, and a collective that operates with a detailed, well-understood plan has been shown so far this season by only one of the two clubs in the fixtures. For Carrick, there is some blame to be swallowed there. But only some. The vast majority goes to higher planes, where the responsibility truly lies for United’s problems. I would doubt Lisandro Martinez’s judgement in designating himself as the man to point it out. But he wasn’t wrong.

Sports.title: Former Man United striker Fraizer Campbell reveals crippling snus addiction during his Premier League playing days that left him 'constantly fatigued'
Sports.content:
Former Man United striker Fraizer Campbell reveals crippling snus addiction during his Premier League playing days that left him 'constantly fatigued'

Former Premier League forward Fraizer Campbell has revealed snus left him 'constantly fatigued' after becoming addicted during his playing career.

Campbell played for Manchester United in the Premier League after coming through the club’s academy, while he also spent time at Tottenham, Hull, Sunderland, Cardiff and Crystal Palace during his career.

The forward told the Sports Agents he was first introduced to snus – a tobacco-based nicotine product that users place between their upper lip and gumline – during his time at Palace, who he represented from 2014-17.

Campbell explained that he was initially introduced to snus by a team-mate and began using it to try to relax after matches.

'I felt relaxed, and it just chilled me out more than anything,' Campbell said.

'It was after a game as well, and after a game is, you know, it's one of them things that it's quite hard to relax after.

Ex-Man United star Fraizer Campbell has revealed he was addicted to snus during his career

'It started off just after games, then training sessions, but that is how it starts and then you have the addiction and you are having them more and more.'

Campbell admitted that he would regularly suffer a 'slump in the afternoon' when he felt exhausted after becoming addicted to snus.

The former forward, now 39, explained that while he initially used snus to relax after matches, he increasingly began using it before training sessions.

'I definitely was addicted, but yeah, obviously, when I had more time on my hands when I retired, I had more time to have the snus,' Campbell said.

'So obviously, in the morning, while I was playing, I might have one in the morning or two in the morning and then for the next couple of hours I'd be out on the training pitch.

'I would never have them on a match day. Because, you know, it chilled me out too much, and I was someone that I'm pretty chill person as it is. If I was more chilled, I'd struggle to get into a jog.

'It got a lot worse after I finished playing football, but I didn't really see the negative side of it while I was playing.'

Campbell added that he is now 'six months clean' after tackling his addiction after feeling 'constantly fatigued'.

Campbell said he first tried snus while at Crystal Palace as he tried to relax after matches, but gradually began using it before training sessions as he became addicted

A study commissioned by the Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) in 2024 found that one in five top-level players were using snus, nicotine pouches or both.

There are concerns that the use of both substances has been linked to a variety of health issues, with the report claiming that users can develop nicotine dependency, 'an increased risk of oesophagus and pancreatic cancer compared to non-smokers', as well as oral health issues and cardiovascular problems.

The PFA earlier this month launched a confidential support pathway to help its members overcome reliance on snus, nicotine pouches and vapes.

'Nicotine use is a growing trend among players right now. We know because we worked with Loughborough University on a world-first study to assess the scale of the issue in professional football,' the PFA said.

'Our research found that while the use of snus and nicotine pouches is high among players, most who use them would prefer to stop.'

Sports.title: Former Man United star Ander Herrera reveals he is now 'playing for free' after choosing to donate weekly wage to his boyhood club - having cashed in on £53m at Old Trafford and PSG
Sports.content:
Ex-Manchester United midfielder Ander Herrera has revealed he is playing for free at his boyhood club Real Zaragoza. The 37-year-old who has two caps for the Spanish national team was, until very recently, living out the final years of his storied career in Argentina with Boca Juniors but has now decided to ply his trade in the Spanish third division with Real Zaragoza, in hopes of bringing the historic club back to the big time. Herrera is reportedly earning £5,500 per week, a far cry from the £150,000 he earned while playing for European giants Paris Saint-Germain. But in an interview with Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand on the former centre-half's YouTube channel, Rio Ferdinand Presents, the Spaniard revealed that every penny of his wage will be going to the club's foundation. The six-time Copa del Rey and one-time Europa League winner said: 'Now in a difficult moment for the club, I think we all, we the fans, we have the responsibility to help the team and the club. And I feel so proud of my career. 'I feel so proud about what I have achieved in terms of football and also in terms of money. So I don't need it. I wanted to play for free. I wanted to help for free. 'At home, my city, where I grew up, and hopefully, as I told you before, helping the club to come back to professional football.' The Spaniard revealed the motivation behind his decision to return to Real Zaragoza in an interview on Rio Ferdinand Presents source: RioFerdinandPresents/YouTube Herrera spent five years with Manchester United winning four major trophies but is now hoping to bring his boyhood club back to the professional game Real Zaragoza, slipped into the third division of Spanish football, officially a semi-professional division, at the end of last season in one of the most shocking declines a big European club has experienced in recent years. Herrera also stressed the importance of his decision: 'I think we also have to give something back to football, you know, and I wanted to do this because I am not only a professional football player, I am also a football fan and I love what I do. 'And one day, probably soon, when I am retired, I want to feel proud of what I have done during my career.' Ferdinand took Herrera's candor as an opportunity to pile more criticism onto Manchester United's rivals, Manchester City, saying: 'In a world where Man City have these charges hanging over their head, it's so good to hear about a gesture like this still in the game of football.' The pair continued to joke about the potential re-attributing of Premier League winners medals following the bombshell Manchester City verdict. Ferdinand began by saying: 'I'm waiting for my medal as well, so you can have one and I can have another one as well.' Herrera gave a classy response saying: 'I don't know if we deserve the trophy, but for sure they don't deserve to win it. 'If the Premier League want to keep being respected all around the world they have to do something.' Herrera could potentially be entitled to a Premier League winners medal as he was a key part of Jose Mourinho's 2017-18 Manchester United side that finished second to City, although they were 19 points off the pace. The one-time Europa League and FA Cup winner with Manchester United did express some sympathy for the Manchester City players during his interview, saying: 'I don't know if you will agree with me but if I was a Man City player I would be angry with my owners, I would be angry with my board, because they have put all that I have done during these years in doubt.'

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho admits Vinicius Jr should have LEFT Real Madrid last summer 'to a country where he is respected' as boss lavishes praise on former Arsenal target
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho admits Vinicius Jr should have LEFT Real Madrid last summer 'to a country where he is respected' as boss lavishes praise on former Arsenal target

Jose Mourinho thinks Vinicius Junior should have left Real Madrid in the summer to go somewhere he is 'respected'.

Arsenal enquired about the Brazilian superstar and reports suggested they were willing to offer him a mammoth £18.5million per season - more than any player at the club.

His contract expires at the end of the season and the club's position is that he must lower his demands if they are to agree an extension. They would still be willing to make him their joint-highest earner alongside Kylian Mbappe.

Vinicius Jr has often been a target of racism in Spain - there have been more than 20 such cases of alleged abuse towards him since he joined from Flamengo in 2018. The situation has reduced him to tears before, but he has insisted on staying in La Liga so that he doesn't 'give the racists what they want'.

His future has come under more scrutiny in recent times as he has had a slow start to the season - one goal and three assists in ten outings - and is now serving a four-match ban for pulling Villarreal star Nathan Saliba's hair.

Mourinho said: 'If I were in his shoes, I probably wouldn't be here. I would have forced a move to a country where he'd be respected, but out of loyalty to Real Madrid and love for the club, he stayed.

Jose Mourinho says he would've left Real Madrid in the summer if he were Vinicius Junior

'I would have forced a move to a country where he'd be respected,' said Mourinho, of the star who has suffered persistent racial abuse in Spain

'He believes things can improve, and he still has that smile. Nothing and no one can take it away from him.

'He's a fantastic guy, and it's easy to get along with him. I spend a few minutes alone with him every day.

'I value him immensely because he always manages to live and survive with a smile.'

Vinicius has been a phenomenon at Real Madrid, scoring 129 times in 386 games from the wing.

But the balance of power shifted to Mbappe when he joined from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024 and talk of his future has increased.

There is a chance that, if Madrid go a third season in a row without significant silverware, they choose to rebuild and go in a different direction.

Moving away from the heavy 'superstar' model has worked for PSG and rewarded them with two Champions League titles in a row.

Vinicius had a tricky summer, being knocked out of the last 16 of the World Cup with Brazil and then missing his pre-season return date as his representatives tried to revive talks over a contract extension.

If an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Madrid could be open to selling in January, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Last year Al Ahli were willing to offer a €1bn five-year contract offer for the 2024 Ballon d'Or runner-up.

Liverpool were also credited with interest earlier this window but are not in the mix for a player who earns around £520,000 a week.

Mourinho has been a strong defender of Vinicius and recently insisted to TNT Sports that he is going to get back on track.

'He is going to emerge,' the Portuguese promised. 'It is just a question of when.'

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres eyeing Arsenal January exit after Gunners' transfer pursuit
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres eyeing Arsenal January exit after Gunners' transfer pursuit

Viktor Gyokeres has struggled to find his footing in Mikel Arteta's Arsenal set-up over the past 12 months, with his future at the Emirates Stadium now under serious doubt as January transfer talk intensifies

View 2 Images Viktor Gyokeres could be looking for a move away from Arsenal (Image: David Price, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Viktor Gyokeres is reportedly keen to leave Arsenal due to a lack of first-team opportunities. The Swedish frontman was the subject of intense speculation in north London last summer, with the Gunners eventually wrapping up a £63.5million agreement with Sporting CP for the 28-year-old following a lengthy and protracted transfer saga.

‌



‌



Yet Gyokeres has found it difficult to establish himself in Mikel Arteta's system over the past 12 months, with his long-term future at the Emirates Stadium now under serious scrutiny. This season, Gyokeres has been restricted to a mere 56 Premier League minutes in total, and has unsurprisingly failed to register a single goal or assist despite his endeavours.

‌



Arsenal also devoted considerable energy towards landing Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez during the summer window, only to come away empty-handed owing to the La Liga outfit's firm refusal to sell combined with the Argentine forward's preference to join Barcelona instead.

‌



With the Madrid club making clear they have no intention of selling their prized asset to their Catalan rivals, and with Alvarez's relationship with the Atletico faithful somewhat strained following his Camp Nou ambitions this summer, Arsenal could be well-positioned to make a renewed push for the striker come January.

That would also all but cement Gyokeres' standing at his current club, with Alvarez likely to spearhead Arteta's attack upon his arrival given the substantial fee Atleti would demand for his services.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



According to TEAMtalk, Atletico Madrid also remains a possible destination for Gyokeres should he depart Arsenal. The La Liga outfit expressed an interest in the striker during their meetings with Andrea Berta over the summer, with discussions over a potential deal for Alvarez also regularly featuring in those conversations.

However, a number of other clubs across the Premier League, Italy and Germany are also keeping tabs on Gyokeres, meaning Arsenal could face a hectic period when the transfer window swings open again at the start of 2027.

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez remains a target for Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Despite shining in the Nations League with Sweden, netting four goals in four appearances throughout the recent international break, Arteta continues to place his trust in Kai Havertz as a false-nine rather than handing Gyokeres the opportunity to lead the line.

That's also despite Gyokeres' track record for thriving on English soil. The striker racked up 43 goals and 17 assists for Coventry City between 2021 and 2023 before securing his move to Sporting.

Article continues below

There, he enjoyed a further 97 goals and 28 assists in 102 games before landing in North London last summer.

Whether the Gunners boss deviates from his current approach or gives Gyokeres the chance he deserves on paper when Arsenal make the trip to the City Ground to face Nottingham Forest on Sunday, 18th October, remains to be seen.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola's bold Liverpool change pays off as nine-man Brentford cause their own undoing
Sports.content:
Liverpool came from behind to beat nine-man Brentford 2-1, with a change from Andoni Iraola sparking their turnaround. The Reds came away from the Gtech Community Stadium with all three points thanks to second-half goals from Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak.

But the stage was set by a dramatic first half that saw two decisions overturned by VAR and a deserved lead for Brentford. Keane Lewis-Potter fired the Bees in front shortly after Liverpool thought they'd been given a penalty.

But Keith Andrews' side - who went into Saturday unbeaten - were reduced to 10 when Yehor Yarmolyuk was deemed to have headbutted Jeremy Jacquet. Munoz and Isak eventually punished Brentford, although it wasn't straightforward for the visitors - even after another Brentford red card.

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Liverpool dealt Szoboszlai blow

When team news was confirmed, Liverpool fans were delighted to see the return to Dominik Szoboszlai. The Hungarian had missed his side's last two games but was back in the starting XI.

Unfortunately for Szoboszlai, he only lasted 32 minutes. The 25-year-old went down off the ball in what appeared to be an aggravation of his prior injury.

All eyes will be on Iraola's post-match comments and whether Szoboszlai will be fit to face Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday. And talk about bad things coming in threes...

‌



Where will Liverpool finish this season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 5 Images Dominik Szoboszlai's return from injury was short-lived (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

VAR dominates first half

It was all going wrong for Liverpool as half-time neared. Shortly after Szoboszlai's substitution, the Reds were given a penalty by John Brooks, as Dango Ouattara went sliding in on Alexis Mac Allister, and quickly had it taken away.

Replays showed that the only contact Brentford winger Ouattara made was with the ball, prompting Brooks to overturn his decision on the recommendation of video assistant referee Darren England. But VAR wasn't done getting involved - more that shortly.

‌



Brentford made the most of their reprieve, as Keane Lewis-Potter's header put the hosts 1-0 up. The goal came about after Mac Allister had lost possession inside his own half, allowing the hosts to pounce.

View 5 Images Keane Lewis-Potter broke the deadlock (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

The ball ended up at the feet of Igor Thiago, whose cross was perfectly converted by Lewis-Potter. Then finally something went right for Liverpool.

At a corner, Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet was having it out with Yehor Yarmolyuk, and the Brentford midfielder lost his cool with a headbutt akin to Rodrigo Bentancur's against Manchester United last weekend. England spotted in the incident and Brooks had no choice but to show Yarmolyuk a red card.

‌



No penalty was awarded because the ball wasn't in play at the time of the incident. Liverpool still had it all to do, but facing 10 men gave them a huge advantage.

View 5 Images Yehor Yarmolyuk was sent off for a headbutt (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

Iraola's bold change pays off

For a spell early in the second period, Brentford held their own with 10 men, testing Liverpool before their onslaught came about somewhat inadvertently. Jeremie Frimpong, brought on as a half-time substitute, had to come off just seven minutes after his introduction due to injury.

Would Iraola turn to Joe Gomez or opt for something bolder?

‌



The answer was the latter. Rio Ngumoha entered the fray, offering more of an attacking threat.

Ngumoha's introduction forced Victor Munoz to right-back, but it didn't put the Spaniard off bombing forward. Munoz would equalise with a brilliant solo goal, cutting inside and producing a cool finish from inside the 18-yard box.

View 5 Images Andoni Iraola made a game-changing attacking substitution (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

Iraola's men kept up the pressure and would be rewarded when Mac Allister picked out Bradley Barcola, who was free at the far post. His header wasn't ideal but Alexander Isak showed superb centre forward play to take the ball away from his man and slot past Caoimhin Kelleher.

‌



Although Ngumoha wasn't involved in either of the goals, the winger's presence changed the dynamic for Liverpool. Gomez did eventually come on to help the Reds over the line, a task made easier by Vitaly Janelt's second yellow card for a foul on Barcola in stoppage time.

Sports.title: Caulfield Cup horse Ohope Wins dies after being brought down by faller in the straight
Sports.content:
Caulfield Cup horse Ohope Wins dies after being brought down by faller in the straight

Last year’s Melbourne Cup winner Half Yours fell in an incident which brought down Ohope Wins. Chris Waller Racing posted a tribute on X, calling the mare "a true star of the turf"

View 2 Images Ohope Wins (circled) fell in the home straight

Kingswood's surprise victory in the Caulfield Cup was marred by the death of another runner after an incident in the home straight.

‌



‌



Half Yours, who won the race and the Melbourne Cup last year, fell near the the 300m mark and unshipped Mark Zahra and Ohope Wins, the mount of Jye McNeil, was brought down.

‌



Vets were quickly on the scene but Ohope Wins, from the stable of Chris Waller Racing, sadly could not be saved.

‌



A tribute from the stable and owners Yulong Investments on X read: "Few words can express our current emotions. Our wonderful Ohope Wins was sadly brought down in today's Caulfield Cup, and despite all efforts from the on-course veterinarians, could not be saved.

Lingfield Park gets local council approval to stage floodlit racing on all-weather track READ MORE :

"A dual Oaks winner and Champion in her native New Zealand, Ohope Wins was a true star of the turf, but to the people who looked after her everyday, she was so much more.

"She was brave. She was kind. She was full of character. But more importantly, she was loved. Our hearts go out to all involved throughout her career, especially those who cared for her on a daily basis. Thank you for all the kind messages."

‌



Zahra and McNeil were taken to hospital for observation but escaped injury according to an update from Racenet.

The Caulfield stewards report via Racing Victoria said: "An inquiry into the circumstances for Half Yours falling near the 300m was adjourned to a time and date to be fixed after taking evidence from Ethan Brown (Zahrann), Rachel King (Green Spaces) and apprentice Jabez Johnstone (Kings Valley), assisted by Matthew Hyland, Chief Executive Officer Victorian Jockey's Association.

View 2 Images Some of the Sportsbet Caulfield Cup field (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"A post-race veterinary examination revealed the gelding had sustained lacerations and abrasions. A veterinary clearance is required prior to being permitted to race again or officially trial."

Kingswood, trained by Gavin Bedggood, finished with the strong late run down the outside to claim victory in the 150th renewal of the race.

"Great performance, unbelievable effort by Gavin, he had the horse spot on," Allen said.

Article continues below

"Bit of a messy race, we were three wide early but he was in a nice rhythm, I didn't want to light him up and push forward.

"When a bit of a wave came around him at the 1200m I was happy to leave that go and track them into the race, I knew he'd show a good turn of foot … and he cantered up to them and put them away."

Enfjaar, trained in Britain by Roger Varian, earned his spot in next month's Lexus Melbourne Cup after finishing third under Ray Dawson and is 20-1 (from 25-1) with William Hill.

Sports.title: Arsenal plan major training ground revamp after falling behind rival upgrades
Sports.content:
Arsenal plan major training ground revamp after falling behind rival upgrades

Arsenal are eyeing up major redevelopments to their training ground after seeing their rivals pour investment into their facilities

View 2 Images Arsenal are looking to upgrade their training base

Arsenal are preparing to upgrade their London Colney training base having accepted that it has fallen behind the standard set by their rivals.

‌



‌



The Gunners have been at their current training ground since 1999 but in recent years the likes of Manchester United and Liverpool have either moved into a new facility or undergone major work to improve their infrastructure.

‌



The Daily Mail reports that internally that the north Londoners accept they need to catch up with their fellow Big Six teams and they're looking at ways they can upgrade.

‌



Arsenal are understood to have seen a refurbishment of their first-team gym and treatment spots whilst they've also been granted planning permission for a temporary women's gym, which is part of a more thorough development plan.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The Gunners are also looking into whether they can build a new state-of-the-art men’s hub which would see their facilities rival the best in Europe. If that comes to fruition then the long-term plan is for the women to eventually move into the facility that the men currently use.

It is understood that last season Arsenal were considering plans to erect stands around a pitch at London Colney, to in effect create a mini-stadium for the Under 21s and Under 19s. It is believed they had an informal talk with the local council before deciding not to seek planning permission.

The Under 21s play at the home of National League leaders Boreham Wood, but their Meadow Park ground is ultimately more of a drive for a lot of players and their families.

‌



View 2 Images The Gunners have been at their London Colney facility since 1999 (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal did also look into whether they could build a mini stadium at their training base, which would've served as a venue for their U18 and U21 teams. It is believed they had an informal talk with the local council before deciding not to seek planning permission.

In February 2024, Arsenal made Dubai-based real estate developers Sobha Realty their first training ground sponsor and the revenue from that has aided them commercially, whilst it will also have raised funds that can help with their planned improvements.

Article continues below

A bulk of the Big Six have also made moves to improve their stadiums. Anfield and the Etihad have enjoyed notable upgrades whilst Tottenham opened their state-of-the-art ground in 2019. The Emirates was purpose built with Arsenal moving there in 2006.

Sports.title: Emma Raducanu 'will win Wimbledon one day' but US Open winner told to make key change
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu 'will win Wimbledon one day' but US Open winner told to make key change

Emma Raducanu has been backed to win Wimbledon during her career despite failing to even make the last eight in SW19 as of yet

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu is looking to compete for another Grand Slam (Image: Getty)

Former British No 1 Dan Evans has claimed he "genuinely thinks Emma Raducanu will win Wimbledon one day" - but maintained she needs to be on the court more often.

‌



‌



The 23-year-old has been on our screens for half a decade having shot to stardom when she was just a teenager. Her stunning victory at the US Open in 2021 saw her profile skyrocket as she broke numerous records en route to claiming the top prize in New York.

‌



That did bring with it huge expectation and Raducanu has not scaled those heights since. She's not even reached a Grand Slam quarter-final outside of her US Open success but Evans still sees her as talented enough to claim one of the sport's biggest honours.

‌



He told the Telegraph : “She’s good, and I think – I’m saying this in as nice a way as possible – I think she thinks she’s good. Not in an arrogant way, but when she plays big matches, she’s like ‘Whatever. This is just another match.’ And yeah, I just think one day she’ll get it.

Andy Murray's return to tennis court confirmed as Rafael Nadal calls out Scot READ MORE :

“The crowd can play such a big part in tennis and you have to keep yourself together on Centre Court, because it’s a daunting place to go and play. But she looks like she loves it out there.”

‌



Raducanu's best result at Wimbledon has been the fourth round, which she reached twice. Last year she showed that she could mix it with the elite, bringing the best out of Aryna Sabalenka when they squared off on Centre Court.

Injuries have plagued her career, whilst she's also struggled to settle on a coach, which in itself has seen her cop criticism. Evans insists that Raducanu would need to spend more time honing her talent if she wants to realise her potential.

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu won the US Open in 2021 (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

“There’s no doubt she needs to have a racket in her hand a bit more," he said. "I’m sure she’s getting pushed side-to-side by endorsements, and there’s a bit of tug of war on what she needs to do, what she doesn’t. I admit I’ve not watched her practices very often, but from what I’m told she’s a good trainer: she works for two, three hours in a row with hardly any break.”

Tim Henman is another former British No 1 who believes Raducanu has it in her to win another Grand Slam. "When you've done it once, you know it's possible to do it again. But ultimately, it all comes down to the process and the daily work," he said.

But last year Mark Petchey, who did serve as her interim coach for a period, said it "won't be easy" for Raducanu to win another major title - but believes it is possible if she changed her baseline game against the "big hitters".

Sports.title: Real Madrid demand La Liga chief Javier Tebas quits after Nazi comparison
Sports.content:
Real Madrid demand La Liga chief Javier Tebas quits after Nazi comparison

La Liga president Javier Tebas compared Real Madrid's media output to 'Nazi propaganda' in an extraordinary claim and Los Blancos have furiously hit back

View 2 Images La Liga president Javier Tebas (Image: Jan Kruger/Getty Images for Soccerex)

Real Madrid have demanded the resignation of La Liga president Javier Tebas after he extraordinarily compared the club's media strategy to 'Nazi propaganda'.

‌



‌



Tebas accused selected journalists of promoting the views of senior Real officials, stating they were acting as the club's 'official mouthpiece' portraying Los Blancos as victims of refereeing decisions.

‌



"Real Madrid's management directs an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing," Tebas wrote on social media.

‌



"Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion, and point fingers at the enemies.

"That method recalls propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Nazi Germany's Minister of Propaganda: systematic repetition, construction of an enemy, and subordination of facts to the narrative.

"The comparison is with those propaganda techniques, not with an ideology or, of course, with the Madridista fanbase. Real Madrid TV is a central piece of that machinery. Where is the full match analysis for each round of games?

"Where are the possible errors that harm other clubs or those that favor Real Madrid? If they applied the same magnifying glass to every match, the result might ruin their script. But the script demands that Real Madrid always appear as the victim."

‌



Real responded in a lengthy statement on their website, branding the comparison 'morally repugnant'.

"The repeated conduct of Javier Tebas shows a lack of neutrality, respect and impartiality incompatible with his institutional responsibilities," they wrote.

"Real Madrid CF considers it absolutely intolerable and extraordinarily serious that someone who occupies two positions of utmost responsibility in Spanish football should resort to a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management and its television.

"His constant attacks on Real Madrid and those who demand transparency and regeneration constitute, in the opinion of our club, a real scourge for Spanish football.

"Consequently, Real Madrid CF demands his immediate resignation as president of LaLiga and vice president of the Royal Spanish Football Federation."

‌



Tebas insists he is unconcerned by Real's latest demand, accusing the club and 'their lapdogs' of trying to destroy La Liga.

He wrote: "I've lost count of the times that, in thirteen years, Real Madrid's leaders have demanded my resignation or tried to disqualify me: complaints to the CSD, directly or through third parties, criminal lawsuits… Today's is just another one.

"What still hasn't arrived are the responses. They confuse neutrality with independence. My position demands independence, not passivity in the face of injustice or silence in the face of the continuous, disproportionate, and insulting attacks from Real Madrid TV and its lapdogs on our competition.

"The La Liga president must defend it. Including against Real Madrid's leaders. My conclusion: they seek to DESTROY the national competition.

"What they haven't achieved so far with the Superliga, they're trying with a distorted narrative from their media and their lapdogs. They call it regeneration while attacking the prestige of the competition they participate in."
