Sports.title: Solomon Dacres Picks Himself to Stop Bakhodir Jalolov
Sports.content:
Solomon Dacres expects to stop Bakhodir Jalolov tonight, but his record offers little support for that prediction against the 6’7″ two-time Olympic gold medalist.

Jalolov has looked sluggish enough lately to give critics room for skepticism. The dominant puncher seen in the amateur ranks rarely appears in his prize ring outings, prompting a few observers to sniff an upset. Regardless, Jalolov looking flat does not suddenly transform Dacres into a top threat.

“Got to get him out of there, man,” Dacres told SecondsOut. “Mid to late rounds.”

That would be a considerable leap for a fighter whose most revealing professional result remains his first-round stoppage defeat to David Adeleye in December 2024.

Dacres describes that loss as a “blip,” but it came against the most notable opponent he had faced. Across five years as a professional, he hasn’t built a record of beating contenders that would make a Jalolov knockout seem likely.

His points win against Vladyslav Sirenko also requires context. Sirenko amassed numbers without testing himself against true threats, meaning that victory hardly proves Dacres can deal with Jalolov’s height, reach, and southpaw boxing skills.

“This fight here is beyond English title level, man,” Dacres said. “This is like world level.”

Jalolov deserves criticism for how slowly his professional career has moved and for performances that haven’t matched expectations. His Olympic medals don’t excuse that, and Dacres has an opportunity to make him work.

Expecting Dacres to win because Jalolov underwhelms ignores his own modest punch output. Managing just three stoppages across ten victories, he lacks the firepower to back up big talk.

For Dacres to land the kinds of sustained combinations required to stop someone Jalolov’s size, he has to pin him down. Jalolov does not fight like a traditional, stationary heavyweight slugger. Even when he looks uninspired, he uses lateral footwork, maintains long range with his southpaw lead hand, and angles off before opponents can set their feet.

Dacres lacks both the foot speed to cut off the ring effectively and the explosive one-punch power to make Jalolov cautious. If Dacres tries to force the issue, he’ll put himself at risk of getting caught. Pressing aggressively against a 6’7″ southpaw who excels at firing straight left hands down the pipe is asking for trouble.

Unless Jalolov completely checks out mentally and stands against the ropes to trade, Dacres will be eating long jabs and counters all night, with a Jalolov stoppage being the far more probable outcome.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Claims Critics Were Happy He Lost
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma sounds bitter about the criticism following his defeat to Filip Hrgovic, claiming some people were happy to see him lose. His disappointment is clear, but his response leaves unanswered whether those critics identified weaknesses he needs to correct.

The young heavyweight repeatedly insists he doesn’t care about outside opinions. Yet his comments suggest the reaction has stayed with him, particularly when it came from people he previously supported.

“I’ve seen personalities change and I’ve seen a couple people be happy that I lost,” Itauma told The Stomping Ground. “I’m like, ‘Wow.’ I was like, ‘Man, I’ve cheered you on.’”

Itauma doesn’t name those people or explain what they said. That makes it difficult to judge whether they celebrated his defeat or offered criticism he didn’t want to hear. Those are different things, and his account provides little detail to support the harsher interpretation.

Being supportive of another fighter also doesn’t require that person to approve of your performance or your corner’s decisions. Someone can want Itauma to succeed while believing his preparation or tactics need work.

Asked about criticism of Ben Davison and his training team, Itauma emphasized their healthy relationship. That explains his loyalty, but a good relationship doesn’t answer questions about what happened during the fight.

To his credit, Itauma acknowledged his responsibility.

“Ultimately I lost the fight and I take full responsibility for that.”

He also credited Hrgovic’s experience and admitted the defeat was difficult to accept. There is recognition that he encountered something his previous fights and sparring hadn’t prepared him for.

The concern is how quickly the conversation about his team becomes a discussion about other people’s personalities. If criticism gets interpreted as pleasure at his failure, potentially valuable observations become easier to dismiss.

Itauma doesn’t have to agree with every pundit. But his return will depend on correcting what went wrong against Hrgovic. Whether the people pointing it out cheered for him beforehand has little bearing on whether their points were right.

Itauma seems to be taking the criticism personally. Rather than discussing what the critics got right or wrong, he’s talking about people being happy he lost. That gives him a reason to brush aside points that might help him.

He may feel let down by people he’s cheered for, but that doesn’t make their criticism wrong. They can support him and still think his conditioning, defense, or preparation wasn’t good enough.

Calling them haters won’t fix any of that. If he dismisses good advice because he doesn’t like hearing it, the next good heavyweight he faces could punish the same flaws.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Sees Hadribeaj’s Left Hand Threatening Fundora
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora could be vulnerable to a left hand he doesn’t see coming against Ermal Hadribeaj, according to Tim Bradley, who gives the challenger a chance of springing an upset on Saturday night despite picking the champion to win.

Bradley sees danger in the southpaw pairing. Fundora’s height and punch output can make him difficult to beat round after round, but Hadribeaj’s awkward delivery could create an opening for a punch that changes the fight.

“Does he have a lot of knockouts? No. But sometimes it’s not about having a lot of power. It’s about catching a guy when he don’t see a punch coming,” Bradley said on his channel.

That is the route Bradley identifies for Hadribeaj. Trying to match Fundora’s volume would require the challenger to spend long stretches within punching range. A well-timed left hand could punish Fundora while he is attacking.

Bradley referenced Sergio Martinez’s knockout of Paul Williams when discussing the danger, using that southpaw pairing to illustrate how an unexpected shot can undo a tall fighter. The comparison describes a possible opening; it doesn’t establish that Hadribeaj has Martinez’s timing or finishing ability.

“I think he has a damn good chance of winning, man. I really do.”

Bradley also believes an unfamiliar challenger can arrive better prepared than the champion expects. He recalled studying Junior Witter for a year before taking his title, searching for weaknesses while Witter knew comparatively little about him.

Hadribeaj could have spent similar time studying Fundora. Finding an opening on video, though, is only the beginning. He still has to exploit it while dealing with the champion’s reach and constant punching.

Bradley gives Fundora credit for living in the gym and improving rather than assuming he will underestimate his opponent. His final pick is Fundora on experience.

The upset case rests on Hadribeaj making one opening count. His modest knockout record makes that harder to sell, but Bradley believes the left hand gives him a chance.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Turns Toward Liam Paro Unification
Sports.content:
Devin Haney could keep his November 28 date in Atlanta and pursue a second welterweight title against Liam Paro after negotiations with Shakur Stevenson broke down.

An official monitoring the talks told BoxingScene’s Lance Pugmire that Haney will move toward a unification against IBF champion Paro at State Farm Arena. The fight has not been announced, but it would give the WBO champion a route back into the ring after months spent negotiating with Shakur.

Haney has a hold on the venue for November 28, with Brian Norman Jr. and Tiger Johnson penciled in for separate support bouts, according to the report.

Keeping that date would be significant. Haney has not fought since beating Norman on November 22 last year. Another round of prolonged negotiations would threaten to stretch his absence beyond twelve months.

The split with Shakur comes with conflicting explanations. Shakur accused Haney of changing the proposed weight from 145 to 147 pounds. Haney rejected that account, writing on X:

“I agreed to 145.”

Haney also accused Shakur of attempting to introduce a rehydration clause and complained about the time spent negotiating:

“I wasted six months negotiating with you.”

An unnamed official quoted by Pugmire offered a different version, alleging that Shakur accepted 145 pounds without a rehydration clause before Haney’s side changed the weight to 147. Those competing accounts leave the cause of the breakdown disputed.

A Paro fight would allow Haney to turn his attention toward collecting another belt at his established weight. It would also give the Atlanta event a championship main event while Shakur searches for his next opponent.

The next step is getting Paro finalized. Haney has a reported venue hold and a possible opponent, but after spending months on a fight that fell apart, he needs an agreement that gets him back into the ring.

Paro is a significantly better stylistic matchup for fans than Shakur Stevenson. A Haney against Shakur pairing had all the ingredients for twelve rounds of clinching and feinting. Both guys prefer to operate on the outside, pick their moments, and control distance through defensive positioning. Put them together, and you get a low-output chess match where neither wants to lead.

Paro forces the issue. When Paro upset Subriel Matias in Puerto Rico, he showed he does not mind trading in the pocket, digging to the body, and fighting through rough spots.

That pressure directly tests Haney’s vulnerabilities. Haney cannot simply coast behind a safety-first jab for twelve rounds if Paro is actively crowding him, ripping hooks to the ribs, and making every clinch costly. Haney would have to throw real combinations to earn respect and keep Paro off him.

Ghana News.title: EC must command public confidence regardless of which party is in power – Victoria Bright
Ghana News.content:
Private legal practitioner Victoria Bright has called for consistency in the appointment of Electoral Commission (EC) officials, stressing that the Commission must command public confidence regardless of which political party is in power.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, she said the appointment of the two new Deputy Chairpersons of the EC must be assessed against consistent standards of constitutional legality, professional suitability and public confidence in their independence.

“I think we must approach this issue with a consistent principle. And that principle is that the Electoral Commission must command public confidence, regardless of which party is in government,” she said.

Ms Bright cautioned against changing the standards applied to appointments whenever political power changes hands, arguing that the credibility of the electoral body depends not only on the legality of its appointments but also on whether Ghanaians have confidence in its impartiality.

She identified three key questions that should guide the assessment of the appointments: whether the constitutional requirements had been met, whether the appointees were suitable for their respective positions, and whether the process provided citizens with reasonable grounds to trust their independence.

According to her, these questions are related but must be considered separately.

She noted that the 1992 Constitution empowers the President to appoint Electoral Commissioners on the advice of the Council of State, while also protecting the Commission from external direction or control in the performance of its functions.

Although she acknowledged that the appointments were not unconstitutional, she said concerns remained about their implications for public confidence in the institution.

“The appointments are not unconstitutional, but they do cause concern,” she said.

Ms Bright argued that, for an institution as sensitive as the EC, the perception of independence was almost as important as independence itself.

She said the central issue was not simply whether the appointments were lawful, but whether they inspired confidence in the neutrality of the Commission across the political divide.

Addressing the appointment of Emelia Afi Agbenyo, Ms Bright said concerns about her perceived political affiliations were relevant to the wider discussion about public confidence in the EC.

She argued that her reported close association with the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) provided a basis for citizens to question how the appointing authorities had considered the potential implications for perceptions of impartiality.

However, Ms Bright stressed that Agbenyo’s qualifications and professional experience deserved fair consideration, adding that competence alone did not automatically resolve questions about independence.

“For me, her qualifications and professional experience do deserve fair consideration. But both competence and independence are necessary for this kind of appointment. And evidence of one does not automatically answer questions about the other,” she said.

On the appointment of Dr Joseph Kweku Asamoah, she acknowledged that his previous experience within the EC was relevant to his new role.

NPP and NDC challenged to maintain consistency

Ms Bright also recalled the controversy surrounding appointments to the EC under former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, including the appointment of Chairperson Jean Mensa, who is allegedly related to the former First Lady, Rebecca Akufo-Addo.

She said those appointments attracted objections from civil society organisations, including the Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO), as well as criticism from the NDC, which was then in opposition.

In her view, the history of those disagreements meant that both the NPP and the NDC had questions of consistency to answer over their positions on appointments to the electoral body.

For the NPP, she said the question was why concerns about partisan associations should carry decisive weight under the current administration when similar concerns were resisted while the party was in government.

For the NDC, she questioned how its own appointments measured up to the standards it had demanded when it was in opposition.

Ms Bright maintained that political parties should uphold the principles they advocated while in opposition once they assumed office.

She cautioned that controversial appointments made by previous administrations should not become a justification for repeating similar controversies.

“Earlier controversial appointments cannot become a standing justification for further controversial appointments. We can't keep going on and on,” she said.

Bright questions argument about balancing EC composition

The private legal practitioner also expressed concern about the reported explanation from the government side that the appointments were intended to rebalance the composition of the EC.

She said such an argument would be troubling if the balance being discussed referred to partisan representation within the Commission.

According to her, the EC should not be viewed as a body made up of representatives of competing political interests whose appointments are intended to counterbalance one another.

Ms Bright warned that such an approach could undermine the Commission's role as an impartial arbiter of the electoral process.

She maintained that the priority should be to protect the independence and credibility of the institution rather than to create a perception that its composition reflects a political contest between the governing party and the opposition.

Her comments come after President John Dramani Mahama swore in Dr Asamoah and Ms Agbenyo as Deputy Chairpersons of the EC on October 16.

Ghana News.title: NDC must dissociate itself from Obuasi SHTS head over sexual abuse allegations – Vicky Bright
Ghana News.content:
Vicky Bright

International corporate lawyer Victoria Bright has urged the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to dissociate itself from the head of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), who is reportedly seeking political office, amid sexual abuse allegations against him.

She said anyone facing such serious allegations should not be given greater political influence while the matter remains under scrutiny, stressing the need to protect students and establish the facts through a fair investigation.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, Ms Bright questioned why the headmaster would seek political office amid the allegations.

“This is exactly the problem with our country. Why should someone like that be contesting for a political post? It is something that defies all logic and all reasoning. I do not understand,” she said.

Read also: Obuasi SHTS head accused of sexually abusing students is NDC Juaben secretary seeking chairmanship

Ms Bright said the governing party should distance itself from the individual, saying that people facing serious allegations of abuse should not be placed in positions that could increase their power or influence.

“And if I were part of the governing party, I would disassociate myself from someone like that. These are not the kind of people who should be given more power. They should not be empowered to carry on perpetrating these kinds of acts,” she said.

Her comments come amid public concern over the sexual abuse allegations involving the head of Obuasi SHTS.

Ms Bright said the response to the allegations should focus on protecting students, establishing the facts and holding anyone found responsible accountable.

She said that the allegations must be investigated fairly, with the evidence guiding any decisions on responsibility.

“The measure of our response will be whether students are protected, whether the allegations are fairly investigated, and whether responsibility is established wherever the evidence leads,” she said.

Describing the allegations as a serious breach of trust, the lawyer called for a thorough investigation into the headmaster’s conduct.

She also said the need to establish what other people who may have had knowledge of the alleged incidents did about them.

“The key question for me is what each responsible person knew, when they knew it, and what they did next,” she said.

Ms Bright called for the matter to be treated with the seriousness it deserved, given the potential risks to students and the responsibility of school authorities to protect them.

She said the headmaster should face prosecution and imprisonment if an investigation established his guilt.

“It’s a total abuse of trust, and he must be fully investigated and jailed if he’s found to be culpable,” she said.

This comes after JoyNews investigative correspondent Manasseh Azure Awuni said the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School in the Ashanti Region, who has been suspended over sexual abuse allegations against female students, is a serving constituency secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and an aspirant for the chairmanship position.

According to him, the headmaster intends to contest the chairmanship at the party’s constituency delegates’ conference, expected before the end of the year.

Ghana News.title: Trump deals with Putin, so why should Ghana fear BRICS? – Ablakwa asks
Ghana News.content:
Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has defended Ghana’s pursuit of BRICS membership, arguing that the United States’ own dealings with Russia demonstrate the importance of pursuing national interests.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 17, 2026, Mr Ablakwa cited President Donald Trump’s recent diesel agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to challenge warnings that Ghana’s engagement with the bloc could attract American sanctions.

He argued that Ghana should not be discouraged from building relations with BRICS countries while Washington continued to pursue economic agreements with those same nations.

Mr Ablakwa said that while critics were urging Ghana to fear Mr Trump’s influence, the US President was making strategic decisions to advance American interests.

"If we really analyse this, President Trump has not stopped dealing with these BRICS countries. He (Donald Trump) has just got into a deal with Russia, President Putin, for diesel as his midterm elections approach, and President Zelensky (Ukrainian President) is furious,"

"So we are being told that because of threats from President Trump, our foreign policies should be determined by threats that other countries may be putting out when those same countries are themselves being strategic, being smart, and they are dealing with the countries that you are afraid to deal with," he argued.

Read Also: Ghana risks 10% to 100% tariffs on exports to US under Trump’s threats as it moves to join BRICS

He also pointed to economic ties between China and the United States as evidence that cooperation could continue despite political differences. "Indeed, China remains the biggest creditor to the US."

The Minister linked Ghana’s BRICS ambitions to the vision of the country’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, presenting the move as consistent with his pursuit of international solidarity and economic independence.

His comments followed concerns, particularly from the opposition New Patriotic Party, about the possible implications of closer engagement with the bloc for Ghana’s relations with Washington.

On October 6, Mr Ablakwa announced that Cabinet had approved Ghana’s decision to formally apply to join BRICS, saying the move would diversify international partnerships and create opportunities for trade, investment and economic cooperation.

The Trump–Putin agreement cited by the Minister was announced on October 9 following a telephone conversation between the two leaders.

According to Reuters, Mr Trump said Russia would supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel to US and global markets as part of efforts to reduce fuel prices.

The arrangement involved easing sanctions on Russian diesel exports. It drew criticism from Ukraine and US lawmakers concerned that the additional revenue could support Moscow’s war effort.

Ghana News.title: Asking Agbenyo to resign will mean everyone else at EC must leave – Vicky Bright
Ghana News.content:
Private legal practitioner Victoria Bright has described calls for newly appointed Electoral Commission (EC) Deputy Chairperson Emelia Affi Agbenyo to resign as excessive, arguing that applying the same standard to other commissioners could require the entire Commission to step down.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, Ms Bright said the focus should be on improving the appointment process to ensure that the EC commands public confidence, rather than singling out one appointee for resignation.

Her comments follow a call by the Coalition of Domestic Election Observers (CODEO) for Ms Agbenyo to resign over concerns about her past political activities and their potential impact on public confidence in the Commission’s independence and impartiality.

Ms Bright argued that demanding Ms Agbenyo’s resignation while allowing other commissioners with perceived political affiliations to remain in office would amount to applying different standards to individuals serving on the same institution.

“I think that's a step too far. If they are saying that, then everybody there should resign, from the EC Chair down. The EC Chair, we know, has a very strong family and political affiliation with the opposition party,” she said.

She added that other members of the Commission also had political affiliations, questioning why one individual should be singled out for resignation while others remained in office.

“So you can't pick and choose. You can't choose one and say resign, and this one stays and all of that. We are where we are,” she said.

READ ALSO: CODEO calls for Emelia Agbnyo’s resignation over partisan ties

Ms Bright said the focus should instead be on addressing the weaknesses in the process for appointing members of the EC to prevent similar controversies in the future.

She maintained that previous administrations had made appointments that attracted criticism over perceived political affiliations, adding that the country needed to move beyond the recurring disagreements and consider the kind of electoral management body it wanted to establish.

She argued that the debate should not be limited to whether appointments made by one administration were acceptable while those made by another were not.

According to her, successive governments had appointed individuals perceived to be aligned with their respective political parties, making it necessary to reconsider the process rather than continue the cycle.

“Every party that has come into power has appointed its own people. So for me, we should now look beyond that and ask ourselves a very, very important question. The test for me is what kind of Electoral Commission that we want to build,” she said.

EC must inspire confidence across political divide

Ms Bright said the ultimate test should be whether the Commission could earn the trust of both major political parties and the wider Ghanaian public, particularly when its decisions did not favour their interests.

She stressed that improving the appointment process was necessary to establish an electoral body whose independence and impartiality would be accepted across the political divide.

“The test for me is whether we are building an Electoral Commission that both parties and the wider public, Ghanaians, can trust when decisions go against them,” she said.

Ghana News.title: Akosua Manu calls for a proper protection framework for sexually abused children
Ghana News.content:
Adviser on Gender and Social Protection to former Vice-President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, Akosua Manu, has called for a proper national child protection framework to safeguard pupils who suffer sexual abuse in schools.

She said Ghana needs a clear system through which children can report abuse, receive protection and seek justice without fear of exposure or intimidation.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile programme on Saturday, October 17, during a discussion on sexual abuse allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Ms Manu said the current arrangements did not adequately protect children who reported such cases.

“So, fundamentally, there’s no protection for these girls, for these children in the schools,” she said.

She said that a national framework should establish safe and confidential reporting channels to ensure that children are protected and their concerns handled with the seriousness they deserve.

“I would think to cure the problem, there should be a framework, a national protection framework, safeguarding these girls, where reports of such cases go to, that there should be a channel where you report to, where you get protected, where your name or where your form or whatever is hidden,” she said.

Ms Manu said that the system must put the welfare of the child first, particularly when the alleged abuse involves someone in a position of authority within a school.

“It should be such that the child is prioritised,” she added.

Ms Manu also raised concerns about situations in which children are expected to report abuse to the same school authorities they accuse of misconduct.

She said such arrangements could discourage victims from speaking out, especially when they fear that their complaints may not be handled fairly.

“But I believe fundamentally a child should not have to seek justice from the same authorities that they’re accusing of abuse,” she said.

Ms Manu referred to a News card shared by JoyNews which stated that six headteachers had allegedly sexually assaulted girls in their schools since 2025.

She said the reported cases raised serious concerns about the effectiveness of existing measures to protect pupils and called for urgent policy action.

“You can imagine the number of girls that have gone through this,” she said.

"And you can imagine the ones that are under-reported. It is a national crisis,” she added, referring to the reported cases.

The allegations against the Obuasi SHTS headmaster have not, in the details provided, been established as proven findings. Ms Manu’s call for reforms centres on ensuring that allegations of abuse are reported safely and investigated properly, while protecting children from further harm.

She called for a policy that would make children feel comfortable reporting abuse and confident that their complaints would be handled appropriately.

“We need to put a policy in place that makes kids comfortable,” she said.

"The last place a child should not feel safe should not be a school. At least, at the very least, from home to school, they should feel safe," she added.

Ghana News.title: No more cover-ups – Zonta demands action against sexual abuse in schools
Ghana News.content:
File photo

The Zonta Clubs of Ghana have called on the Ministry of Education to take urgent action against sexual abuse in schools, demanding swift investigations, accountability and protection for survivors.

In a statement, the clubs described the sexual abuse of schoolgirls by teachers and headteachers as a grave betrayal of trust and the duty of care owed to children.

“Schools must be places of safety, learning, and opportunity, not environments where girls are exploited, violated, and robbed of their childhood by the very people charged with protecting them,” the statement said.

The clubs urged the ministry to ensure that allegations are investigated promptly and independently, with due process and appropriate sanctions.

They called for the dismissal and prosecution of teachers and headteachers found to have sexually abused children, stressing that professional connections and institutional positions must not shield perpetrators from accountability.

School authorities who conceal abuse or retaliate against survivors must also be held accountable, the statement added.

“A teacher’s position is not a licence to exploit a child, and a headmaster’s authority is not a shield against justice,” the clubs stated.

Their demands include zero tolerance for child sexual abuse in educational institutions, immediate protection and psychosocial support for survivors, and action against officials who fail to respond to credible reports.

The clubs also called for measures to protect survivors from victim-blaming, intimidation and retaliation.

“Every survivor deserves justice, dignity, and support — not silence or retaliation,” the statement said.

They urged the Ministry of Education to move beyond condemnation and demonstrate through concrete action that children’s safety is a priority.

The statement was issued on behalf of the Zonta Clubs of Ghana by Adodo Abla Adih-Nuviadenu, President of the Zonta Club of Accra Metropolitan.

It listed the participating clubs as Accra, Accra II, Tema, Accra Metropolitan and Accra Jubilee.

Ghana News.title: Police arrest 41 suspected criminals in intelligence-led operation at Lapaz and Chantan
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Police Service has arrested 41 suspects during an intelligence-led operation targeting criminal and narcotics-related activities at Lapaz and Chantan in Accra.

The operation, carried out by the Service’s Special Operations Team (SOT) at about noon on Thursday, October 15, led to the arrest of 35 males and six females.

In a statement, the police said quantities of dried leaves suspected to be narcotic substances were retrieved during searches conducted on the suspects and within the areas covered by the operation.

According to the police, investigations are under way to establish the source and ownership of the suspected narcotic substances, as well as their intended use.

The Service said the findings would determine the next course of action against the suspects.

“Investigations are ongoing to establish the source, ownership and intended use of the suspected narcotic substances, after which appropriate legal action will be taken against any suspect found culpable,” the statement said.

Ghana News.title: World Food Day 2026: Forikrom women champion local foods and call for stronger support for rural farmers
Ghana News.content:
As the world marks World Food Day under the theme “Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow”, women farmers in Forikrom, in the Bono East Region, have added their voices to the global call for action, urging Ghanaians to eat local, support rural farmers, and push for policies that strengthen food security.

The international day, an initiative of the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), comes amid growing pressure on global agrifood systems, with over 36 million people in West and Central Africa still struggling to access sufficient food.

In Forikrom, the day was marked by a mini local food Durbar at the training camp of the Abrono Organic Farming Project (ABOFAP), organised in collaboration with the Rural Women Farmers Association of Ghana (RUWFAG).

The event brought together women farmers, agricultural extension officers, nutrition experts, and traditional leaders to celebrate Ghana's local foods and advocate for sustainable farming.

Executive Director of ABOFAP, Nana Kwao Adams, encouraged participants to prioritise locally produced food and to work harder to produce enough food for the country.

"We should eat our own food and keep working harder to produce the needed food for the country. It is time we look at policies that will empower rural farmers so that farming becomes sustainable," he said.

Chairing the function, Forikromhemaa Nana Sakyiwaa Abanaba, admonished Ghanaians to embrace the consumption of organic foods, which she described as healthy and beneficial.

"I urge everyone to consume organic foods. They are healthy for our bodies and good for our well-being," she stated.

Anita Suntaa, National Coordinator for the Rural Women Farmers Association of Ghana, called for policies that will help women farmers produce enough food.

"We need policies that will help women farmers produce enough food. This includes the establishment of irrigation systems to aid all-year-round farming, particularly in the Upper West Region," she said.

Festus Addai, the Techiman Municipal Agric Extension Officer, noted that despite available resources to produce more food, it is quite unfortunate that many people still go hungry.

"With available resources to produce more food, it's quite unfortunate that a lot of people still go hungry. More needs to be done to address this," he emphasised.

Faiza Issah, Nutrition Officer at the Forikrom Health Centre, admonished participants to consume local foods that contain the four-star diet—a nutrition framework promoting a balanced intake of different food groups for good health.

"I admonish us all to consume our local foods that contain the four-star diet for our good health," she advised.

This year's World Food Day commemoration in Forikrom served as a reminder that sustainable food systems begin with supporting those who produce our food—especially rural women farmers—and with a collective commitment to eating what we grow.

As the world reflects on the challenges facing global agrifood systems, the message from Forikrom is clear: empower rural farmers, invest in irrigation, promote organic and local foods, and ensure that no one goes hungry.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Pope Leo returns to Vatican after lung cancer surgery
World.content:
Doctors say they are seeing ‘continued improvement’ after the US-born pope had a lump removed from his lung on Tuesday.

Pope Leo has returned to the Vatican, four days after receiving surgery for lung cancer in Rome.

The pope said he was feeling “much better” when asked about his health as he was driven away from the Gemelli University Hospital against cries of “holiness” from onlookers on Saturday.

Leo had the lower lobe of his right lung removed on Tuesday. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, which is the most common type of lung cancer.

He is set to resume some duties on Sunday, when he greets the faithful with the Catholic Church’s traditional Angelus blessing.

Doctors have said tests confirmed his “continued improvement”.

Since having surgery, the pope has had a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, held meetings with senior aides and celebrated mass in a makeshift hospital chapel.

Leo thanked staff in the Rome hospital for the work they do every day “taking care of the sick in their fragility”, as well as for “what they had done for him”, a Vatican spokesperson said.

Pope Leo’s next major engagement is a trip to Latin America in mid-November, giving him about three weeks to recover for an ambitious journey that includes a dozen flights and two helicopter trips.

Leo is the first pope from the United States, hailing from Chicago. However, he has spent decades living and working across South America and is a naturalised Peruvian citizen.

World.title: Trump faces bipartisan backlash over Russia sanctions waiver
World.content:
Republicans and Democrats condemn Trump’s decision to suspend sanctions, saying it undermines support for Ukraine.

United States President Donald Trump has drawn criticism from Democrats and Republicans after waiving sanctions targeting Russia and countries that buy its oil and gas, days before the restrictions were due to take effect under a law he signed last month.

In an executive order signed on Friday, Trump said the waiver was in the US national interest. He did not specify when the restrictions might be introduced, saying they would remain suspended until he or senior officials determined further action was appropriate.

The move has been condemned by both Democrats and Republicans.

Republican Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina called the decision “beyond irresponsible”, accusing the administration of capitulating to Russian President Vladimir Putin, who launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

“What part of enforcing a law passed 86-11 by the Senate does the President and his advisers not understand?” Tillis wrote on social media on Saturday.

Republican Senator John Cornyn of Texas also criticised the move, saying the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina, who championed the legislation, “would be appalled”.

Representative Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat, said Trump’s move betrayed Ukraine and disregarded Congress’s intent to punish Russia for its invasion.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts accused Trump of “thumbing his nose” at Congress and enabling Putin to continue his war against Ukraine, urging colleagues to take action to reverse the decision.



The legislation, named after the deceased Senator Graham, was passed with overwhelming bipartisan support. It would have allowed tariffs of up to 100 percent on goods from countries that continued buying Russian oil and gas or helped Moscow evade sanctions. The bill was then signed into law by Trump last month. Before he unexpectedly died earlier this year, Graham had worked for about a year to get the legislation passed.

The decision came shortly after Trump agreed to a deal to buy Russian diesel in an effort to lower fuel prices, which have risen amid the US-Israeli war on Iran. Politicians from both parties have questioned whether the deal would meaningfully reduce energy costs while providing Moscow with revenue to support its war effort.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also criticised the sanctions waiver on Saturday, saying easing pressure on Russia would encourage further attacks.

“Financial rewards for Putin – all of this only encourages him to keep attacking,” Zelenskyy posted on X, urging the US to maintain pressure on Moscow.

Congress is in recess until after the November 3 midterm elections, limiting immediate opportunities to challenge Trump’s decision. Representative Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, has introduced legislation to block the separate diesel deal with Russia.

World.title: Why are Latin American countries building closer ties with Israel?
World.content:
A wave of new Latin American leaders reverses measures meant to isolate Israel after its genocidal war on Gaza.

When Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar announced on October 8 that Colombia would be moving its embassy to Jerusalem, he made sure to point out how important the development was for his country’s diplomatic narrative, and that it heralded warming relations with Latin American governments.

“We will work hard because this is the diplomatic battle over the truth,” Saar said. “And the truth is, Jerusalem was always the capital of one nation.”

Brazil, Saar went on to say, might soon join Colombia and the growing list of Latin American countries that had moved their embassies to Jerusalem, the disputed city claimed by Israelis and Palestinians as their capital.

Latin America’s relationship with Israel is shifting, as right-wing parties come into power in the region and pro-Israel politicians use their support for the country to rally voters.

Brazil, the largest country in the region, is in the midst of a presidential election campaign in which the relationship with Israel has become a key talking point.

President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, a left-wing ardent supporter of Palestine, is locked in a close contest with right-wing rival Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. He has sported Israeli flags at campaign rallies and played up his friendship with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The pair are scheduled to take part in a run-off election after Bolsonaro performed surprisingly strongly in the first -round, apparently raising hopes for a detente with Israeli officials like the foreign minister.



Last month, for instance, Colombia and Israel began allowing their citizens to travel visa-free between their countries, yet another signal the newly inaugurated government of Abelardo de la Espriella wants to restore ties that were cut in the wake of Israel’s war on Gaza.

Experts say the realignment with Israel is driven, in part, by new leaders trying to signal they have joined a regional alignment with United States President Donald Trump. But it’s also being fuelled by a massive lobbying effort in which Evangelical Christian groups and Israeli-government-backed organisations in the region have pushed Latin American countries to support Israel.

“It’s not one factor or the other, but a convergence,” said Marta Tawil Kuri, Research Professor at the Center for International Studies at the College of Mexico. “Right-wing leaderships seeking validation from Washington, evangelical bases giving them electoral and ideological grounding, and an Israeli diplomatic offensive that finds fertile ground in Latin America precisely as its image deteriorates elsewhere.”

“The most Zionist president in the world”

Colombia’s last leader, Gustavo Petro, severed ties with Israel over what he said was the genocidal war on Gaza. He stopped exporting Colombian coal to Israel, cut military and security cooperation and planned to open a Colombian embassy to Palestine. The former left-wing fighter seemed to take every public opportunity to criticise Israel, even using a trip to New York City for a United Nations summit to take part in a protest against Trump and the war on Gaza.

His successor, de la Espriella, has rapidly reversed Bogota’s stance on Israel since coming to power in August, announcing plans to move his country’s embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem, re-appoint ambassadors and even recognising Israeli control over the occupied Syrian territory of the Golan Heights.

Strong presidential systems and weak, unprofessional diplomatic corps allow new heads of state to quickly pivot on issues such as ties with Israel, said Kuri.

“Unlike the US, where support for Israel has stayed relatively stable across administrations thanks to more consolidated institutions and bipartisan consensus, in much of Latin America foreign policy can swing sharply from one election to the next because that institutional buffer doesn’t exist,” Kuri said.

In 2023, Argentina elected right-wing populist Javier Milei as president, who pledged to move the embassy to Jerusalem, refused to recognise a Palestinian state at the UN and said he was “proud to be the most Zionist president in the world.”



In Bolivia, the leftist administration of Evo Morales, who was president from 2006 to 2019, had refused to have full diplomatic ties with Israel. This continued under the presidency of Luis Arce, who joined other regional left-wing leaders in recalling their ambassadors from Israel after October 7, 2023. When Arce was voted out last year, his replacement Rodrigo Paz promptly reversed that policy.

Soon after coming to office this August, Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast undid his leftist predecessor’s actions against Israel as well, appointing an ambassador to Israel who describes himself as a “proud Zionist”.

Over in Honduras, the left-wing government was replaced by a right-wing leader this January. New President Nasry Asfura, the grandson of Palestinian immigrants from Bethlehem, similarly reappointed an ambassador to Israel this year.

In August, Venezuela announced it would restore consular relations with Israel, undoing nearly two decades of an antagonistic stance towards Israel under previous leaders Nicolas Maduro and Hugo Chavez.

Besides deciding where to put their embassies, Latin American governments have also sometimes lent support to legal efforts against Israel over the Gaza war. Mexico, Bolivia, Colombia, Brazil, Chile, Belize, Cuba and Nicaragua are among governments that at one point backed South Africa’s genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice.

Signalling in the Trump era

When Flavio Bolsonaro launched his Brazilian presidential campaign last July, he did so standing beside Argentinian President Milei. Some in the crowd waved Israeli flags and watched as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delivered a video message calling Bolsonaro a friend and a “great champion of the friendship between our peoples”.

Giving foreign leaders such a prominent role in an election campaign is “unheard of in Latin America,” said Alexander Main, Director of International Policy at the Washington-DC-based Center for Economic and Policy Research. “This did not happen before, at least not so overtly.”

Bolsonaro’s campaign, experts say, is seeking to make itself part of a larger political camp that is led in the hemisphere by Trump and internationally includes Israel. Some received direct endorsements from Trump, such as Colombia’s de la Espriella and Honduras’s Asfura.

They’ve joined new right-wing umbrella groups led by the US, such as the Shield of the Americas, a counter-narcotics security alliance bringing together Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guyana, Honduras, Panama, Paraguay, Peru and Trinidad and Tobago. The effort is part of Trump’s policy for the Western Hemisphere that seeks to keep out the influence of other global powers like China.

Members of this Trump-led bloc have helped facilitate controversial US policies to deter migration, such as El Salvador, which is housing third-country deportees for the US. They’ve also chosen to frame their war on narcotics as a new kind of war on terrorism, a zero-sum conflict that is inspired by Israel’s war on the Palestinians, according to Main.



“They find common ground with Israel on a lot of these things,” Main said.

“Before, you had left-wing politicians in these regions that have seen what has happened in Gaza and called that war crimes and human rights abuses,” Main said. “Now you’ve seen, on the other hand, sectors seeing this as an existential fight against a deep-rooted enemy and that merits a kind of war on terror framing.”

Having good relations with Israel could translate into access to key military and security resources as well, Main said, including the use of sophisticated spy software such as Pegasus – which was developed by an Israeli software company – and sales of military jets or training of forces.

Isaac Accords and evangelical lobbying

The rally in August in Brazil that featured Netanyahu’s video message was also an attempt to win support from a large and influential voter bloc there who see protecting Israel as part of their religious worldview.

The Evangelical Parliamentary Front, a caucus of pro-Israel evangelical legislators, includes more than 40% of the Chamber of Deputies and more than a quarter of the Senate. If they formed a party, the loose alliance would become the third-largest in the country.

“Those constituencies have become increasingly politicised in recent years, to the point it is beneficial for politicians to court them and one of the ways they can do that is rallying behind Israel,” Main said.

Brazil is not the only country seeing this evangelical push to build ties with Israel.

“Evangelicalism — particularly Christian Zionism — is a real and growing factor in countries like Honduras and Guatemala,” Kuri said.

Around 40 percent of the population in those countries are evangelicals and both governments have moved their embassies to Jerusalem.

Groups from the US have also been lobbying on Israel’s behalf.

The Latino Coalition for Israel, led by Florida-based evangelical pastor Mario Bramnick, sends delegations throughout Latin America and has met with leaders in Guatemala, El Salvador, Brazil, Panama, Chile, and Costa Rica.

“Our support for Israel is first and foremost rooted in the Bible, where it was clearly established that God gave the Land of Israel, with Jerusalem as its undivided capital, to the Jewish people as an eternal covenant,” the group says on its website. A spokesperson for Bramnick declined to comment for this story.

In 2025, the Genesis Prize – an Israeli nonprofit launched with a $100 million endowment and Israeli government backing – awarded $1m to Argentinian President Milei for his “unequivocal support of Israel during one of the most difficult times since the founding of the Jewish State”.

Milei took the money and established the Isaac Accords, modelling the effort after the Abraham Accords, a Trump-backed effort to restore diplomatic and economic ties between Israel and the Arab world. The initiative gives grant money for pro-Israel civil society groups in Latin America. It also keeps meticulous track of many of the signalling moves right-wing governments are making in recent months to show their new stance on Israel, from moving embassies to Jerusalem to how they vote on Israel-related resolutions in the United Nations.

The initiative’s latest push? At the end of Netanyahu’s trip to the UN General Assembly in late September – where most of the audience walked out of his speech in protest – he and the leaders of Bolivia, Panama and Paraguay held their own summit. The Israeli leader urged them to join the Isaac Accords, writing on X that he sought to “expand the circle of friendship and partnership with Israel”.

World.title: Kenya confirms four more Ebola cases, bringing total to seven
World.content:
⁠Three health workers who ⁠treated the country’s first Ebola patient are among the latest confirmed cases.

Share Kenya confirms four more Ebola cases, bringing total to seven on social media

The Kenyan government says four new patients have tested positive for the Ebola Bundibugyo virus, bringing the total number of confirmed cases in the East African nation to seven.

Three of the new cases were among health workers who treated the country’s first patient, Kenya’s Ministry of Health said in a statement posted on X on Saturday.

The fourth case is a relative of that same patient, who died from the disease, it added.

The relative had been in quarantine since October 6, the ministry said.

This comes a day after Kenya confirmed three cases in the country. The patient identified on Friday was a “primary contact and a close relative of the first and second cases”, the Health Ministry said.

Kenya’s cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), which has recorded more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,300 deaths since it was officially detected in May.

Kenya’s index patient died on October 5 after being ill in the DRC for a month and then flying to Nairobi on October 3. The cases are the first known infections ⁠passed on inside Kenya.

Of the first patient’s 130 contacts, the Health Ministry said 128, or 98.5 percent, had been quarantined – above the global benchmark of 85 percent to break the chain of transmission.

The ministry says it has traced and quarantined nearly all of the first patient’s contacts and there is no evidence that the virus is spreading in the community.

Kenya has reacted quickly by strengthening screening and establishing a hotline for anyone who suspects they may have been in contact with an Ebola patient, but some observers have questioned how the index patient managed to bypass health screenings upon returning to Kenya and make contact with so many people.



Ebola is highly contagious and spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person, including blood and vomit, or through contact with contaminated materials and surfaces, such as bedding and clothing.

The dominant strain in this outbreak is the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are currently no vaccines or treatments. This has complicated efforts to control the spread of the disease.

Research is under way to develop one or more vaccines that work against the strain, and some of these vaccines are already in the early phases of testing in humans.

World.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
World.content:
Donald Trump has blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky deepens.

The sanctions were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by Trump in September.

But the US president issued an executive order on Friday night saying that suspending some was in the US "national interest", prompting a backlash from US lawmakers. Zelensky said it was unfortunate the US has decided to "completely disregard" the sanctions.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv frayed after the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel last week. Ukraine then accused the Trump administration of withdrawing key military support.

Trump and Zelensky have exchanged sharp words about one another. Ukraine's president declared it was nice to be among "real leaders" while addressing an EU summit, after Trump said Zelensky was "more difficult to deal with" than Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The new US sanctions law took aim at Russia's economy, giving Trump broad powers to levy tariffs of up to 100% on imports from the top five purchasers of Russian oil and gas â most significantly China and India.

It also included sanctions against senior Russian figures, including Putin, as well as Russian financial institutions and Moscow's so-called "shadow fleet" of vessels used to circumvent existing embargoes.

World.title: Teacher fought US school attacker before armed dad shot suspect 'multiple times'
World.content:
Some readers may find this article distressing.

A female teacher in the US state of Oregon tackled a teenage shooter who entered her classroom and tried to wrestle the gun from his grasp, police have said.

The teacher, who has not been named, threw her mobile phone before trying to disarm the 16-year-old on the floor of a classroom at Silver Rail Elementary in the city of Bend.

The attacker killed three children and a teacher after shooting his way into the building on Thursday.

He was shot dead by a father with two daughters at the school, who was driving past as the attack started to unfold and, armed with a pistol, ran in to confront the suspect.

Police said the attacker used to be a student at the school. His motive remains unclear.

He had been armed with about 44 more rounds of shotgun ammunition when he was stopped, police said. He fired as many as 15 rounds in the class.

"To the people who showed courage in the face of such violence and intervened to prevent this tragedy from being any worse, we owe you a debt of gratitude," Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said.

Police used a news conference on Friday to identify two of the four victims of the school shooting. They were five-year-old Rhoam Summer and 25-year-old teacher Meghan Lambert.

Lambert's family said in a statement shared by the police that her goal was to be a teacher in the district in which she grew up and that she was "compassionate and had a huge heart".

"She always fought for the underdog and those with special needs," they said.

Bryan Jolly, Summer's grandfather, said the family was devastated by his death.

"The whole thing is senseless, and a shock," he told the New York Times, saying his grandson was "was very bright and very mischievous and very fun-loving, and totally without fear".

The families of the two other students who were killed, an eight-year-old and 11-year-old, did not wish to have them publicly identified yet, police said.

Two others were injured in the attack. Another teacher, a 54-year-old, was still being treated at hospital, and a seven-year-old student, who was in serious but stable condition.

World.title: Three men jailed for 158 years each for murdering Australian and US surfers in Mexico
World.content:
A Mexican judge has sentenced three men convicted of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their US friend Carter Rhoad to 158 years and nine months in jail each.

The Robinsons and Rhoad were killed in an apparent botched robbery of their truck on a secluded beach in Baja California in 2024 while they were on a surfing trip, the court heard during the trial.

The murders sent shockwaves around the world, particularly in Australia, as the area is usually safe from the violence seen in other parts of Mexico.

The guilty verdict was handed down last week. Debra Robinson, the brothers' mother, told the courtroom that her sons' murders had taken "the future we had imagined with them".

The convicted killers' full names were not given for legal reasons, meaning they were only identified as JesÃºs Gerardo, Irineo Francisco and Ãngel JesÃºs.

In November last year, the girlfriend of the alleged ringleader, JesÃºs Gerardo (alias "El Kekas"), was sentenced in a separate trial to 20 years in prison. She had admitted to involvement in the robbery.

The court heard that the bodies of the victims were found dumped down a well with gunshot wounds to their heads.

At the time, the murders shocked locals and tourists in the beach town of Ensenada who were disturbed at the apparent ease and sheer pointlessness of the killings.

Ensenada has a reputation as a welcoming spot for surfers, but the chilling murders revealed how commonplace such extreme violence remains in Mexico.

The only explanation the authorities were able to give was that the surfers - all in their early 30s - had ultimately been murdered for being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Their killings happened barely 36 hours after they crossed into Mexico from the US. Their bodies, however, were not found for another week, when their families were able to identify them.

Local surfers also called for greater security for residents and visiting tourists, citing other recent examples of violence in the state. Tourism is a key part of the regional economy in Baja California.

World.title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms
World.content:
Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off in which the rainforest's future is a key issue.

Left-wing President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon. It had surged under his right-wing predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro.

Lula will face Bolsonaro's son Flavio in the run-off on 25 October, with polls suggesting a neck-and-neck race. Flavio is expected to continue his father's policies if he wins, though he has pledged to fight organised crime in the Amazon.

Satellite data shows that in the year to July 2026, the deforestation rate fell by 41.8% in the Amazon - the biggest drop since records began in 1988. The fall in the Cerrado, Brazil's savanna region, was 23.8%.

The Amazon rainforest - the world's largest - is a crucial buffer in the global fight against climate change and 60% of it is located in Brazil.

World.title: Nursery owner in China jailed for life after hundreds of children poisoned
World.content:
