A nursery owner and five members of her staff have been jailed after they were found to have poisoned more than 200 children with lead-tainted food.

Li Huifang, who operated the Heshi Peixin Kindergarten in Tianshui, in the Gansu province, was sentenced to life in prison for producing and selling toxic and harmful food, according to Chinese state media.

In July 2025, 247 pupils and staff at the nursery were found to have abnormally high blood lead levels after children began falling ill.

A report into the incident found that chefs at Heshi Peixin had used inedible paint to "enhance the look" of its meals to attract more students - despite the paint being being clearly marked as such.

In addition to the sentence, the Lanzhou Intermediate People's Court also ordered the confiscation of 500,000 yuan (Â£56,200; $74,700) of Li's personal assets, state broadcaster CCTV reported.

Nursery executive principal Zhi Jinglin was sentenced to 15 years in prison and fined 300,00 yuan.

Four other members of staff who worked in the nursery's kitchen received sentences of between six to eight years, according to state media.

The court found the four had been instructed by Li and Zhi to add toxic and harmful ingredients to food served to children and staff.

Food samples were later found to contain lead 2,000 times in excess of China's national safety limit.

The investigation into the poisoning began after 235 children from Heshi Peixin nursery had to be treated for lead poisoning after eating steamed red date cakes and sausage corn buns.

Investigators found that the red date cake and the corn sausage rolls had lead levels of 1052mg/kg and 1340mg/kg respectively, both of which far exceed the national food safety standard limit of 0.5mg/kg.

Lead poisoning is "particularly harmful to young children" and can "severely damage the brain and central nervous system", according to the World Health Organization.

Officials later found that dozens of provincial officials and hospital staff attempted to cover up the incident by tampering with blood tests and accepting bribes from a nursery investor.

China has since published a set of national guidelines for the provision of meals on campuses. Among the measures is the requirement for every new batch of food to be tested, and for flour, rice and cooking oil to be purchased from centralised procurement points only.

World.title: Rare pink diamond goes on display in France 100 years after amateur heist
World.content:
A rare pink diamond is going on display in France for the first time since it was stolen almost 100 years ago to the day - the last time it was shown to the public.

The nine-carat, pear-shaped gemstone known as the "Grand CondÃ©" was pilfered in an overnight raid on the ChÃ¢teau de Chantilly in October 1926 and concealed in a hollowed-out apple.

The diamond - one of few royal jewels to survive the French Revolution - was recovered a few weeks later when a hungry maid at the hotel in which the thieves were staying took a bite of the apple.

It will once again be on display in the CondÃ© Museum at the ChÃ¢teau de Chantilly until 3 January.

The museum's director Mathieu Deldicque said that while the apple story may sounds far-fetched, it was widely covered by newspapers at the time.

Deldicque has faced questions about whether the exhibition may be tempting fate, especially given the string of heists on European cultural institutions in the past 12 months, including the daring daylight robbery of jewellery from the Louvre museum in Paris.

While he declined to reveal to CNN how much the diamond was insured for, he noted that extensive academic study into the properties of the diamond had taken place to make it uniquely identifiable.

The results of this analysis, as well as previously unseen archive material about the gem's history and theft, form part of the exhibition, according to the museum.

Naturally occurring pink diamonds are exceptionally rare and often sell for tens of millions of dollars. The highest price ever fetched for one at auction was $71.2m (Â£53.6m) in 2017, according to Sotheby's.

The exact origins of the Grand CondÃ© remain a mystery.

It was first mentioned in 1740 in an inventory of Louis Henri de Bourbon, Prince of CondÃ©, drawn up following his death, the ChÃ¢teau de Chantilly said.

It then became part of the collection of Queen Marie-AmÃ©lie of Bourbon-Sicily, the wife of French King Louis Philippe I, and then her son, Prince Henri of OrlÃ©ans, the Duke of Aumale.

He bequeathed it to the Institut de France, which now owns the ChÃ¢teau de Chantilly, 50km (31 miles) north of Paris, along with thousands of artworks and manuscripts which became the MusÃ©e CondÃ© collection.

World.title: Pope discharged from hospital days after lung cancer surgery
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has been discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital, just four days after an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung.

The 71-year-old walked unaided to his waiting car, stopping to speak to well-wishers.

The Vatican said the Pope will give the traditional Angelus prayer and blessing to a crowd in St Peter's Square on Sunday, as he did last week when he surprised the world by announcing the surgery.

On Friday, photographs were released of the Pope celebrating Mass and distributing communion in hospital for staff.

A statement from his doctors said blood tests and a chest X-ray showed "steady improvement" following his operation.

The surgery on Tuesday, which lasted for 90 minutes, included the removal of the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung. The results of further tests to check for any sign that the cancer has spread have not yet been announced.

The Pope also spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday, in their first call since June 2025. The Vatican said the call was to urge "dialogue and peace".

It came as Russia's bombardment of cities across Ukraine intensifies, with a growing number of civilian casualties and no sign of Putin being ready to halt the invasion.

The Pope also called for a humanitarian ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshkiy, occupied by Russia and under constant shelling, to allow people to be evacuated and for the urgent delivery of food and medicine. The BBC recently reported on residents there being forced to eat garden weeds to survive.

The Pope's schedule has been cleared completely until 20 October, so his reappearance in public so soon is a surprise and will be some relief for Catholics around the world.

Those close to the Pope said he was keen not to delay a trip to Latin America, planned for early November and which includes a visit to Peru, where he was a missionary for many years.

It is not yet clear whether he might be fit to travel or require further treatment.

World.title: Katie Zacharia leaving White House role less than five days into job
World.content:
Katie Zacharia will be leaving her post as White House press secretary, just five days after her shaky public debut.

US President Donald Trump told reporters moments before news of her exit was announced that he had told her "you don't have to do this if you don't want to" and "honestly, if I were you, I'd reconsider".

Zacharia faced heavy criticism for her first press briefing on Tuesday, which lasted less than 15 minutes and included only three questions from reporters.

The 42-year-old spent the days following playing defence, fielding tough questions from news outlets about her credentials and preparedness for the job.

Trump hinted at her impending exit early on Friday afternoon, during an impromptu news conference in front of the Marine One helicopter.

"I said, 'Is this for you, Katie? Because honestly, you don't need this'," Trump said.

"You don't have to be treated this badly," he continued, adding that he believed she had been treated "pretty nastily" by the media.

Hours later, she praised Trump as "kind, wonderful, gracious, thoughtful, enthusiastic, and the most hardworking man" on X, writing that it had been an honour to work for him.

As the November midterm elections, which will decide who controls the US Congress, draw closer, Democrats are seizing on Zacharia's abrupt departure as a sign of failure in the Republican White House.

"The White House Press Secretary is gone. Maga extremists continue to fall apart," the top Democrat in the House of Representatives, Hakeem Jeffries, posted on X.

Zacharia appeared visibly nervous during her inaugural White House press briefing, in which she read talking points from a notebook, answered only a few questions and referred to her husband as the president.

During the briefing, a reporter asked Zacharia - who had been called an attorney by Trump and others and who graduated from Pepperdine University's law school - about where she passed the bar exam. To practise law in the US, an attorney must be admitted to a state's bar association by passing a rigorous exam.

"When I was in China," she replied.

After intense scrutiny and digging by the media, Zacharia admitted on Thursday that she did not pass the bar exam.

She did say in a statement that she had practised international transaction law in China with the "appropriate credentials".

Questions about her legal credentials became a major talking point throughout the week, with Sean Hannity, from conservative-leaning Fox News, lobbing particularly pointed questions at her during an interview on Thursday.

When she said she had not passed the bar, he replied: "Why didn't you just say, 'I never practiced law?'"

Zacharia also described how quickly she had taken on the press secretary role - having been hired less than a week before her debut - prompting him to ask: "Am I hearing that you think the staff should have better prepped you?"

When she appeared on Fox & Friends, which Trump often watches, on Friday, Zacharia faced a similar line of questioning.

She told the show's hosts that she did not disclose to Trump that she was not an attorney because "those questions weren't asked", saying she was hired for a communications role, not a legal one.

Host Lawrence Jones then asked her: "Do you think you still have the confidence of the president?"

She avoided offering a direct answer but ended by saying: "I hope to be able to build the confidence and trust of everyone around me."

Zacharia's early exit is the quickest among Trump's White House press team.

Anthony Scaramucci left his post as White House communications director after only 10 days during Trump's first term.

"Records are made to be broken," Scaramucci wrote on X on Friday. "But I take no pleasure in other people's pain."

Prior to her appointment as press secretary, Zacharia was a frequent fixture on right-wing US networks such as Fox and Newsmax.

She had a brief stint as a spokeswoman at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and worked as a communications adviser for Trump's social media platform Truth Social, according to her LinkedIn.

In her early career, Zacharia worked as an intern for the Republican National Committee and the White House Office of Political Affairs during the Bush administration in 2006.

World.title: Mental health group welcomes Senate move to decriminalise attempted suicide
World.content:
A mental health advocacy group, Nigerian Mental Health (NMH), has welcomed the Senate’s passage of the Suicide Prevention Bill, 2024 (SB 730), seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide in Nigeria.

The bill, sponsored by the senator representing Cross River South Senatorial District, Asuquo Ekpenyong, passed second reading on 13 October 2026 and was referred to the Senate Committees on Health (Secondary and Tertiary) and Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters for further consideration.

NMH and the Nigeria Suicide Prevention Advocacy Working Group (NSPAWG) made their position known in a joint statement shared with PREMIUM TIMES on Friday, calling for inclusive public hearings as the bill progresses.

The organisations urged the Senate committees to allow mental health professionals, civil society organisations, healthcare professionals and people with lived experience to contribute to the legislative process.

Why the bill matters

Under Section 327 of the Criminal Code and Section 231 of the Penal Code, attempted suicide remains a criminal offence, with survivors exposed to the risk of prosecution and imprisonment.

NMH and NSPAWG said criminalisation can discourage people experiencing suicidal distress and their families from seeking timely support.

“A person who survives a suicide attempt should be able to access care without fear of criminal punishment,” the organisations said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The groups cited World Health Organisation (WHO) estimates that Nigeria records more than 15,000 deaths by suicide and roughly 300,000 suicide attempts annually.

The bill’s sponsor, Mr Ekpenyong, said during deliberations, that attempted suicide should be treated as a mental health emergency requiring medical intervention rather than criminal punishment.

What the bill proposes

The proposed legislation seeks to establish a coordinated national framework for suicide prevention, going beyond the removal of criminal penalties for attempted suicide.

It proposes medical assessment, referral, treatment and follow-up support for people who survive suicide attempts, as well as crisis-response services.

The bill also provides for training of relevant professionals and first responders, public education and stronger national data collection.

NMH and NSPAWG said effective implementation would require clear responsibilities, sustainable funding and accountability.

The organisations said the bill’s progress builds on advocacy efforts following the passage of the National Mental Health Act, 2021.

NMH said it launched the #SuicideNotCrimeNG campaign, bringing together more than 40 mental health organisations, professional associations and civil society partners calling for an end to the criminalisation of attempted suicide.

Akpabio’s position

The Senate’s consideration of the bill also featured opposition from Senate President Godswill Akpabio to removing imprisonment as a punishment for attempted suicide.

During the debate, Mr Akpabio argued that removing the penalty could encourage suicide attempts.

“If you attempt suicide, make sure you die. Anyone who attempts and fails will go to jail,” he said.

He also called for adequate input from state Houses of Assembly during the public hearing to avoid conflicts between the proposed legislation and existing laws.

Call for public hearings.

NMH and NSPAWG urged the two Senate committees handling the bill to ensure that the next stage of consideration is informed by evidence, the experiences of affected people and the practical realities of delivering mental health services across Nigeria.

“The Senate has moved the process forward; now it is our turn. This next stage, which opens the door to public hearings, is a meaningful opportunity for people with lived experience, mental health professionals, and civil society to engage and help shape a framework that protects lives and upholds human dignity,” said Chime Asonye, founder of NMH.

The organisations urged Nigerians, health advocates and community leaders to participate by submitting memoranda and supporting the national petition for decriminalisation.

They also renewed their call on the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare to “operationalise and adequately fund the Department of Mental Health Services established under the National Mental Health Act, 2021.”

“The bill’s passage through second reading is progress, but the legislative process is not over. Nigeria needs a legal and service-delivery framework that prioritises prevention, treatment, recovery and the dignity of people experiencing suicidal distress,” NMH noted.

World.title: Gunmen kill four vigilantes in Plateau community
World.content:
Four vigilantes have been killed during an attack on Shurum, a village in the Dorowa Babuje District of Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State.

The vigilantes were attacked by gunmen at about 11:56 p.m. on Friday, according to residents.

A community member, Bulus Bature, said the vigilantes were on duty when the attackers struck.

“They were watching over our community when the gunmen struck and killed them,” Mr Bature said.

He described the killings as painful, noting that the victims had volunteered to protect their community from attacks.

The National Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM), Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the incident.

Mr Tengwong said the association received reports of the attack and confirmed that four people were killed.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He condemned the killings and called on security agencies to investigate the incident and bring the perpetrators to justice.

ALSO READ: Gunmen kill traditional ruler in Plateau

He also urged the government and security agencies to strengthen security in the affected communities, warning that residents should not continue to live in fear while those volunteering to protect them are being targeted.

Efforts to reach the police for confirmation were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report.

The latest killings add to the spate of attacks reported in parts of Plateau State, where communities have repeatedly faced deadly violence.

World.title: Two officers killed as gunmen attack police station in Abia
World.content:
Two police operatives were killed on Saturday in Abia State when gunmen attacked a divisional police headquarters in Aba, the commercial hub of the South-eastern state.

PREMIUM TIMES gathered that the attackers invaded the police facility at about 2 a.m. on Saturday.

Residents told this newspaper that the hoodlums opened fire upon arrival at the station before throwing an improvised explosive devices into the facility which damaged some structures at the station.

They said the attackers also set a police van ablaze and destroyed a Toyota vehicle, a power generator and other valuables in the building.

Police speak

The police spokesperson in Abia State, Maureen Chinaka, confirmed the attack and the killings in a statement on Saturday.

Ms Chinaka, a deputy superintendent of police, said the attack happened at exactly 2:26 a.m. at Urratta-Eziukwu Area, a community in Aba South Local Government Area of the state.

“At about 02:26hrs, the hoodlums attacked the division with explosives, resulting in a fire that damaged part of the building and the divisional patrol van.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Sadly, two senior police officers lost their lives, while three inspectors sustained injuries and are currently receiving medical attention,” she said.

The spokesperson clarified that, contrary to claims, no firearms or ammunition were carted away by the gunmen during the attack.

Ms Chinaka said, in response to the attack, the Commissioner of Police in Abia State, Wilfred Afolabi, has personally led an operational team comprising tactical units of the command to the area.

“The team combed the surrounding environment and restored calm, while intensified security operations and monitoring are ongoing to apprehend the perpetrators,” she said.

The spokesperson said Mr Afolabi has condemned the attack and vowed to track down the attackers.

The commissioner emphasised that the police in the state would deploy all necessary operational and intelligence resources to identify and track down the killers.

The police chief commiserated with the families of the slain operatives.

He urged residents to remain calm, vigilant and to support the police with information that could assist the ongoing investigation.

“Information can be reported at the nearest police station, through the suggestion boxes and contact details of the DPO’s provided at police divisions,” he said, dropping some mobile numbers for residents with information.

First time in long time

The latest attack marks the first such incident is happening in the state in a long time.

Like in other parts of the South-east, attacks by armed persons especially on police facilities had significantly waned in recent years in the region.

The region, before now, witnessed increased attacks often attributed to the outlawed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB).

But IPOB, a group seeking secession of the South-east and South-south from Nigeria, had repeatedly denied its involvement in the attacks.

Recall that a recent PREMIUM TIMES’ special report revealed that attacks and killings have reduced by 50 per cent in the South-east since the arrest and imprisonment of a controversial Biafra agitator, Simon Ekpa, in Finland in 2025.

Meanwhile, no group has claimed responsibility for the latest deadly attack in Abia State.

World.title: Fuel Tanker Fires: Safety expert warns against scooping spilt petrol
World.content:
The President of the Institute of Safety Professionals of Nigeria, Timothy Iwuagwu, has warned Nigerians against scooping spilt fuel at accident scenes, saying a single spark could trigger a deadly explosion.

Mr Iwuagwu also blamed poor tanker design, inadequate inspections and weak enforcement of vehicle safety standards for many of Nigeria’s deadly fuel tanker accidents.

He spoke on Friday during an appearance on Arise News’ News Night, a day after a gas pipeline explosion in Aleto, Eleme Local Government Area of Rivers State.

On Thursday, PREMIUM TIMES also reported that a petrol tanker caught fire in Oluku, Benin City, Edo State, as residents scooped spilt fuel.

Keep away from spills

Mr Iwuagwu said people should stay away from fuel spills and ensure affected areas are cordoned off to keep people from approaching.

“Keep away, keep away,” he said, warning that people who rush to collect spilt petroleum products often underestimate the danger.

“Scooping the material that has spilt is the most foolhardy of all decisions,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He explained that fuel vapour could ignite when it comes into contact with an ignition source, even from a considerable distance.

“An explosion could occur from even an electrostatic source or a spark,” he said.

He added that fuel vapour could travel away from the leak point before igniting and triggering a fire at the source.

The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) said 411 people died in 2024 while scooping fuel from crash sites, accounting for about 7.6 per cent of road deaths recorded that year.

A separate study covering January 2009 to October 2024 documented 169 tanker fire and explosion incidents that killed 1,613 people.

Poor tanker design

When he was asked about root causes of tanker accidents, Mr Iwuagwu pointed to the design and configuration of the vehicles.

He said tankers should be built to prevent leaks, even when they overturn.

“Not a drop of the liquid content is expected to leak out of that truck, by its very design and configuration,” he said.

He explained that tankers should have internal baffles to reduce liquid movement inside the tank, particularly when the vehicle travels on uneven roads.

He also identified suspension systems, steering mechanisms and tyre pressure as important safety considerations, warning that uneven tyre pressure could destabilise a loaded tanker.

Inadequate inspections

Mr Iwuagwu said many tankers are imported and cleared through the country’s ports without adequate scrutiny of their safety features.

He said safety professionals were rarely involved in the inspection process and called for imported tankers to be thoroughly examined and certified before they are released for use.

“We hardly have the presence of safety professionals in such places,” he said.

He also criticised some companies for resisting safety inspections.

“A lot of companies are even reluctant to allow safety professionals to look into some of these conveyances,” he said.

He said Nigeria had failed to adequately address the problem of tankers with different designs and configurations entering the country and being deployed on its roads.

Mr Iwuagwu also faulted road safety and vehicle inspection officers, saying they often focus more on vehicle documents than on the mechanical condition of the vehicles.

He recalled an encounter with a loaded truck near Terminal 2 of the Murtala Muhammed Airport in Lagos, where he noticed that the wheel nuts were loose.

“The wheel nuts were all slack and falling off,” he said, adding that he overtook the truck and forced the driver to stop.

Rail transport as an alternative

Mr Iwuagwu called for greater use of rail transport to move petroleum products, arguing it would reduce the risks of transporting highly flammable materials on roads.

“The best way to move these things is by rail,” he said.

He also identified pipelines as an option but stressed that they must be properly maintained to prevent leaks and explosions.

He said transporting petroleum products by rail would help keep them away from road users and communities exposed to tanker accidents.

Aleto pipeline explosion

Residents of Aleto have called for the replacement of the gas pipeline involved in Thursday’s explosion, rather than repairs limited to the ruptured section.

They alleged that the pipeline had been leaking for about three weeks before the explosion.

In a report by Arise News, the president of the Aleto Community Youths, whose name was not provided, said no representative of the pipeline operator had arrived at the scene by midday on Friday.

“They need to do a proper rehabilitation,” he said. “Remove all the pipes and replace them with another one, not to endanger our lives here.”

Another resident said the community had notified the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) about the leak, but that no substantial action had been taken.

“They informed NNPC; they came and put caution tape. For over three weeks now, they did nothing,” the resident said.

A safety engineer also urged NNPC to inspect its pipelines, noting that many had been laid decades ago.

“Most of these pipelines were laid 30-40 years ago,” the engineer said.

NNPC Limited confirmed the incident on Friday, saying the affected pipeline belonged to its subsidiary, NNPC Gas Infrastructure Company Limited.

READ ALSO: Sokoto disburses N143 million to victims of fire incidents

The company said it had isolated the affected section and activated its emergency response procedures. It added that investigations were underway to establish the cause and full extent of the incident.

Reports said at least 20 people were injured and more than 50 houses were destroyed in the explosion. No deaths had been independently confirmed in the reports available at the time.

A team from the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) was also at the scene and promised a joint investigation.

In Edo State, casualty figures following the Oluku tanker fire remain unclear. The police confirmed that eight people sustained burn injuries, while other reports said four people were feared dead.

World.title: How more Nigerian-born players are switching to represent other African countries
World.content:
When Akpan Udoh helped Nigeria win the FIFA Under-17 World Cup in Chile in 2015, his future appeared tied to the country whose colours he wore alongside future Super Eagles stars Victor Osimhen and Samuel Chukwueze.

More than a decade later, the former Golden Eaglets goalkeeper is pursuing an international career with Uganda, a country to which he has a family connection.

Udoh made his international debut for Uganda on 2 October, keeping a clean sheet in a 2-0 friendly victory over the Democratic Republic of Congo.

His journey reflects a growing trend in African football, where national teams are looking beyond their borders for players who qualify through ancestry or naturalisation.

From Uganda and Malawi to Sudan and Benin Republic, several footballers born in Nigeria or with Nigerian heritage have found opportunities to represent other African countries. Their experiences vary, ranging from players who developed their careers abroad to those whose family ties have opened the door to international football.

Uganda’s search for heritage players

The Federation of Uganda Football Associations (FUFA) announced on 27 September that Udoh and Kingdom Osayi were among nine players identified through its national team recruitment programme.

The initiative followed a scouting exercise involving more than 200 potential heritage players, with 20 identified for further consideration.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Udoh, born on 18 July 1999, was part of Nigeria’s 2015 Under-17 World Cup-winning squad. He qualifies to represent Uganda through his grandmother, Auma, who was born in Busia, according to information published about his recruitment.

Osayi, born on 3 June 2004 to Nigerian parents, qualifies through his maternal grandmother, who was born in Kaberamaido, Uganda.

Before his move to Swedish club Assyriska FF, Udoh played for several Nigerian clubs, including Heartland, MFM, Doma United and Rangers International.

Osayi, meanwhile, had been involved with Nigeria’s Under-23 team setup but was not fielded at the 2019 U-23 Africa Cup of Nations. Having not represented Nigeria in a match at that tournament, his path to Uganda differed from that of players who have already featured for another national team.

Both players’ recruitment reflects Uganda’s efforts to widen its pool of available talent ahead of international assignments, including the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign.

For Udoh, the transition is particularly striking because he previously represented Nigeria at youth level. His Uganda debut has now taken his career into senior international football with another country.

Malawi’s Nigerian connection

Malawi offers another example of how footballers with Nigerian connections are finding international opportunities elsewhere in Africa.

Jubril Okedina, a defender who developed in English football, attracted discussion about a possible future with Nigeria’s youth teams. He ultimately committed his senior international career to Malawi, receiving his first senior call-up and making his debut in March 2024.

Forward Babatunde Adepoju followed a different route.

Born and raised in Lagos, Adepoju built his professional career in southern Africa, particularly Malawi, where he played for clubs including Blue Eagles, Masters Security, Mighty Wanderers and FCB Nyasa Big Bullets.

After spending several years in the country, he obtained Malawian citizenship through naturalisation. He has also expressed a desire to give back to the country that helped develop his football career.

His international breakthrough came when he received his first call-up for Malawi’s 2026 FIFA World Cup qualifying campaign. He subsequently featured for the Flames in their competitive fixtures and contributed to the team’s Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign.

For Malawi, both players provide additional options, illustrating how national teams can strengthen their squads by recruiting eligible players with connections to other countries.

Adetunji’s move to Sudan

Former Nigerian international Sunday Adetunji’s career took another turn in 2026 when he switched his international allegiance to Sudan after establishing himself in the country’s domestic game with Al-Hilal Omdurman.

The forward previously played for several Nigerian clubs, including Abia Warriors, Plateau United and Rivers United.

Adetunji had made one senior appearance for Nigeria, coming on as a substitute in a 4-0 friendly defeat to Mexico on 4 July 2021.

His subsequent career took him to North Macedonia and Serbia before he moved to Sudan. His spell with KF Shkupi in North Macedonia was particularly productive: he scored 20 league goals in his debut season and helped the club win its first league title.

His limited senior involvement with Nigeria is relevant to his change of association. FIFA permits certain players to change the national association they represent, but the process is subject to conditions involving nationality, previous international appearances, age and participation in major competitions.

A player cannot switch national teams simply because he has changed clubs or obtained another passport. He must satisfy the applicable eligibility criteria and secure formal approval where required.

Adetunji’s case illustrates how a player’s international prospects can change after club football takes him to another country, where he may establish the legal and sporting connection required to represent its national team.

Benin Republic: Family heritage and international opportunity

Benin Republic has a longer history of fielding footballers with Nigerian connections, reflecting the close geographical, cultural and family ties between the neighbouring countries.

Among the players who illustrate this relationship are Junior Olaitan, Tosin Aiyegun and emerging forward Joseph Ede Oloko.

Olaitan was born in Porto-Novo, Benin, to a Nigerian father and a Beninese mother. He spent much of his formative years in Lagos before returning to Benin to join Ayema FC in Porto-Novo.

His performances helped him earn a senior debut for Benin in 2021 and a move to French club Niort in 2022.

“I started in Lagos, then I returned to Benin, where I started with Ayema FC,” he told So Foot.

Olaitan’s story illustrates how family heritage and formative experiences in two countries can shape a player’s career before he reaches senior international football.

Aiyegun was born in Lagos to a Nigerian father and a Beninese mother. He began his professional career in Latvia with FK Ventspils, where he made 89 appearances, scoring 35 goals and providing 20 assists, before moving to FC Zürich and later Lorient.

He chose to represent Benin at senior level in 2022 and started all four of the team’s matches at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations, including its round-of-16 defeat to Egypt.

Oloko is among the more recent Nigerian-born players to earn an opportunity with Benin.

Born in Lagos, the striker developed with 36 Lion FC before moving to AS Cotonou in Benin and subsequently to Europe.

His performances for Latvian club Liepāja in 2026 earned him a first senior call-up from Benin coach Gernot Rohr in September.

Oloko has a Nigerian background through his birthplace and a Beninese connection through his mother, giving him links to both countries.

“My mother is Beninese, so I have always had that link with Benin. I also have Nigerian roots, and I am proud of both sides of my identity,” he told Joueurs Béninois.

His comments offer a personal explanation for such decisions. Rather than presenting his choice as a rejection of Nigeria, Oloko described an identity that encompasses both countries.

The choice is not always about opportunity

The movement of players between national teams also works in the opposite direction. Nigeria has benefited from footballers who developed abroad and chose to represent the Super Eagles.

Among the players who have recently pursued this route is Felix Agu, the German-born defender who received clearance to represent Nigeria in 2025 after previously playing for Germany’s Under-21 team in friendly matches.

George Ilenikhena, born in Lagos and raised in France from the age of three, also featured for France’s youth teams, beginning with the Under-16s in 2021.

Ilenikhena subsequently switched his international allegiance to Nigeria and made a scoring debut for the Super Eagles in Uyo in their first match of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers on 25 September.

These cases show how international football brings together players shaped by different development systems, provided they satisfy the relevant eligibility rules.

However, dual nationality does not guarantee that a player will choose the country with the more prominent footballing history or greater international profile.

South African defender Ime Okon, who has a Nigerian father and a South African mother, has made his commitment to Bafana Bafana clear.

Born and raised in South Africa, Okon came through the country’s football system, including SuperSport United, before joining German club Hannover 96. He made his Bafana Bafana debut against Mozambique at the 2025 COSAFA Cup and scored his first international goal against Zimbabwe three days later.

Despite being eligible for Nigeria through his father, he has maintained that his football identity is rooted in South Africa.

“I know where my heart lies,” he said.

Okon’s position challenges the assumption that players with dual nationality will automatically choose Nigeria because of the Super Eagles’ reputation or the country’s large football-playing population.

Upbringing, personal identity and emotional attachment can be as important as professional opportunity. While some players identify more closely with the country where they grew up, others may place greater emphasis on family heritage or the opportunity to represent a national team.

Their motivations differ, and their choices should not be treated as interchangeable.

What FIFA’s rules permit

FIFA’s eligibility regulations determine who may represent a national team and under what circumstances a player can change the country they represent. The rules distinguish between possessing a country’s nationality and meeting the additional requirements to play for its national team.

Under FIFA’s Regulations Governing the Application of the Statutes, a player must hold the relevant nationality. Depending on the circumstances, the player must also establish a recognised connection to the country through birthplace, the birthplace of a biological parent or grandparent, or a prescribed period of residence.

For players who have never represented a country in an official competition, the requirements differ from those governing players who have already played for another national association.

Where a player has acquired a new nationality, for instance, FIFA’s rules generally require a qualifying connection through birth, descent or residence. The qualifying residence period depends on the age at which the player moved to the country.

A player who has represented another country in an official competition may need formal approval from FIFA to change association. Such a change is not automatic and depends on the player’s international record, nationality and the specific conditions set out in Article 10 of the regulations.

FIFA also distinguishes between official competitions and friendly matches. Participation in an official competition can tie a player to a national association even at youth level, provided the player has physically taken part in the match. A friendly appearance, by contrast, does not by itself create that restriction.

Some players who have represented a country at senior international level may still qualify to change association, but only under specific conditions. These include provisions covering players with dual or multiple nationality who have made limited senior appearances, as well as other narrowly defined circumstances.

The applicable requirements can include age limits, the timing of nationality acquisition, the number of appearances and the period since the player’s last senior international match.

The rules therefore do not give players an unrestricted right to switch national teams simply because they have obtained another passport or moved abroad to play club football. Each case depends on the player’s nationality, international history and the applicable eligibility provisions, with formal approval required where stipulated by FIFA.

Is Nigeria losing talent?

The recruitment of Nigerian-origin players by other African countries raises questions about whether Nigeria is losing footballers who could have strengthened its own national teams.

Sports analyst Seun Anifowose feels indifferent, instead, he believes Nigeria should focus on making the best use of the talent available rather than trying to prevent players from representing other countries.

“The major task for football authorities is to provide an enabling environment that would allow for local talents to be discovered and nurtured into stardom,” Mr Anifowose told PREMIUM TIMES.

He added: “If we have the right system in place, anyone that is deserving of a place in the national team will not be denied or hampered on any grounds, including ethnicity, religion or having a godfather. Those that are not good enough can take their skills elsewhere depending on what the guiding FIFA rules state.”

Football agent Friday Onajafe noted in an interview with PREMIUM TIMES that for a country with a large football-playing population and a history of producing international talent like Nigeria, effective scouting and communication with players abroad remain important.

He said: “Domestic competitions and youth development structures must provide credible pathways into the national teams.

“The question is not whether Nigeria can or should prevent players from representing other countries. Where players qualify for another national team and meet FIFA’s requirements, their choices must be respected.

“Rather, Nigeria must ensure that its football structures are organised enough to identify talent, maintain contact with eligible players and offer meaningful opportunities to those who wish to represent the country,” Mr Onajafe concluded.

As more African federations look beyond their borders, Nigeria’s challenge is to develop its own players while recognising that competition for international talent now extends well beyond the traditional boundaries of national development systems.

World.title: Dial *315# before buying phones, NCC tells Nigerians
World.content:
The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) has urged Nigerians to verify their phones using the code *315# before paying for them, warning that unverified devices could be counterfeit or substandard.

The commission’s Director of Technical Standards and Network Integrity, Edoyemi Ogoh, said the verification process would protect consumers from buying fake devices and help prevent substandard handsets from affecting network service quality for other users.

“Before you buy a phone, dial *315# and confirm that the phone is fully verified before you pay,” Mr Ogoh said.

He spoke on Friday during an interview on News Night on Arise News, explaining the NCC’s new Device Checker, which took effect on 7 October.

Why the NCC introduced the check

Mr Ogoh gave three reasons for the verification process: compliance with the law, consumer protection and improved service quality.

He said the Nigerian Communications Act 2003 requires telecommunications equipment to undergo type approval to ensure it meets the country’s standards.

“The whole intent of that is to ensure that every device coming into the country is genuine and works the way it should work,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The second reason, he said, is to protect consumers from paying for counterfeit or imitation products.

“When you’re spending your hard-earned money buying a particular device, you want to be sure that the device you’re buying is actually the genuine device,” he said.

“You’re not paying over the odds for a device that is fake or an imitation of the real thing.”

The third reason is service quality. According to Mr Ogoh, the NCC’s assessments found that a significant proportion of complaints about network service were linked to the devices consumers used.

“We knew that we had to do something very important, in line with the statutory requirement, protecting the consumers, as well as ensuring that quality of service is assured for every user,” he said.

He stressed that the effects of using unapproved devices could extend beyond their owners to other subscribers in the same environment.

“When consumers use devices that are not type approved, it does not just impact them, it also impacts others within the same environment,” he said.

“We’ve seen scenarios where a subscriber was having a quality of service issue, and it was actually attributable to the device the person was using.”

A failed check does not necessarily mean a phone is fake

Mr Ogoh said a phone’s failure to pass the Device Checker does not automatically mean it is counterfeit.

“Not necessarily,” he said when asked whether a failed check meant a device was fake.

He explained that the process involves two stages: type approval of a phone model and verification of each individual device.

Type approval involves laboratory tests to establish whether a phone model meets Nigerian standards and can function properly on service providers’ networks.

“Once that phone is switched on, it can connect to the service provider’s networks and can actually talk properly,” he said, adding that the approval is conducted once for each model.

The second stage involves verifying individual units of an approved model.

“Someone can type approve a particular model, and about 100,000 units of that model can be brought into the country,” he said.

“So each particular unit is now meant to be assured.”

Mr Ogoh said importers and other parties responsible for bringing devices into the country must register their International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) numbers on the NCC’s system.

“It’s only when that process is done that we can say the full end-to-end process for verification is completed,” he said.

He said importers, manufacturers and vendors were responsible for completing the process, not buyers.

“It’s not for buyers to carry it out,” he said.

What about phones bought before 7 October?

Mr Ogoh said owners of phones that were already active on Nigerian networks before 7 October do not need to take any action.

“Every single device that was active on the networks at midnight on October 6th was fully onboarded and verified,” he said.

“We had about 231 million devices. So they are verified.”

The enhanced verification process applies to devices arriving in the country from 7 October, he said. Such devices must be checked for type approval and registered on the Device Checker system.

Mr Ogoh also said phones identified as cloned before the new system took effect would not be blocked under the new process.

“Prior to October 7, the device checker was not in place in terms of requiring Nigerians to check before they buy,” he said.

“We’re not going to punish them to say, ‘You bought something fake, take it out.’ So those phones are fine.”

He did not explain what action the commission would take against a newly imported device confirmed to be cloned. He urged prospective buyers to check a device’s verification status before making payment.

NCC addresses privacy concerns

Addressing concerns about privacy, Mr Ogoh said the Device Checker uses only a phone’s IMEI to establish its verification status.

“We don’t know that a particular device belongs to you from you dialling that, because the only information that is utilised is just the IMEI,” he said.

“We don’t have access to your communications. We don’t know your contacts, your messages or anything that you stored.”

He said the system was designed solely to establish whether a device was genuine and properly verified.

“It’s purely to verify the genuineness or otherwise of the device,” he said.

According to him, a verified phone is genuine and should function as designed.

“You are not going to get surprises,” he said.

Consumers can dial *315# to check a phone’s verification status. The NCC’s consumer complaint line is 622.

The commission has also warned consumers to use only the official *315# code and its website for device verification. It cautioned them against sharing one-time passwords or verification codes with sellers or callers.

World.title: PT HEALTH WATCH: What pregnant women should know about bloating, warning signs
World.content:
Bloating, a feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen, is common during pregnancy because hormonal changes slow digestion, increasing the likelihood of gas and constipation.

Although often harmless, persistent or unusual abdominal discomfort, particularly when accompanied by severe pain, vomiting, fever or vaginal bleeding, may indicate a condition requiring medical attention.

To explain the causes, management and warning signs of pregnancy-related bloating, PREMIUM TIMES spoke with Halimat Jimoh, a midwife, who also cautioned against self-medication.

Why bloating occurs during pregnancy

Ms Jimoh said bloating could occur at any stage of pregnancy, although some women experience it more during the first trimester because of hormonal changes.

She explained that increased progesterone levels relax the muscles of the digestive tract, slowing the movement of food through the intestines. This can cause gas accumulation, constipation and abdominal discomfort.

As pregnancy advances, the growing uterus may also put pressure on digestive organs.

According to her, pregnancy-related bloating is generally mild, may come and go, and can improve after passing gas or having a bowel movement.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

However, she advised women not to assume that every episode of abdominal discomfort is a normal pregnancy symptom.

Warning signs women should not ignore

Ms Jimoh said severe or persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, fever and vaginal bleeding should prompt medical assessment.

She noted that conditions such as gastrointestinal infections, appendicitis, gallbladder problems and intestinal obstruction could cause abdominal discomfort and swelling.

Severe upper abdominal pain, particularly on the right side, accompanied by a severe headache, changes in vision or sudden swelling of the face and hands, could indicate pre-eclampsia, a potentially serious pregnancy complication.

Other warning signs include difficulty breathing, fainting and a significant deterioration in the woman’s general condition.

She also advised women to seek immediate assessment if they notice reduced or absent fetal movements after their baby’s movements have become established.

Managing bloating safely

According to Ms Jimoh, fizzy drinks, beans and other gas-producing foods may worsen bloating in some women, while large meals and very fatty foods may increase digestive discomfort.

She recommended eating smaller, more frequent meals, eating slowly and drinking enough water. Gentle physical activity, such as walking, may also support digestion and relieve constipation.

For women experiencing constipation, she advised increasing fibre intake through fruits, vegetables and whole grains, while ensuring adequate fluid consumption.

However, she encouraged women to identify their individual food triggers rather than unnecessarily eliminating entire food groups from their diets.

Dangers of self-medication

Ms Jimoh warned against taking medicines or herbal preparations for bloating without consulting a qualified healthcare professional.

She explained that over-the-counter medicines are not automatically safe during pregnancy, as their suitability may depend on the stage of pregnancy and the woman’s individual circumstances.

She added that products described as natural are not necessarily safe, particularly when their ingredients have not been adequately studied in pregnancy or may interact with other medicines.

The midwife advised women to disclose their stage of pregnancy, medications and supplements to their healthcare providers before taking anything for persistent bloating or constipation.

She also cautioned that self-medication could mask symptoms of an underlying condition requiring treatment.

When to seek medical care

Ms Jimoh urged pregnant women to seek urgent medical attention when bloating occurs alongside severe or persistent abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, vaginal bleeding, fever, fainting or difficulty breathing.

Sudden swelling of the face or hands, severe headache, visual disturbances and severe upper abdominal pain also require prompt assessment because they may indicate pre-eclampsia.

She reiterated that reduced or absent fetal movements warrant immediate assessment.

According to her, persistent, severe or unusual symptoms should be investigated rather than simply treated as digestive discomfort.

She encouraged women to seek professional advice whenever they are unsure whether a symptom is normal, stressing that timely assessment can help identify complications and prevent delays in care.

World.title: Osinbajo’s spokesperson rejects ex-SGF Babachir Lawal’s claims about ex-VP
World.content:
Laolu Akande, erstwhile spokesperson for former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo, has rejected allegations by the former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Babachir Lawal, about Mr Osinbajo’s relationship with former President Muhammadu Buhari and the composition of his (Osinbajo’s) office.

Mr Akande, who served as Senior Special Assistant to the Vice President on Media and Publicity from 2015 to 2023, said he was responding because he was part of the Office of the Vice President and witnessed several of the decisions Mr Lawal referred to.

Mr Osinbajo contested the APC presidential primary in June 2022 but lost to Mr Bola Tinubu, who eventually became the party’s presidential candidate.

Mr Lawal had alleged, among other things, that Mr Buhari considered Mr Osinbajo’s decision to seek the presidency in 2022 “immoral,” and that the former vice president had submitted a memo containing more than 20 names of proposed staff which was allegedly delayed by the president’s chief of staff.

Mr Akande rejected both claims.

In a statement titled, “A response to Babachir Lawal’s falsehoods against Yemi Osinbajo, SAN, GCON,” Mr Akande described Mr Lawal’s claims as “a string of allegations”. He said the former SGF’s account contained fabrications that needed to be corrected.

“Ordinarily, such fabrications would not deserve a response. But I served as the vice president’s spokesperson. I was in the room where many of these decisions were taken,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Buhari supported Osinbajo’s 2022 ambition — Akande

According to Mr Akande, the claim that Mr Buhari considered Mr Osinbajo’s presidential ambition immoral was false.

He said the former president personally offered to support Mr Osinbajo’s political ambition on at least four occasions.

“President Buhari personally offered to support the vice president, telling him plainly: ‘If I don’t support you, who will I support?’” Mr Akande said.

He also recalled an incident during the 2022 APC presidential primary campaign when Mr Buhari praised Mr Osinbajo at a Federal Executive Council meeting for conducting what he described as a dignified and issues-based campaign.

Mr Akande said the president’s comments were made in the presence of members of the council.

“That is not a president who found Osinbajo’s ambition distasteful. That is a president who broached it, encouraged and applauded it,” he said.

Akande denies existence of 20-name memo

Mr Akande also rejected Mr Lawal’s account of a memo allegedly containing the names of more than 20 staff members proposed by Mr Osinbajo.

He described the claim that the memo was delayed by the Chief of Staff to the President and subsequently taken to Mr Buhari by Mr Lawal as “a complete fabrication”.

“There was no such memo,” he said.

Mr Akande also disputed the claim that Mr Buhari made an ethnic remark about the proposed staff, saying such conduct was inconsistent with the former president.

He explained that Mr Osinbajo had direct access to Mr Buhari and ordinarily took his memos directly to the president for approval.

According to him, once approved, the memos were passed to Mr Osinbajo’s Chief of Staff, Ade Ipaye, who communicated them to the relevant agencies for implementation.

He said the SGF’s office was not involved in that process except at the stage of issuing appointment letters to staff.

Mr Akande also challenged Mr Lawal’s claim that the alleged memo had been delayed for three months.

“I resumed in the Office of the Vice President in June 2015, alongside several other colleagues. So did many of those whose names he now invents. There was no three-month delay,” he said.

He said the process involved different batches of memos submitted by Mr Osinbajo at different times as the office was being established and government policies evolved.

He said no single list of staff appointments was based on ethnic or religious considerations.

‘Osinbajo’s office was pan-Nigerian’

Mr Akande further rejected Mr Lawal’s allegation that Mr Osinbajo staffed his office largely with members of his church.

He described the claim as false, saying the office’s composition showed otherwise.

“The Office was one of the most inclusive, pan-Nigerian offices in that government — North, South, East, West, Christian, and Muslim,” he said.

He cited the appointment of Mr Ipaye, a Muslim lawyer, as deputy chief of staff to the vice president as evidence of the office’s religious diversity.

Mr Akande also said three of Mr Osinbajo’s four special advisers were Muslims, including Maryam Uwais, who served as special adviser on Social Investments, and Ahmad Zakari.

He argued that the staff composition contradicted the claim that Mr Osinbajo operated a narrow religious agenda.

Mr Akande said his response was intended to place the disputed claims on record, stressing that he had firsthand knowledge of the workings of the Vice-President’s office during the period under review.

“It is quite simply incredible that Mr Lawal would create such falsehood,” he said.

World.title: Nigeria’s economy needs continuation of Tinubu’s reforms – Wike
World.content:
Photo: NAN

The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says Nigeria’s full economic recovery depends entirely on sustaining the bold reform policies initiated by President Bola Tinubu.

Wike said this on Saturday, at the Rainbow Coalition’s stakeholders’ consultation in Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area of Rivers.

He said that only the continuation of the current administration’s economic direction could permanently pull the country back from the brink of collapse.

He noted that the hard economic choices being implemented presently were necessary remedies to salvage a system that was virtually “dead” when Tinubu took office.

“Only the continuation of the economic reforms initiated by the Tinubu government can bring this country back from the economic comatose it was in before this present administration took over,” he said.

He said that the presidential candidate of the Africa Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Abubakar Atiku and his vice, Rotimi Amaechi, had nothing to offer to Nigerians.

The minister urged residents of the state not to surrender the country’s progress to “career politicians” and “political opportunists” whom he likened to “chronic pool betters” who repeatedly gamble with public trust.

According to him, supporting politicians who have made decades-long pursuits for power would mean diverting national funds to recoup lost campaign expenses rather than consolidating economic gains.

Wike further said that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, would not make any meaningful difference if elected, stressing that Tinubu was the person who had shown true commitment.

Reaffirming that leadership must be judged by past governance records, the former Rivers governor challenged his predecessor to account for major capital allocations in Rivers.

Explaining the political strategy behind the cross-party Rainbow Coalition movement, he said that delivering economic recovery required total alignment between the executive and the national assembly.

He urged voters to support Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates vying for the Senate and House of Representatives seats in the area to ensure legislative cooperation for the president’s economic policy agenda.

He also called on party leaders and community mobilisers to prepare for an overwhelming turnout on election day.

“I want total mobilisation on Jan. 16, 2027. Everybody must be mobilised. Make sure we vote and win decisively to protect our collective future,” he said.

In his remarks, the Executive Chairman of the council, Dr Chukwu Shedrack, commended Wike for his historic development projects in the council, including road construction, hospital upgrades, and human capital investments.

Shedrack highlighted several local governance achievements which he said aligned with the FCT minister’s leadership model.

Reaffirming the council’s political commitment to the Tinubu administration’s economic recovery drive, he pledged a complete block vote for the APC across all elective positions come 2027.

“We are fully mobilised, ward by ward and unit by unit. Come the 2027 general elections, our people will deliver 100 per cent. From president to national assembly and house of assembly, no vote will drop,” Shedrack assured. (NAN)

World.title: Troops rescue 27 abducted residents in Katsina Forest
World.content:
By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina

KATSINA — Troops of the Nigerian Army, working with local hunters and the Community Watch Corps, have rescued 27 residents abducted by armed bandits during an attack on Gamji village in Sabuwa Local Government Area of Katsina State.

The attack, which occurred on Friday, also claimed the life of a 70-year-old resident, Alhaji Saleh Kasim, while six cows were reportedly rustled.

The Katsina State Ministry of Internal Security and Home Affairs disclosed this in a statement issued on Saturday, October 17, 2026.

According to the statement, signed by the state Commissioner for Internal Security and Home Affairs, Dr Nasir Mu’azu, about 40 armed bandits, reportedly led by a gang leader identified as Kachalla Alhaji Bawa Kabir, invaded the community in the early hours of October 16 on 20 motorcycles.

The attackers abducted 27 residents, comprising mainly women, children and elderly people, and killed Kasim during the raid.

The ministry said security forces launched a coordinated operation after receiving intelligence about the attack.

Troops of the 17 Brigade mobilised alongside local hunters and members of the Community Watch Corps to pursue the fleeing attackers and secure the release of the victims.

The joint security team reportedly blocked escape routes towards the Madaci forest enclave to prevent the bandits from moving the abducted residents deeper into the forest.

The operation culminated at about 6pm on Friday when troops engaged the suspected bandits at Tashar Bawa forest and rescued all 27 victims, according to the statement.

The rescued residents were subsequently taken to the Machika Military Forward Operating Base for medical attention and other necessary care.

The ministry added that joint security teams had commenced clearance operations to track down suspected members of the gang who escaped the encounter.

The operations are also aimed at preventing possible reprisal attacks and protecting Gamji and neighbouring communities from further threats.

Mu’azu commended the troops of the 17 Brigade, local hunters and the Community Watch Corps for their prompt response, courage and cooperation, which he said contributed to the successful rescue.

He reaffirmed the commitment of the Katsina State Government, under Governor Dikko Umaru Radda, to protecting lives and property and intensifying security operations in communities affected by criminal activities.

World.title: Defend Tinubu’s reforms with facts – Shettima tells APC think tank
World.content:
VP Shettima

— Says North has spoken with loud voice, unmistakable conviction, unveils Arewa for Asiwaju campaign office*

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA –The Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, has said the growing Northern support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election is not a blank check, and the administration will earn it through facts, radical transparency and measurable results.

Speaking directly to the political stakes, he maintained that expanding loyalty in the region demands greater accountability, and an honest dialogue with citizens about ongoing reforms undertaken by the Tinubu administration.

Senator Shettima, who spoke on Saturday in Abuja when he unveiled the Arewa for Asiwaju Campaign Head Office and formally inaugurated the campaign structure of the northern think tank, expressed a firm belief that the North has spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction in its support for the President.

According to him, renewed political confidence should never be taken for granted, as the government and its supporters must continue to engage Nigerians on the basis of facts and demonstrate how the ongoing reforms are improving security, livelihoods, and economic opportunity.

“By now, I believe the North has spoken. We have spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction. From Adamawa to Zamfara, from Borno to Niger, we have spoken. Such confidence places an obligation upon us that no officeholder should ever underestimate,” he stated.

The Vice President noted that President Tinubu’s bid for a renewed mandate must rest on the administration’s record and a clear account of how another term would advance the interests of Nigerians.

He restated that the north had nothing to be afraid of in President Tinubu second term and Nigeria’s leaders.

“The mandate belongs to the people. We must account for its use and explain how another term would advance their interests,” he said.

Shettima acknowledged that Nigerians have endured difficult economic adjustments, warning campaigners against dismissing genuine concerns or relying on political slogans to defend government policies.

“Our citizens have endured difficult adjustments. We cannot pretend otherwise. What we owe them is an honest account of the decisions taken, the gains achieved and the difficulties that persist. We lose our hearing when applause becomes our only source of information,” he added.

The Vice President said the concerns of traders facing higher costs, graduates searching for work and families struggling with daily expenses must remain central to government decision-making.

“A failed policy enters somebody’s home as a missed meal, an unpaid school fee or an opportunity lost,” he said.

He also defended criticism as essential to democratic governance, saying the administration must remain open to useful ideas irrespective of political affiliation, ethnicity, religion or region.

“There is no democracy without critics. Progress demands that our assumptions endure the examination of those who disagree with us,” VP Shettima said.

He urged the Arewa for Asiwaju campaign structure to serve not merely as an election platform but as a channel through which concerns from communities can reach those in authority.

“A complaint should travel from a community to those who can act upon it. The people who speak through this organisation deserve to know that somebody is listening,” he said.

The Vice President said the administration’s priorities remains security, economic opportunity, poverty reduction, education and stronger public institutions.

“The farmer should be able to cultivate in safety. A child’s education should prepare that child for a productive life. Public institutions should give citizens confidence that effort can yield opportunity,” he said.

The VP added that while elections create a deadline for political persuasion, the obligations of government continue beyond campaign periods.

“Even as elections impose a deadline upon persuasion, public service imposes no deadline upon our duty,” he said.

Earlier, Deputy Senate President, Barau Jibrin, stated that the inauguration of the A4A structure for the 2027 presidential elections comes at a time when the region requires a strong, trusted platform to mobilize support for President Tinubu.

He expressed confidence that the A4A structure in the northern region would help in telling the accurate story of President Tinubu’s transformational strides.

For his part, National Chairman of the APC, Prof. Nentanwe Yilwatda, moved a motion for the northern region to support the re-election of the Tinubu/Shettima ticket, outlining reasons why the region should mobilize massively for the president.

He noted that the region’s strong backing stems from the Vice President’s inclusive leadership and progressive mindset over the past three years.

This impact, Yilwatda added, is clearly demonstrated through the execution of landmark projects across multiple sectors and the strategic appointment of prominent local leaders to key positions.

Similarly, Secretary to Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, said history was beckoning on the North to act with wisdom, evidence and not sentiment in its decision to support the Tinubu administration in the 2027 elections.

Reeling out the achievements of the administration in the region, the SGF said the north’s position and strength in driving Nigeria’s unity and progress must be leveraged in the forthcoming presidential elections in 2027.

For his part, the Governor of Kano State, Abba Kabir Yusuf, who spoke on behalf of all the governors of the North, said Arewa would massively support the re-election of the Tinubu/Shettima ticket on the basis of the administration’s track record of performance.

He said the northern region’s support for the President in the forthcoming elections would be based on its conviction to uphold fairness, equity, unity and the progress of the country.

In his welcome address, Abubakar Mohammed Badaru—the Director General of A4A and former Jigawa State governor—stated that the emergence of the group was not accidental, but rather born out of the conviction that President Tinubu and his deputy have performed well and deserve to be re-elected.

He assured the President and APC leadership that the message of continuity and completion of the Tinubu administration’s transformational works would be taken to every nook and cranny of northern Nigeria, using the A4A network across the region and beyond.

Also present at the event were serving members of the National Assembly, ministers, presidential aides, heads of government agencies, former governors, and senior citizens, all from the northern region.

World.title: EPL: Haaland stars in Man City win, Liverpool beat Brentford
World.content:
Manchester City’s Norwegian striker #09 Erling Haaland (R) scores the team’s third goal during the English Premier League football match between Manchester City and Ipswich Town at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, north west England, on October 17, 2026. (Photo by Oli SCARFF / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services. Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /

Erling Haaland starred with a double as Premier League leaders Manchester City beat Ipswich 3-2, while Liverpool came from behind to seal a 2-1 win at Brentford on Saturday.

City are in turmoil off the pitch after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.

On the grass they have made a perfect start, with seven successive league victories marking their best opening to a Premier League season.

City, who are appealing against the guilty verdict after branding it a “Premier League conspiracy”, sit six points clear of champions Arsenal.

Second-placed Arsenal can close the gap with a win at Nottingham Forest on Sunday.

With City potentially facing a massive points deduction or even expulsion from the top flight if their appeal fails, it remains to be seen whether their results will even matter by the end of the season.

For now, Enzo Maresca’s side are in fine form after bouncing back from their midweek loss to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.

There was a defiant mood at the Etihad Stadium, where City fans booed the Premier League anthem before kick-off, while thousands waved inflatable bananas to underline their commitment to the club regardless of its plight.

City supporters took toy bananas to matches to lighten the mood when the team was struggling in the late 1980s.

Phil Foden put Maresca’s men ahead in the 19th minute with a sharp turn and finish after Jeremy Doku’s incisive run prised open the Ipswich defence.

Foden’s first goal this season was followed by an Ipswich equaliser in the 21st minute when Daizen Maeda evaded Marc Guehi to fire home.

Haaland restored City’s lead in the 34th minute with a pin-point header from Mateo Kovacic’s cross.

Haaland killed off Ipswich in the 69th minute, sprinting onto Iliman Ndiaye’s pass and steering his shot past Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton.

Zian Flemming’s 90th-minute penalty, awarded for a foul by Guehi, set up a tense finale but City held on.

“Very happy with today’s game, we controlled it for 95 minutes. We create chances, we score. We finish a little bit suffering together but overall, it is good,” Maresca said.

– Liverpool revival –

In west London, Liverpool were stunned when Brentford defender Keane Lewis-Potter looped a header past Alisson Becker from Igor Thiago’s cross in the 44th minute.

But the Bees were reduced to 10 men in first half stoppage-time after Yehor Yarmolyuk’s head made contact with Jeremy Jacquet’s face while they waited for a corner.

Liverpool lost Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong to injuries, but still made their numerical advantage count in the 62nd minute.

Victor Munoz cut inside and slotted a composed equaliser past Brentford’s former Liverpool keeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

Alexander Isak blasted Liverpool’s winner in the 70th minute after Barcola teed up the Sweden striker for his fifth goal this term.

Brentford finished with nine men following Vitaly Janelt’s second booking in stoppage-time.

Beaten by City in their previous league game, Liverpool are up to fifth place after inflicting Brentford’s first league defeat of the season.

“You see the results of Brentford at home and you have to be ready for these kinds of battles. We had 45 minutes to do the comeback and I think we played really well,” Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said.

Pedro Neto’s double condemned Everton to a first defeat of the season as fourth-placed Chelsea won 2-0 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium despite the loss of goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez to a head injury.

Neto opened the scoring inside the first minute of the second half and secured the points during stoppage-time.

The Argentine international was involved in a sickening head clash with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite and was taken to hospital.

Fulham won for the first time in the league this season as Alex Iwobi’s 33rd-minute goal clinched a 1-0 victory against Hull at Craven Cottage.

Alvaro Arbeloa’s side moved out of the relegation zone despite having Ryan Sessegnon sent off for a crude lunge on Robinio Vaz in the final minutes.

Newcastle host Aston Villa in Saturday’s late game.

AFP

World.title: Reps seek tougher food safety laws amid malnutrition concerns, organ failure
World.content:
By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja

ABUJA — The House of Representatives has called for stronger food safety laws and enforcement mechanisms to address malnutrition, food insecurity and the health risks associated with unsafe food and the indiscriminate use of agricultural chemicals in Nigeria.

The House Committee on Nutrition and Food Security said existing policies had not adequately addressed the challenges, stressing the need for enforceable legislation to guarantee access to safe, nutritious and affordable food.

The committee’s position was contained in a speech delivered by its Clerk, Agenti Milicent, on behalf of its chairman, Chike Okafor, at a World Food Day media briefing in Abuja on Friday.

The event was organised by the Centre for Food Safety and Agriculture Research in conjunction with LoveWorld Ministry of Food Technology and Sovereignty.

According to the committee, Nigeria continues to grapple with malnutrition, stunting, wasting and anaemia, alongside poor exclusive breastfeeding practices.

“We have many policies, but few enforceable laws,” the chairman said, calling for legislative action to address the country’s food and nutrition challenges.

He added that legislative measures were needed to ensure that every Nigerian, from unborn children to farmers and other citizens, had access to safe, nutritious and affordable food.

The committee also warned that unsafe food production and the indiscriminate use of chemicals could worsen public health problems, including kidney and liver diseases.

It called for legislation to protect local food systems, ensure the effective utilisation of nutrition funds and shield children from aggressive marketing of unhealthy foods.

Okafor said the committee was working on legislative measures, including a bill to establish the Nutritionist Registration Council of Nigeria to regulate the nutrition profession.

He also disclosed that the committee was involved in efforts to advance a National Nutrition Bill sponsored by the Presidency through the Office of the Vice-President, which he said had reached an advanced stage ahead of its transmission to the National Assembly.

On its achievements, the committee said it had facilitated the establishment of nutrition and food security committees in 32 state Houses of Assembly following a legislative retreat in Owerri, Imo State.

The committees subsequently formed the National Legislative Network of Nutrition and Food Security, which was inaugurated by the Speaker of the House of Representatives on July 22, 2024.

The committee further disclosed that it was investigating the alleged misuse of government agricultural intervention funds by agencies, schemes and programmes operating outside the Federal Ministry of Agriculture.

The investigation also covers concerns surrounding agricultural interventions and issues associated with ginger blight disease, which devastated production in parts of the country.

Okafor said the committee had engaged the Central Bank of Nigeria, the National Agricultural Development Board and other relevant agencies as part of the investigation.

He called for collaboration among federal and state legislatures, civil society organisations, development partners and other stakeholders to tackle food insecurity.

“Malnutrition and food insecurity remain a constant threat to socio-economic development in Nigeria, as much as they have become an existential threat,” he said.

He added that worsening inflation had increased the burden on ordinary Nigerians, arguing that the country’s arable land, water resources and human capital should enable it to tackle hunger and malnutrition through coordinated action.

Ginger production crisis

Speaking at the event, a food safety advocate, Dr. Shego, raised concerns about the decline in Nigeria’s ginger production, alleging that contaminated agricultural inputs contributed to a devastating outbreak of ginger blight disease that destroyed farmers’ harvests.

He recalled that Nigeria was previously among the world’s leading ginger exporters but suffered severe production losses that increased its reliance on imported ginger.

According to him, farmers who used certain agricultural inputs supplied under intervention programmes began noticing black spots, blight and softening in their crops before harvest.
