He said the resulting losses caused the price of a bag of ginger to rise from about ₦25,000 to approximately ₦800,000.

The advocate called for a thorough examination of agricultural intervention programmes and the chemicals used in food production, warning that poorly regulated inputs could undermine food security and public health.

He also advocated a shift towards organic farming and the use of natural seeds, urging Nigerians, where practical, to consider planting edible crops rather than ornamental plants.

“Food safety concerns everyone, regardless of their religious affiliations or background,” he said, stressing the need to prioritise safe food production.

Stakeholders advocate sustainable farming

Other participants urged farmers, investors, processors and distributors to work together to promote safe food production and strengthen Nigeria’s agricultural value chain.

The founder of Benjamin Protocol Incorporated, Nwaoloko Ifeanyi, said his organisation had ventured into ginger farming as part of its commerce and investment activities.

He described food safety as essential to sustainable agricultural production, saying, “Safety first before harvest. You can’t get harvest from what you do not preserve.”

Ifeanyi said the organisation supported farming approaches that gave farmers greater control over their planting materials, including regenerative seeds that could be replanted after harvest.

He called for collaboration among farmers, researchers, investors, entrepreneurs, processors and distributors to build a food system that protects consumers and creates economic opportunities.

Similarly, Lucas Samu of Lufris Global Enterprise said his organisation was working with the initiative to promote safe agricultural production, food processing and packaging.

“The best medicine you consume is your food,” he said, urging Nigerians to pay greater attention to the quality and composition of what they eat.

Samu added that food processing and packaging must be properly managed to ensure products reaching consumers were safe.

Another participant, agricultural commodity sourcing and processing expert Ella Omezi, said the initiative was committed to providing farmers with organic seeds to support the production of organic raw materials for food processing and export.

She said the programme was designed to encourage Nigerians across religious, economic and regional backgrounds to participate in food production.

Participants said the “Let’s Go Planting” initiative was intended not only to encourage household and commercial farming but also to attract investment into agriculture, food processing and other segments of the food value chain.

The event commemorated the 2026 World Food Day, themed “Innovate Today, Nourish Tomorrow.”

World.title: NASS kicks against externally influenced staff promotion
World.content:
By Henry Umoru

The National Assembly has kicked against what it described as externally influenced promotion of its staff not backed by merit, as provided for in the National Assembly Service Act 2014 and applicable scheme of service.

The National Assembly has also rejected existing ad hoc arrangements of personnel training which, according to it, are not sustainable and lack the institutional capacity the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies ( NILDS) is known for.

Speaking on Saturday at the commencement of a three-day retreat for top management of the National Assembly and National Assembly Service Commission (NASC), held at Transcorp Hilton Hotel, Abuja, Clerk to the National Assembly, CNA, Kamoru Ogunlana said the National Assembly service is a professional one, requiring staff to be appointed, promoted and developed principally based on merit, competence, experience and performance as stipulated by the National Assembly Service Act 2014.

“Where appointments or promotions are influenced by considerations outside the National Assembly Service Act 2014, and the applicable Scheme of Service, we risk creating serious institutional consequences, that is, judicial review, administrative embarrassment and institutional instability,” he warned.

The CNA noted that the consequences may not be limited to the individuals involved; they may also affect the entire Service, adding, “When seniority, cognate experience and competence is subordinated to ‘where you come from’ or other considerations, we may find ourselves with positions occupied by people who do not possess the requisite competence, experience or capacity for those responsibilities.

“The result can be an institution with too many people in positions and too few people with the capacity to perform those positions effectively.”

On training, the CNA said time had come for NASS to look inward for training of its personnel through an affiliate agency, the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies ( NILDS), on account of Institutional capacity and scarce resources.

He said: “Our staff require continuous exposure to legislative practice, parliamentary procedure, policy analysis, research, digital technologies, public financial management, ethics, leadership and emerging global practices in parliamentary administration.

“The present ad hoc arrangement of training personnel of service is not sustainable given our limited financial resources.

“In this regard, I believe we should make more deliberate use of the considerable institutional capacity of the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies (NILDS) as the central professional platform for the training and development of staff of the National Assembly Service.”

In his message, the Executive Chairman, National Assembly Service Commission (NASC), Chief Saviour Enyiekere, said the commission remains committed to fostering a disciplined, competent, responsive and forward – looking legislative service in which merit is recognised, due process respected, staff welfare receives appropriate attention and every officer encouraged to contribute meaningfully to institutional progress.

Both the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio and Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Tajudeen Abbas, were represented at the ceremony.

World.title: Tinubu scraps recruitment waiver for federal universities, strengthens autonomy
World.content:
By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has removed federal universities from the requirement to obtain recruitment waivers from the Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation (OHCSF), in a major policy shift aimed at easing staffing bottlenecks and strengthening institutional autonomy.

The reform, which allows universities to respond more directly to their manpower needs, was disclosed by the President at the maiden convocation ceremony of the Federal University of Health Sciences, Azare, FUHSA, Bauchi State, on Saturday, where 50 pioneer graduates received their degrees.

Tinubu, who is the visitor to all federal universities, was represented at the ceremony by the Executive Secretary of the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund), Arc. Sonny Echono.

He said the removal of the recruitment waiver requirement was captured in recent agreements signed between the Federal Government and university staff unions, describing the measure as part of broader efforts to strengthen the administration and operations of tertiary institutions.

“This measure empowers the Federal Ministry of Education and university Governing Councils to discharge their respective responsibilities in staff recruitment, enabling institutions to respond more effectively to their legitimate manpower needs,” the President said.

The development is expected to give university authorities greater room to address staffing gaps without the additional administrative hurdle of securing recruitment waivers from the OHCSF.

Tinubu also disclosed that the Federal Government was moving to improve personnel and payroll administration in tertiary institutions through the migration of their staff from the Integrated Personnel and Payroll Information System (IPPIS) to the Government Integrated Financial Management Information System (GIFMIS).

According to him, the transition is designed to improve payroll efficiency, transparency and accountability, ensure timely and accurate salary payments, and accommodate the operational peculiarities of universities and other tertiary institutions.

The President said the measures reflected the government’s commitment to strengthening institutional autonomy and creating a more enabling environment for teaching, research, innovation and service delivery.

Beyond the recruitment reforms, Tinubu announced substantial funding commitments to FUHSA, disclosing that the university had received an initial N8 billion intervention through TETFund to support its establishment.

He said the investment followed lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic, which exposed critical weaknesses in Nigeria’s healthcare system and underscored the need to strengthen the country’s capacity to train health professionals and conduct medical research.

The President said additional funding would be made available to the institution through TETFund’s regular and special interventions, alongside allocations in the 2026 national budget for roads, lecture halls, laboratories and utility vehicles.

He also disclosed that the Federal Government had provided N10 billion for the National Research Fund in the 2026 fiscal year, urging universities, particularly specialised institutions such as FUHSA, to prioritise research capable of addressing Nigeria’s pressing health challenges.

Tinubu said investments in health sciences education and research remained critical to producing the skilled workforce required to improve healthcare delivery and reduce the country’s vulnerabilities in the health sector.

On staff welfare, the President announced that the Federal Government had signed agreements with academic and non-academic staff unions on the payment of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) and Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance (CONTTA), effective January 1, 2026.

He said the agreements, covering universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, recognised the distinct but complementary contributions of teaching and non-teaching personnel to the effective running of tertiary institutions.

“These agreements recognise the distinct but complementary contributions of academic and non-teaching personnel to the effective functioning of our tertiary institutions.

“Both categories are indispensable to the delivery of quality education and national development,” he said.

The agreements form part of the government’s broader engagement with tertiary education unions on staff welfare and the conditions required to sustain effective teaching, research and institutional administration.

Tinubu further revealed that 1,798 students of FUHSA, representing 43 per cent of the university’s student population, had secured support from the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) for the 2025/2026 academic session.

He said the student loan scheme was intended to ensure that financial difficulties did not prevent qualified Nigerians from accessing higher education.

The president congratulated the 50 pioneer graduands, urging them to apply their knowledge and professional skills to improving healthcare delivery, particularly for vulnerable Nigerians.

“Your success will be measured not only by your personal achievements but also by the positive difference you make in the lives of others,” he said.

He charged the graduands to uphold professionalism, integrity, compassion and service as they begin their careers, stressing the importance of placing the welfare of patients and the wider society at the centre of their work.

Tinubu also commended the university’s management, staff and governing council for laying the foundation of the institution, urging them to build it into a centre of excellence in health sciences education, research and innovation.

He encouraged FUHSA to deepen its collaborations with international institutions, including the University of Miami, Boston University and Universiti Sains Malaysia, while ensuring that the partnerships translate into measurable improvements in teaching, research and healthcare delivery.

The President reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to supporting the university’s development, expressing confidence that its growth would strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to produce competent health professionals and researchers

World.title: Lagos halts unauthorised wetland reclamation over flood risks
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

LAGOS — Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State has warned residents and property developers against building on wetlands and drainage channels, saying their destruction is worsening flooding and coastal erosion in the state.

The governor also said the state government had suspended reclamation activities affecting wetlands, floodplains and lagoon fronts where the required Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and drainage approvals were not obtained.

Sanwo-Olu gave the warning on Saturday at the 20th Annual Walk for Nature, organised by the Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF) in collaboration with the Lagos State Government at Makanjuola Hall, Lagos State University (LASU), Ojo.

Represented by the Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Ministry of Environment and Water Resources, Dr. Omobolaji Gaji, the governor said Lagos generates about 13,000 tonnes of waste daily, with plastics accounting for approximately 15 per cent of the volume.

He said much of the plastic waste finds its way into drains, canals and the lagoon, contributing to environmental degradation and increasing the risk of flooding.

According to him, Lagos’ coastal location, low-lying terrain and dense population make the protection of wetlands essential to public safety.

“Our wetlands, mangroves and lagoons are our first line of defence against floods and coastal erosion. Where they are filled or built over, water has nowhere to go,” he said.

Sanwo-Olu said the state had banned Styrofoam and other single-use plastics, adding that enforcement had been ongoing since July 1, 2025.

He warned that outlets found storing, selling or distributing the banned items would face sanctions.

The governor added that the government was working with innovators to develop sustainable alternatives while promoting environmental education in schools and communities.

On wetland protection, he said the government suspended reclamation activities affecting wetlands, floodplains and lagoon fronts in September 2025 where developers had failed to obtain the required environmental and drainage approvals.

“Development in Lagos must pass the test of drainage and environmental approval,” he said.

Sanwo-Olu said the government was also investing in drainage infrastructure, mangrove restoration, tree planting and the development of parks as part of efforts to address environmental challenges.

He urged residents to stop dumping refuse in drains, reduce their use of single-use plastics and avoid building on wetlands.

The governor also charged LASU students to embrace waste separation, plant trees and hold both their neighbours and the government accountable for environmental protection.

He said the 20 years of the Walk for Nature had helped raise environmental awareness, adding that the next two decades must focus on translating that awareness into tangible results.

Earlier, the Chairman of the NCF National Executive Council, Justice R. Adebiyi, said Lagos was at the forefront of Nigeria’s climate vulnerability, with rising sea levels, flooding, extreme heat and wetland loss threatening communities.

“Our wetlands, our forests, our waterways, our green spaces — they are not luxuries; they are infrastructure that we need to keep Lagos liveable,” she said.

Adebiyi cited the Lekki Conservation Centre as an example of an ecosystem preserved within a rapidly growing urban environment.

She urged universities to promote waste separation, campus clean-ups and energy conservation, while calling on the government to integrate climate action into land-use planning and flood management.

The Vice-Chancellor of LASU, Prof. Ayodeji Badejo, represented by the Senior Deputy Bursar, Jerry Jinadu, described the Walk for Nature as more than an exercise, saying it promoted physical fitness, social interaction and environmental responsibility.

The event featured a road walk from the LASU campus to Iyana School Bus Stop and the unveiling of a giant plastic waste bin at the university to encourage responsible waste disposal.

Corporate partners, including 7UP Bottling Company, Zenith Bank and Fidelity Bank, pledged support for environmental sustainability initiatives.

World.title: TETFund Budget Jumps From N320bn To N1.6trn, Says Masari
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) budget has risen sharply from N320.3 billion in 2023 to N1.6 trillion in 2025, reflecting increased federal government investment in tertiary education.

Chairman of TETFund Board of Trustees, Aminu Bello Masari, disclosed this at the 2026 National Town Hall Meeting of the Fund held in Abuja yesterday.

Masari said the figure rose from N320.3 billion in 2023 to N683.4 billion in 2024 before hitting N1.6 trillion in 2025, about five times the 2023 allocation, demonstrating President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to human capital development.

He however stressed that the increased funding must translate to tangible results in academic performance, research output and graduate employability.

Masari disclosed that 271 institutions are covered under the 2026 annual direct intervention, with about N2.526 billion for each university, N1.871 billion for each polytechnic and N2.057 billion for each college of education.

He said the Fund committed N10 billion in 2026 to skills acquisition centres in polytechnics, supported innovation and entrepreneurship facilities in 12 universities, and approved N48 billion for upgrading engineering and technology facilities.

He added that about N6.09 billion was approved for 174 successful research proposals under the 2025 National Research Fund grant cycle, while presidential approval has been secured for six additional Centres of Excellence in robotics, coding, Artificial Intelligence, machine learning and cybersecurity, bringing the total to 36 centres.

Masari urged beneficiary institutions to ensure transparency, prudent management and proper maintenance of facilities, warning that funding alone cannot fix all challenges.

Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, said government is pushing curriculum reforms to produce graduates with practical, industry-relevant skills, commending TETFund for supporting infrastructure, research and specialised equipment.

Alausa said reforms include a proposed 80 percent practical and 20 percent theoretical curriculum model, with 36 new and reviewed National Diplomas, 10 additional ND programmes, 30 National Certificates in Education and 21 National Occupational Standards already produced 27 new and four reviewed.

He said programmes will continue to be aligned with labour market demands, and that initiatives like NELFUND will expand access so that financial hardship, disability or location does not block qualified Nigerians from completing education.

Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, described education as critical to human capital development and national productivity, calling for effective monitoring and transparent reporting to ensure investments deliver impact.

Executive Secretary of TETFund, Sonny Echono, disclosed that over 418 projects are ready for commissioning across beneficiary institutions, with 14 projects at one institution alone.

He said the Fund is expanding investments in infrastructure, research, student welfare, innovation and digital learning, supporting student innovation from idea development to intellectual property protection and industry linkage.

Echono added that student transportation initiatives cover 42 institutions, with about 98 schools provided electric-powered vehicles for affordable student transport, while the Fund is working with the Ministry of Labour to align skills development with manpower needs.

World.title: Over 1,000 Participate In Pinknaija Walk 2026, Puts Port Harcourt At Centre Of Breast Advocacy
World.content:
Sylvester Idowu in Warri

‎

More than 1,000 participants converged on Captain Elechi Amadi Polytechnic, Rumuola, Port Harcourt, on Saturday, October 10, for PinkNaija Walk 2026, in a major show of support for breast cancer awareness, early detection and improved access to cancer care.

‎

‎Organised by Engraced Life Foundation (ELF), the annual eight-kilometre walk brought together representatives of the Rivers State Government, health institutions, cancer organisations, survivors, students, corps members, business owners, influencers and members of the public under the theme, ‘United By Unique—Every Story Matters. Every Life Counts.’

‎

‎Recognised by the state, as the leading statewide breast cancer awareness mobilisation since 2021, and the biggest of its kind in the South-south region, the event transformed the Rumuola venue into a meeting point for organisations and individuals working to improve cancer awareness and patient support.

‎

‎The morning opened with an energetic warm-up session, before the Rivers State Government delegation and WHO led participants on the walk. The eight-kilometre route began and ended at Captain Elechi Amadi Polytechnic, taking participants through Rumuola and surrounding parts of Port Harcourt.

‎

‎The walk was followed by an interactive health and community engagement featuring medical information stands, breast health demonstrations, health talks, games, vendors and free screening services.

‎

‎Representing the Permanent Secretary of the Rivers State Ministry of Health, Dr Hope Avundaa, in an opening remarks, highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and collaboration in improving health outcomes.

‎

‎The Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), the Medical Women’s Association of Nigeria (MWAN), Peter Odili Cancer and Cardiovascular Hospital (POCCH) and the World Health Organization (WHO) community were among the medical and institutional stakeholders represented at the event.

‎

‎More than 400 women and men received health screening services, including breast and cervical cancer screening, prostate screening, blood pressure and blood sugar checks, alongside access to medical consultations assisted by Power Oil.

‎

‎The screening activities reinforced the foundation’s message that awareness must translate into practical access to health information, medical assessment and appropriate referrals.

‎

‎One of the event’s major highlights was a special parade by the Engraced Life Foundation medical team, led by Dr. Stella Jerry Chukwu that showcased the foundation’s achievements and recognitions over the years, culminating in the presentation of its latest international honour.

‎

‎In September 2026, the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) announced Engraced Life Foundation as the winner of the World Cancer Day Campaign Award for its PinkRoom Schools Outreach initiative.

The award was presented at the World Cancer Congress in Hong Kong, recognising the foundation’s work in advancing the global United by Unique campaign through education, community engagement and people-centred cancer care.

‎

‎The recognition places a Nigerian community-based cancer advocacy organisation among the international initiatives celebrated by UICC and highlights the contribution of locally driven programmes to global cancer control.

‎

‎For founder Ethel Olumo, the recognition represents both an achievement and a call to greater responsibility.

‎

‎“Receiving this recognition on an international platform means a great deal to us. It affirms that the work we are doing in our communities matters, and that solutions developed in Nigeria can contribute meaningfully to the global fight against cancer. For us, the award is not the end of the journey. It is a call to reach more people, especially young girls and underserved women who may otherwise be left out of essential health information and care,” Olumo said.

‎

‎The foundation’s achievement comes amid growing international attention to Nigeria’s role in cancer advocacy and the country’s contribution to global cancer-control efforts.

‎The walk provided a platform for cancer survivors to share their experiences and encourage others to seek care without shame or fear.

‎

‎Among them was Benita Egone, a six-year thriver who travelled from Warri, Delta State, to participate. Her account of survival offered encouragement to women navigating diagnosis, treatment and recovery, while underscoring the importance of emotional support and a community that treats survivors with dignity.

‎

‎Dr Ngozi Welle, breast cancer survivor and New York-based founder of VictoriousNG, also joined the engagement, addressing women and celebrating survivors. She was one of many guests who travelled from different locations, including the United States, to participate in the campaign and show solidarity with the cancer advocacy community.

‎

‎For many participants, the gathering was an opportunity to see breast cancer awareness beyond the usual October campaign: as a continuing responsibility that involves listening to survivors, supporting patients and ensuring that women can access timely information and appropriate care.

‎

‎Another important feature of the engagement was the official introduction of FT3, From Testing to Targeted Treatments, by Barbara Ariolu from the ELF medical unit.

‎

‎The international initiative provides patient-centred resources designed to help people affected by cancer and their representatives understand targeted therapies, biomarker testing and the questions they can ask healthcare professionals when considering treatment options. Its inclusion at PinkNaija Walk 2026 extended the campaign beyond prevention and early detection to address the importance of treatment knowledge and informed conversations between patients and medical teams.

‎

‎Survivors and advocates were engaged on how improved understanding of treatment options can support more meaningful participation in healthcare decisions and help patients navigate their care pathways. National Coordinator of Engraced Life Foundation, Tamunotonye Pamela Daniel, thanked the Rivers State Ministry of Health, the office of the Permanent Secretary – Dr. Vincent Wachukwu, WHO Rivers State coordinator and team, medical associations, institutional partners, volunteers, supporters and individuals whose contributions helped make the walk possible.

‎

‎She said the foundation would continue to use every available resource and communication channel to advance breast cancer awareness, encourage early detection and improve access to screening, particularly among underserved communities.

‎

‎“PinkNaija Walk opens our October campaign, but our work continues long after the walk. We are taking the message into communities where women and men may have limited access to screening, reliable information and medical guidance. Our goal is to make early detection and informed health decisions accessible, regardless of where people live or their financial circumstances,” Daniel said.

‎

‎Following the Port Harcourt event, the foundation plans further awareness and screening activities across Ekiti, Lagos and Abia States, alongside additional outreaches in Rivers State and other communities. The national campaign will offer free breast screening, health education and other available health checks, connecting participants to medical professionals and appropriate referrals where necessary.

‎

‎Although the Niger Delta and the wider South-south remain core areas of focus, the foundation says its mission extends across Nigeria, particularly to communities where access to cancer information and early detection services remains limited. As the foundation builds towards World Cancer Day on February 4, 2027, attention is turning to its next phase of school-based advocacy through the PinkRoom Schools Outreach, which targets 20 schools.

‎

‎The initiative provides age-appropriate breast and cervical health education, personal hygiene information, guidance on recognising changes in the body and information on when to seek help from a trusted adult or qualified health professional. It also aims to equip girls with practical self-care resources and dignity kits, helping to make health education accessible and relevant to their daily lives.

‎

‎The urgency of reaching young people is underscored by the need to ensure that girls understand their bodies, can discuss health concerns without stigma and know where to seek reliable guidance. While breast changes and lumps do not automatically indicate cancer, any unusual or persistent change should be assessed by a qualified health professional.

‎

‎The foundation is therefore calling on schools, government agencies, healthcare providers, corporate organisations, development partners and individual supporters to collaborate in reaching the 20 targeted schools and expanding the programme’s impact. With PinkNaija Walk 2026 setting the pace for another season of advocacy, Engraced Life Foundation is urging Nigerians to support the campaign towards World Cancer Day 2027 and help ensure that awareness leads to practical action.

‎

‎For the foundation, the message remains clear: every story matters, every life counts, and access to cancer awareness and early detection must extend beyond the event ground into the communities where it is needed most.

World.title: Navy Intensifies Crackdown on Oil Thieves, Uncovers Three Underground Reservoirs Containing 75,000 Litres of Crude Oil
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Navy has intensified its crackdown on oil thieves, as troops of Operation Delta Sentinel uncovered three dugout reservoirs containing a total of 75,000 litres of crude oil in the Oteghele general area of Delta State. The discoveries followed two separate operations conducted on 12 and 14 October 2026.

The Service said the operations, carried out by Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Delta, led to the discovery of approximately 30,000 litres of suspected crude oil in one reservoir on 12 October and a further 45,000 litres in two large reservoirs on 14 October.

According to a statement by the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, the reservoirs and their contents were handled in accordance with established procedures.

“The successive discoveries highlight the presence of concealed storage points that could facilitate the accumulation and onward movement of suspected stolen crude oil.

“Uncovering these stockpiles disrupts a key link in the illicit petroleum trade and reduces opportunities for the unlawful exploitation of the nation’s oil resources.

“Through Operation Delta Sentinel, the Nigerian Navy has continued to uncover concealed petroleum stockpiles and disrupt infrastructure suspected of supporting crude oil theft,” Captain Folorunsho said.

He stressed that the Navy would sustain intelligence-led operations to identify and dismantle such facilities, constrain the activities of oil thieves and illegal refiners, and protect critical national assets. The ultimate aim, he added, was to curb oil-related economic sabotage and safeguard Nigeria’s petroleum revenue.

World.title: AI Will Transform Healthcare, Says Prof. Okeji
World.content:
.Urge medical professionals to embrace technology

.As PAMO University inducts 28 health professionals

Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

A professor of Radiography and Radiological Sciences at the University of Nigeria Nsukka, Prof. Mark Okeji, has noted that Artificial intelligence (AI) is set to revolutionise healthcare delivery by accelerating diagnosis, improving patient monitoring and supporting clinical decisions.

Prof. Okeji however, urged medical professionals to embrace emerging technologies to remain relevant in a rapidly changing health sector.

Okeji, made the assertion as the induction lecturer at the joint induction and oath-taking ceremony for graduates of the Departments of Medical Laboratory Science, Nursing Science, and Radiography and Radiation Science at PAMO University of Medical Sciences, Iriebe, Obio/Akpor Local Government Area of Rivers State, yesterday.

He said AI would enhance the efficiency and accuracy of healthcare services rather than simply replace human professionals.

Okeji, warned that practitioners who failed to acquire the skills required to work with the technology risked being left behind.

“AI has not come to replace you. It has come to help you. It makes the job simpler and makes our patients feel better. So, don’t be afraid of it. But if you’re not there to understand AI, AI will take over from you,” he said.

Okeji explained that AI-powered diagnostic systems could analyse medical samples, interpret images and process large volumes of patient information within seconds, significantly reducing the time required for investigations and improving the speed of clinical decisions.

According to him, AI is already being deployed in medical diagnostics, telemedicine, hospital administration, clinical decision-making and remote patient monitoring.

He said wearable devices, including smart watches, could help monitor vital health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen levels and sleep patterns, providing clinicians with information that could support early intervention.

The professor also highlighted AI’s potential to strengthen public health surveillance by analysing disease patterns, predicting outbreaks and helping authorities deploy medical personnel and resources to areas with urgent healthcare needs.

He identified data fragmentation, privacy concerns, algorithmic bias and inadequate trust among some healthcare professionals as challenges requiring urgent attention.

While advocating stronger ethical safeguards and regulation, Okeji urged medical practitioners and healthcare institutions to develop the competence needed to harness AI responsibly.

“AI is transforming healthcare today. Tomorrow, it will redefine it. The future is intelligent, connected and very human-centred,” he said.

Earlier in his welcome address, the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Smith Jaja, said the 28 inductees had undergone rigorous academic and clinical training, expressing confidence in their preparedness to serve the healthcare sector.

“We are proud to inform everyone that these graduates have gone through the best training anybody in their respective professions can receive,” Jaja said.

He charged the graduates to uphold professional ethics and honour the oaths they had taken, describing the occasion as a significant milestone for the university, the graduates and their families.

Representing the Pro-Chancellor, Dr. Peter Odili, former Rivers State Commissioner for Health, Prof. Adaeze Oreh, congratulated the inductees and emphasised the importance of collaboration among nurses, medical laboratory scientists and radiographers in delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care.

She described medical laboratory scientists as the “detectives of medicine,” nurses as the “heart and backbone of patient care,” and radiographers as the “eyes of medicine,” stressing that each profession played a critical role in improving patient outcomes.

Oreh also announced that the university’s governing board had approved automatic employment after internship for the best graduating students from the three departments.

She urged the inductees to take their internship seriously, noting that the period was essential to their transition into fully credentialed and licensed professionals.

The Acting Dean of the Faculty of Allied Health Sciences, Dr. Clement Nyenke, said the induction represented more than the completion of academic programmes, describing it as the beginning of a lifelong commitment to patients, professional colleagues and society.

He urged the graduates to demonstrate sound judgement, accuracy and respect for human life in their practice.

World.title: 2027: Kwara ADC Promises to Tackle Insecurity, Food Security If Formed Govt
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

The opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Kwara State has said that it would embark on intensive intelligence gathering, deployment of technology and improved support for conventional security among the residents of the state so as to return the state into her original status of ‘State of Harmony’ if it forms government of the state come 2027.



The party also said that the administration would develop agricultural potential of the state so as to ensure affordable food for all and sundry.



The governorship candidate of the ADC in the state, Hon. Zakari Mohammed, made the promises in Ilorin yesterday while addressing journalists on the sidelines of his governorship ambition in the state.

Mohammed, a former member of the House of Representatives representing Baruten/Kaiama Federal Constituency from 2011 to 2019, stressed that security remained fundamental to development, warning that the rising insecurity in parts of the state could undermine farming activities, economic growth and residents’ livelihoods.

“No meaningful development takes place without security,” he said, outlining his proposed approach to tackling insecurity in the state.

According to him, his administration would prioritise community-based intelligence gathering, the deployment of technology and improved support for conventional security agencies to strengthen the protection of lives and property.

He also called for greater collaboration between residents and security agencies, urging members of the public to report suspicious activities to relevant authorities.

Mohammed, who served in the National Assembly for eight years, said Kwara needed a comprehensive development strategy that would address the peculiar challenges facing its northern, central and southern senatorial districts.

He identified agriculture as a critical sector requiring urgent attention, noting that several communities in the state depended on farming for their livelihoods.

The ADC candidate argued that improving agricultural productivity and supporting farmers would help address food insecurity and reduce the cost of living.

He criticised the economic policies of the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led governments at the federal and state levels, accusing them of placing additional financial burdens on households through taxation and other economic measures.

Mohammed maintained that government should adopt policies that would make food more affordable, citing agricultural subsidies in some countries as examples of interventions that could help reduce production costs and improve food availability.

He also highlighted education and healthcare as important areas that required sustained investment, stressing the need to expand opportunities for residents and improve access to essential services.

On political leadership, the former lawmaker urged voters to assess candidates based on their programmes, competence and capacity to deliver, rather than sentiments or political affiliations.

He challenged political parties and their candidates to explain how they intended to address the challenges confronting the people instead of relying solely on campaign promises.

Mohammed further said the ADC was committed to implementing its manifesto, insisting that candidates elected on the party’s platform would be expected to operate within its policy framework.

He expressed confidence that a government focused on security, agriculture, education, healthcare and economic relief could improve the living conditions of residents across the State.

World.title: Defence Minister Urges Graduating Officers to Adapt Faster Than Those Seeking to Undermine National Security
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd.), has urged graduating military officers to strengthen their ability to anticipate risks, identify vulnerabilities and adapt more quickly than those seeking to undermine national security. He stressed that their task is not simply to respond to threats after they emerge.

He also urged the officers to combine professional competence with intellectual curiosity and the courage to make difficult decisions under pressure.

Speaking at the graduation ceremony of Army War College Nigeria Course 10/2026 yesterday in Abuja, the Defence Minister stressed that Nigeria was making efforts to develop indigenous defence capabilities in various areas while strengthening cooperation with reliable international partners.

He said, “The task before you, therefore, is not simply to respond to threats after they emerge. We must strengthen our ability to anticipate risks, identify vulnerabilities and adapt more quickly than those who seek to undermine our national security.

“I believe this college has imparted these skills to you. Today’s commanders and leaders must combine professional competence with intellectual curiosity and have the courage to make difficult decisions under pressure.

“At the forefront of our strategic vision, we are making efforts to develop indigenous defence capabilities in various areas while strengthening cooperation with reliable international partners. Our long-term security architecture cannot rest solely on foreign technologies.”

General Musa said Nigeria was progressively building the capacity to understand, maintain, adapt and produce systems that respond to its own operational realities.

He said this required purposeful collaboration among the Armed Forces, universities, research institutions, defence industries and Nigerian innovators.

He added, “Our institutions must build capacity in areas relevant to hybrid warfare, such as unmanned aerial systems, artificial intelligence, cyber capabilities and data analytics, to enhance operational effectiveness. As current and future operational and strategic leaders, you have a direct role to play in this process.

“Innovation is not the exclusive responsibility of engineers, scientists or procurement specialists. Commanders are often best placed to identify operational gaps, articulate problems clearly and work towards developing solutions.”

He concluded that the value of the college would ultimately be measured not by the certificates alone, but by the quality of judgement the officers demonstrated in leadership and the results they delivered in the field.

World.title: Jonathan to Chair Launch of Solomon and Mary Lar Leadership Institute in Abuja
World.content:
Kasim Sumaina in Abuja

Former President Goodluck Ebele Jonathan will chair the public launch of the Solomon and Mary Lar Leadership Institute scheduled for November.

Jonathan accepted the invitation when members of the institute’s Central Planning Committee paid him a courtesy visit at the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation in Abuja.

Speaking during the visit, the former president stressed the importance of leadership to sustainable development in Nigeria and across Africa, calling for renewed attention to leadership recruitment, training and development.

He said Nigeria needed to review its leadership structures to ensure they delivered greater impact and tangible benefits to citizens.

Jonathan, who is internationally recognised for his role in promoting peace and democratic values following his acceptance of defeat in the 2015 presidential election, commended the contributions of the late Chief Solomon Daushep Lar to Nigeria’s democratic development.

He recalled Lar’s role in leading the G-34, a group of prominent Nigerians that challenged the military regime of the late General Sani Abacha and demanded a return to democratic governance.

The former president also praised Lar for resigning from Abacha’s cabinet, where he served as a federal minister, describing him as a courageous statesman and an “emancipator of the minorities.”

Jonathan equally paid tribute to the nonagenarian matriarch of the Lar family and founder of the institute, Prof. Mary Lar, who was part of the delegation.

He described her as an exemplary mother and leader whose vision for the institute would contribute to leadership development and mentorship in the country.

The former president further urged Nigeria to draw lessons from other democracies by strengthening leadership values and institutions at both the subnational and federal levels.

He cited the 2014 National Conference convened by his administration as one of the initiatives aimed at addressing critical national issues and improving governance.

Jonathan expressed satisfaction with the establishment of the institute, noting that its objectives aligned with the commitment of his foundation to mentorship and democratic development.

He said the institute had the potential to make meaningful contributions to strengthening democracy and preparing future leaders for responsible service.

Members of the delegation included former Deputy Governor of Kogi State, Dr. Philip Salawu; former Director General of the National Council of Women Societies and former member of the House of Representatives, Dr. Dorgu; Alhaji Abubakar Rimi Jnr; and Hon. Beni Lar, a five-term member of the House of Representatives and daughter of Chief Solomon and Prof. Mary Lar.

Others were the Chairman of the Central Planning Committee, Hon. Bimbo Daramola; Mrs. Amina Okeke; and Mr Ilya, secretary of the committee.

The November 24 launch is expected to formally introduce the institute and its leadership development vision to the public.

World.title: AICL GMD, Tamuno Seeks Stronger Diaspora Investment in Africa
World.content:
The Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Abuja Investments Company Limited (AICL), Her Excellency, Ambassador Maureen Tamuno, has called for stronger partnerships between Africa and its diaspora to accelerate investment, facilitate skills transfer, create jobs and promote sustainable economic development across the continent.

Tamuno made the call on Thursday while delivering the keynote address at the seventh Diaspora Africa Conference, held at the Afreximbank Africa Trade Centre, Abuja, under the theme, ‘Homecoming: Bridging the Divide from Diaspora to Africa’s Future’.

She said homecoming should go beyond reconnecting with ancestral roots to building lasting relationships through productive investments, knowledge exchange, enterprise development and initiatives capable of improving livelihoods.

Drawing on her experience as Nigeria’s former High Commissioner to Jamaica, with concurrent accreditation to Haiti, Belize and the Dominican Republic, Tamuno stressed that diaspora engagement should extend beyond financial remittances to include professional expertise, international networks, entrepreneurship and technology transfer.

She identified trust, capital, skills, identity and policy as five critical bridges required to strengthen collaboration between Africans at home and abroad.

According to her, transparency, accountability and reliable institutions are essential to attracting diaspora investments. She urged governments to make investment information accessible, digitise public systems and ensure that transactions are transparent and independently verifiable.

“Patriotism should inspire an investment; it must never replace due diligence. Shared ancestry does not guarantee financial return,” she said, advocating structured investments backed by clear agreements, proper documentation and effective accountability mechanisms.

The AICL chief executive highlighted investment opportunities across the company’s portfolio, including real estate, markets, public infrastructure, transportation, entertainment and the creative economy. She invited diaspora entrepreneurs, investors and institutions to explore mutually beneficial partnerships with AICL to unlock opportunities within the Federal Capital Territory.

She also advocated a shift from the traditional emphasis on remittances for consumption towards structured investments that generate financial returns while delivering social and economic benefits.

Tamuno called for stronger collaboration in professional training, research, technology and enterprise development, noting that diaspora professionals could contribute through mentoring, knowledge exchange and partnerships without necessarily relocating permanently to Nigeria.

She further stressed the importance of including women, young people and persons with disabilities in investment opportunities, leadership, technical training and enterprise ownership, saying Africa’s development must provide inclusive opportunities for all.

To translate the conference’s resolutions into measurable outcomes, Tamuno proposed a Homecoming Partnership Compact to track progress over the next 12 months. The proposed framework would monitor partnerships established, enterprises supported, people trained and jobs sustained.

She said the success of diaspora engagement should be measured not by announcements and promises alone, but by functioning businesses, responsible investments and tangible improvements in people’s lives.

Tamuno urged Africans at home and abroad to embrace shared responsibility in building a prosperous continent, stressing that trust, mutual respect and sustained collaboration were essential to creating an Africa that future generations would be proud to call home.

“Let this seventh edition mark a movement from recognition to relationship, from relationship to responsibility, and from responsibility to results.We cannot undo the journeys that divided us. But we can choose the partnerships that shape our future.” she added.

World.title: ‘We’re already paying high taxes’: South Africans push back on grants demand
World.content:
Adult woman working with receipts and a bright pink calculator at a desk, focusing on finances. Image: Pexels

The call for a larger SASSA grant has reopened an old wound in South Africa: the feeling among working people that they already carry too much of the country’s financial burden.

On The South African’s Facebook page, many commenters supported older persons in principle but questioned how the country could pay for a major increase.

The cost question about the grants demand

Simm Vuzi put it plainly. “No offence but who’s footing that bill, we’re already paying high taxes as it is,” he wrote.



Franza von Horsten asked the same question in fewer words: “Where will all the money come from?”

Their concern is not about pensioners themselves. It is about the pressure on salaries, fuel, food and electricity that working households already face. Any sharp increase to the older person’s grant, currently R2 400 per month would require billions more in government spending.

Doubt over delivery

Others doubted the idea would ever move beyond social media. Steve Benton wrote: “Carry on dreaming.”

Fred Denysen added: “Wish upon a star.”

These comments reveal deep distrust in government’s ability to manage public money, even among those who sympathise with pensioners.

A different solution

Jacques Burger offered an alternative that shifts the focus from grants to tax. “If you retire after paying tax your whole working life you should be exempted from any further taxes,” he wrote.



His idea would help retirees living on private pensions and savings, who still pay tax on that income after decades of contributions.

The debate shows a country caught in the middle. South Africans want older persons to live with dignity, but many fear the bill will land, once again, on those still working.

World.title: DJ Sox’s 10-year-old son Busa Sokhela laid to rest [video]
World.content:
Busa Sokhela, the ten-year-old son of esteemed South African DJ and music producer DJ Sox and his wife, Gloria Sokhela, has been laid to rest following a battle with pneumonia.

The young boy was on life support for two months before his passing. Despite the devastating loss, DJ Sox remains proud of his son’s courage throughout his illness.

DJ SOX MOURNS THE PASSING OF HIS SON BUSA SOKHELA

DJ Sox penned a lengthy and deeply personal caption on Instagram in which he opened up about the pain of losing his beloved son.



He also placed his faith in God and prayed that his son would rest peacefully among the angels.

“No parent can ever be ready for the pain of losing a child so young. I miss you more than words can explain, and it hurts knowing I won’t get to hold you again,” he wrote.

“Even through this heartbreak, I trust God and His will, though I may not understand it. I believe you are resting safely in His loving arms and that you will be one of His beautiful angels,” he added.

The Uyozisholo Wena hitmaker also thanked their friends for the outpouring of love and support, including the doctors and nurses who cared for Busa and pulled out all the stops to save his life.

“To all our friends who supported my wife and me through this difficult time, thank you. Your love, prayers and kindness have helped carry us through, and we are deeply grateful,” he wrote.



“To all the doctors who did their best to save Busa’s life, and the nurses who cared for him throughout these two months, thank you from the bottom of our hearts. We deeply appreciate your dedication, compassion, and every effort you made to save our boy,” he added.

BUSA SOKHELA’S AUNT PENS TOUCHING TRIBUTE

Siphelele Sokhela, Busa’s aunt found the strength to share moments from his funeral.

In a lengthy Instagram post, she also shared how she is leaning on her faith in God as the family navigates life without Busa.

“Busa, you were only here for a little while, but you gave us a lifetime of love. Our family will never be the same without you,” she wrote.

“I pray that God carries us through the days when the grief feels unbearable and that, somehow, we learn to live with this emptiness,” she added.

CELEBRITIES ATTEND BUSA SOKHELA’S FUNERAL

DJ Cndo, Zakes Bantwini, Lindelani Mkhize, and Tbo Touch were among the notable industry peers who attended Busa’s funeral service on 15 October 2026.

After the service, DJ Cndo shared the following message on Instagram:

“We laid to rest our precious little nephew, Busa. To @djsoxsa and @mrsgee_sokhela, may God give you strength, comfort, and peace during this incredibly difficult time.”

World.title: Stormers batter Bristol Bears in seven-try Champions Cup rout
World.content:
The Stormers turned on the style to open their European Investec Champions Cup campaign with a commanding 49-12 victory over the Bristol Bears in Cape Town on Saturday.

Like all fixtures across the rugby community today, the pre-game build-up was an emotionally charged affair following the sudden and untimely passing of Lions lock Hyron Andrews. As expected, the Stormers and Bears, along with the relatively good crowd, held a moment of silence for the 31-year-old before the action kicked off.

And when it did, it was the visitors who enjoyed the better start across the opening five minutes or so, but once the Stormers overcame the early onslaught and settled into a rhythm of their own, there was nothing Bristol could do to stem the tidal wave.



The three standout features from today’s encounter were the Stormers’ dominant scrum, their clinical execution when in the red zone and Sacha Feinberg-Mngozulu’s near-perfect place-kicking display (seven from eight), the last which have been inconsistent in the early stages of the URC.

FIRST HALF RECAP: STORMERS KEEP BEARS AT BAY AND THEN FIRE

Bristol made a fast start, depriving the Stormers of the ball and instead forcing them into defence mode. Unfortunately for English Premiership side, the failure to turn that early dominance into points cost them dearly later in the game.

Because the Stormers’ fetchers were limited at the breakdown up to that point, it took a special solo turnover effort by Seabelo Senatla to hand them possession of the ball. They set an attacking lineout and from there, Senatla was put into a gap, turned on the afterburners and dotted down in the corner for the opening touchdown.



Moments later, the Stormers thought they were in again, after a quickly taken throw-in saw Cobus Reinach scuttle away untouched, but they were brought back for a knock-on as Leolin Zas lost control of the ball before Reinach pounced. That, however, was only a momentary reprieve for the visitors, as the Stormers secured turnover possession against the scrum feed and set a lineout before their driving maul was brought down, earning them yet another penalty. From the resultant scrum, they spread the ball to Senatla, who stepped three would-be defenders before freeing up Zas for the Stormers’ second.

Flank Joe Owen pulled a try back for the visitors, but the Stormers would cross the whitewash again with Feinberg-Mngomezulu slotting the conversion to maintain his perfect record off the kicking tee.

The Stormers did hit a bump in the road when hooker JJ Kotze was given a straight red card for a for a head-high tackle. But luckily for the hosts, being a man down didn’t cost as the defence held firm until the half-time break.



SECOND HALF RECAP: STORMERS CLOSE OUT WELL

The second half had the same pattern as the first; Bristol started brightly, only this time they actually managed to score, through replacement hooker Sol Moody.

Bristol continued asking tough questions of the Stormers defence, but the hosts stood their ground from there. Reinach read play beautifully to snatch a long pass out of the air and run away to score against the run of play, but his try was disallowed for a high tackle.

While it would have been a wonderful feat and just reward for the scrumhalf himself, it made little to no difference in the wider scheme of things as Jonny Roche would eventually score the sought-after fourth try to guarantee a bonus-point win for the Stormers.



There was a late blitzkrieg of tries by Warrick Gelant, Andre-Hugo Venter and Zas to capped off a resounding all-round performance.

World.title: These retirement-friendly South African cruises are affordable
World.content:
When you reach retirement age, it makes sense to enjoy the golden years.

After decades in the workforce, it’s time to relax and explore.

But sometimes the budget can get in the way. Thankfully, cruises offer an affordable way to travel.



Affordable Cruises Offer All-Inclusive Holidays

With a cruise, you get accommodation, excursions, and food for one price.

For these reasons, cruises have become especially popular among retirees.

In South Africa, the most affordable cruises depart from Durban’s Nelson Mandela port.



From here, you can spend as little as R5 458 for an all-inclusive 4-night cruise to Mozambique.

Other cruises from the Nelson Mandela port include a 2-night round trip out to sea starting at R5 534.

Then there’s also a 3-night one-way trip to Cape Town starting at R5 889 per person.



Cape Town also has affordable cruises, just far fewer than Durban. These are local cruises or sea trips.

The most affordable cruise from Cape Town on MSC is a 3-night one-way cruise to Durban. The starting price is R6 401 per person.

Travelling to international waters from Cape Town, the cheapest cruise is a round-trip to Walvis Bay, Namibia. The 5-night cruise includes 2 days in Walvis Bay and starts at R12 235 per person.



For R8 068 from Durban, you can book a 4-night cruise to Mozambique that stops at two ports: Pomene and Portuguese Island.

Well-heeled travellers can explore more.

A one-way MSC Grand Voyages departs Durban on 1 April 2027 and journeys to Italy. The 26-day cruise includes stops in Reunion, Madagascar, Mauritius, Seychelles, Jordan, Egypt and Greece.



However, this trip costs R37 441 per person.

Cruising Affordably

To get an affordable cruise, look for last-minute deals.

You can save up to 30% by booking a cruise with one month’s notice.



That’s especially true if you couldn’t get an early-bird special.

Take the 4-night round-trip to Pomene, Mozambique. It costs R5 548 if you book for November. However, for a December booking, the costs jump to R7 668.

To further reduce your cruise costs, don’t buy packages if it’s your first time cruising. Rather, book a short, cheap cruise to test the waters.



Then, if you want to book future cruises, think about what you’ve learned from your first trip.

There are some standard packages that can make financial sense. Drink packages, for example, can make sense if they include bottled water.

You can also make the most out of your trip by analysing:



The Itinerary: Where are you stopping, how long will you be there, and what can you do?

Ask these questions before booking. The destination can be just as exciting as the journey. If it’s in a place you want to visit and the ship is docked for hours, you can venture farther than the port.

Number of Occupants: In South Africa, the MSC cruise ships operating (Armonia and Sinfonia) have a similar occupancy limit. They range from 976 to 990 occupants.



Ship size: How large is the ship? South Africa has access to two ships of roughly the same size. However, each is arranged differently. You might prefer one over the other.

World.title: Chiefs defended deep, still conceded in Confederation Cup loss to Red Arrows
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs fail to defend against Red Arrows in a 0-1 Confederation Cup loss in Zambia. Image: Kaizer Chiefs (X).

Kaizer Chiefs were looking to make history against Red Arrows today (17 October).

Instead, the Amakhosi are trailing after a 0-1 loss in the CAF Confederation Cup second preliminary round.

Here’s what went down at the Levy Mwanawasa Stadium in Ndola.



Kaizer Chiefs vs Red Arrows not shown live

The club confirmed today (17 October) that the match would not be broadcast.

Chiefs said this was due to Red Arrows being unable to provide the SABC with the means to air the game.

Updates were instead relegated to live coverage by social media and live scoring sites.



The lack of updates on the match frustrated fans on social media.

Some questioned if Chiefs were losing, while others debated the XI for the first leg.

The Amakhosi relied on a strong defensive unit, as confirmed on social media.



CAF Confederation Cup: Second Preliminary Round 1st Leg: Red Arrows vs. Kaizer Chiefs



Starting 11: Leaner, Monyane, Miguel, Moloisane, Cross, Mako, Frosler, Mthethwa, Shabalala, Vilakazi, Baartman



Subs: Bvuma, Dortley, Nkgwesa, Mabaso, Velebayi, Abrahams, Ighodaro, Da Silva,… pic.twitter.com/rtAIgTYqKp — Kaizer Chiefs (@KaizerChiefs) October 17, 2026

Chiefs announced their starting lineup as follows:

Leaner; Cross, Moloisane, Miguel, Monyana; Mako, Frosler, Mthethwa, Vilakazi; Shabalala, Baartman.



How the game went down

Chiefs lost Thabiso Monyane early in the game due to an injury.

Thulani Mabaso replaced him after just half an hour, marking yet another concern for Fernando da Cruz.

The game remained goalless after the first 45 minutes.



Flavio da Silva replaced Luke Baartman as the teams came on for the second half.

Mfundo Vilakazi and Mduduzi Shabalala were replaced by Wandile Duba and Etiosa Ighodaro at 71 minutes.

5 minutes later, Red Arrows opened the scoring with a Alassane Diarra header from a corner set piece.



The game ended in a lacklustre 0-1 win for the hosts, taking a lead into the second leg on 23 October.

Chiefs now need to salvage a win at the FNB Stadium to keep their Confederation Cup dream alive.

World.title: ‘Exempted from any further taxes’: Pensioners make bold demand
World.content:
South Africans who spent their working lives paying tax believe retirement should come with a reward, and one commenter has called for a change that would put more money back in pensioners’ pockets.

The suggestion emerged during a lively debate about pensions on The South African’s Facebook page.

A clean break from tax

Jacques Burger proposed a bold solution. “If you retire after paying tax your whole working life you should be exempted from any further taxes,” he wrote.



His comment speaks to retirees who live on private pensions, retirement annuities or savings and still see tax deducted from that income. SARS already gives older taxpayers some relief through higher tax thresholds from age 65 and again from 75, but many retirees feel these concessions fall short when living costs keep climbing.

‘They paid their taxes’

Marianna De Bruin Schmidt backed the idea that older persons have already done their part. “I agree these pensioners paid their taxes so deserve to have a decent liveable pension,” she wrote.

Shantell Scheepers argued that seniors deserve far more than they currently receive: “In my opinion Seniors the eldery should have the full right to R6000.”



Their views highlight two groups of older South Africans who feel let down: those relying on private income who want lower taxes, and those depending on the Older Persons Grant, which increased to R2 400 per month from April 2026.

Working South Africans push back

Not everyone agreed. Simm Vuzi warned that someone must carry the cost. “No offence but who’s footing that bill, we’re already paying high taxes as it is,” he wrote.

Franza von Horsten asked: “Where will all the money come from?”



Their concern points to a hard truth. Every tax break for retirees and every grant increase shifts more of the burden onto a shrinking pool of working taxpayers.

The debate leaves government with a difficult balancing act: honouring the contribution of older South Africans while keeping the tax system fair for those still in the workforce.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs fall in Zambia, Orlando Pirates put one foot into the next round
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs, competing in the CAF Confederation Cup, have suffered a 1-0 defeat to Zambia’s Red Arrows, while Orlando Pirates secured a 1-0 win over African Stars.

KAIZER CHIEFS IN THE CAF CONFEDERATION CUP

Falling to Arrows at the Levy Mwanawasa Stadium, coach Fernando Da uz had opted for a cautious approach. His defensively structured lineup keet the hosts at bay throughout the first half.

Alassane Diarra scored in the 76th minute after Amakhosi had resisted Red Arrows for much of the match, which was not televised. As a result, Kaizer Chiefs must now overturn the deficit in the second leg.



Meanwhile, Amakhosi will host the Zambian side at Durban’s Moses Mabhida Stadium on Friday, 23 October. Kick-off will be at 18:00.Victory for Kaizer Chiefs will secure a place in the final 16 group stage.

How Kaizer Chiefs lined-up: Renaldo Leaner, Thabiso Monyane, Inacio Miguel, Thabo Moloisane, Bradley Cross, Paseka Mako, Reeve Frosler, Sibongiseni Mthethwa, Mduduzi Shabalala, Mfundo Vilakazi, Luke Baartman

Substitutes: Bruce Bvuma, Rushwin Dortley, Kabelo Nkgwesa, Thulani Mabaso, Asanele Velebayi, Faiz Abrahams, Etiosa Ighodaro, Flavio Da Silva, Wandile Duba.

ORLANDO PIRATES IN THE CAF CHAMPIONS LEAGUE

In contrast, Orlando Pirates laboured into a 1-0 victory over Namibian champions African Stars. The game was played at the Botswana National Stadium in Gaborone, as Namibia has no CAF-approved venues.

Abdeslam Ouaddou’s Bucs struggled to find a breakthrough in a closely contested first half, with both teams creating half-chances. The decisive moment arrived in the 78th minute. Tshepang Moremi found the back of the net. His goal handed the Buccaneers a valuable first-leg advantage ahead of the return fixture in Soweto next Saturday.
