World.title: Trump’s new press secretary says China lacked ‘proper’ toilets
World.content:
Washington – White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia, who was appointed less than a week ago, said China lacked “proper toilets” in an interview that aired on Thursday.

Zacharia, 41, is already under scrutiny over her legal credentials, after giving an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the United States.

The press secretary, who previously lived in China, recalled in an interview that the perception in 2016 was that China would soon overtake the United States.

“We were all being told Hillary (Clinton) was going to win. The golden days or the glory days of America were over. That China was on the horizon,” Zacharia told right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec.

“I remember this very distinctly, having just come from China, thinking, ‘How is China the next country on the horizon? They don’t even have proper toilets,” she added.

There was no immediate comment from Chinese authorities.

Trump has boasted about his “great relationship” with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

During a Washington summit in September, the two leaders discussed topics ranging from AI and trade to the stalled war in Iran, and confirmed that they would meet for a third and fourth time this year.

Zacharia held her first White House press briefing on Tuesday and only answered questions from three journalists.

She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, a loyal Trump supporter and often combative spokesperson, who stepped down in August to care for her young children.

Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit. She also said she had worked at a law firm in Beijing.

Asked about her legal background on Thursday, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was then “distracted and overwhelmed” by plans to move with her husband to China.

Zacharia said that she did not retake the bar exam upon returning to the United States due to the birth of her first child.

World.title: Indonesian stocks dive 11% as MSCI weighs market reclassification
World.content:
Jakarta – Indonesian stocks plunged more than 11 percent Friday as index compiler MSCI said it was “no longer appropriate” to maintain the country’s emerging-market status, fuelling fears of an exodus of foreign investment.

The US firm said earlier this year that investors had raised concerns about “ongoing opacity in shareholding structures” as well as co-ordinated trading behaviour that affected price information.

Authorities in Jakarta said in April they had completed reforms, hoping to avoid the downgrade, which could deal a blow to government efforts to kickstart Southeast Asia’s biggest economy, and have a significant impact on investment decisions.

But on Friday MSCI said investors had indicated the “sufficient progress has not been observed consistently across the Indonesian equity market”.

“Despite the announced reforms, significant concerns remain around market dysfunction, including continued suspected coordinated trading behaviour and lack of evidence of meaningful enforcement.

“Accordingly, MSCI considers Indonesia’s continued classification as an Emerging Market no longer appropriate and is launching a consultation on a proposal to reclassify Indonesia as a Standalone Market.”

“A reclassification to Frontier Markets would not properly recognise the depth of the market problems,” it said.

A standalone classification could force investment funds tracking the MSCI’s emerging market indexes to sell Indonesian holdings.

Argentina, Lebanon and Palestine are among the markets with the designation, with none in Asia, according to Bloomberg.

The Jakarta Composite Index collapsed eight percent at the open, sparking a trading halt. When trading resumed it was down 11.1 percent, its heaviest fall since early 1998 and sitting at its lowest level since 2020.

The index has now fallen more than 40 percent since the start of the year.

– Rupiah weakens –

In reaction to the news, the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) said it “respects MSCI’s independence in assessing and determining market classification based on its proprietary methodology”.

“However, considering the various progress and reform measures that have been taken, the IDX will request further clarification from MSCI regarding the basis for the considerations and assessments behind this announcement.

“We also need to emphasise that this MSCI announcement is still part of the consultation process, with input being accepted until April 30, 2027, and does not constitute a final decision.”

The rupiah dropped about 0.8 percent against the dollar to sit at around around 18,060, having hit 18,209 in June, its weakest level on record.

Erwin Gunawan Hutapea, the Indonesian central bank’s head of monetary management and securities, said the bank would take action to ensure stability of the rupiah, which had already tumbled around eight percent this year to a record low.

“Amid rising global risk-off sentiment, which has driven US dollar strengthening and put pressure on domestic financial markets, capital outflows from domestic portfolio assets are expected to continue.

“Bank Indonesia is committed to maintaining a presence in the market to uphold Rupiah exchange rate stability in line with its fundamentals and to ensure that market mechanisms function properly.”

The central bank had carried out several rate hikes earlier in the year to shore up the rupiah, after it came under pressure over the state of Southeast Asia’s biggest economy.

The bank is due to hold its next monetary policy meeting on Wednesday.

New York-based MSCI produces international indexes used by investors as a benchmark to balance their portfolios.

It has a significant impact on investment decisions through its flagship emerging markets index, which contains 1,200 companies with a market capitalisation more than $10 trillion.

Fund managers worldwide keep a close eye on what countries are included or excluded in MSCI’s indexes as that can trigger adjustments to their portfolios.

World.title: Iraq’s parliament approves new cabinet ministers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — On Thursday, Iraq’s parliament confirmed 11 cabinet nominees and three deputy prime ministers, including Laith al-Khazali, a key member in Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq who faces US terrorist sanctions.

The nomination is a politically risky decision for Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, whose administration is dealing with strained regional ties and severe economic challenges as a result of the continuing US-Israeli war against Iran.

Al-Khazali is the brother of Qais al-Khazali, the commander of Asaib Ahl al-Haq, which Washington listed as a foreign terrorist organization in 2020.

Both brothers were classified as specially designated global terrorists, and the US Treasury sanctioned them individually in 2019 for suspected participation in violence against Iraqi demonstrators.

Their US designations also included references to assaults on American troops, such as a 2007 operation that killed five US soldiers.

The parliamentary decision raises concerns about al-Khazali’s nomination and its ramifications for Baghdad’s relationship with Washington, especially as al-Zaidi wants to reinforce Iraq’s sovereignty and manage ties with neighboring nations.

World.title: ‘Mixed feelings’: AI cracks centuries-old ciphers
World.content:
Tokyo – Napoleon Bonaparte ordered the wartime missive written in code, creating a puzzle that went unsolved for more than 200 years — until AI cracked it in a matter of hours.

Artificial intelligence is helping non-specialists unlock the secrets of historical sources, a trend described as a “turning point” in a field previously the preserve of scholars and dedicated hobbyists.

One new sleuth is Carter Church, a 27-year-old AI engineer who decrypted a 19th-century letter to one of Napoleon’s generals.

Without digital tools, the task could have taken weeks, but the latest model from ChatGPT-maker OpenAI broke the cipher in just six hours.

“What AI mostly brings is persistence,” Church told AFP, saying he felt “an unbelievable sense of satisfaction and excitement when I saw the result”.

The message from 1809 — detailing French and allied troops’ positions in two dozen lines of symbols, numbers and letters — had lain ignored in an online academic archive.

Because traditional, low-tech methods to crack ciphers are effective but time- and labour-intensive, historians “have more important problems to solve, so many ciphers like this often sit unattended”, said Church.

To find the solution, Church, who works at US cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, needed to learn “very little” about code-breaking techniques or the historical period.

He spent some evenings going over it, then consulted Japanese patent engineer Satoshi Tomokiyo, who maintains an online list of unsolved ciphers, to verify it.

“2026 will be remembered as a turning point for codebreaking of historical ciphers,” Tomokiyo wrote on his website Cryptiana, a go-to resource for the small but enthusiastic global community of amateur cryptographers.

– ‘Mixed feelings’ –

Researchers were already developing AI models to break ciphers, but the public release of state-of-the-art generalist tools has unleashed dozens of new solutions.

Although Church used OpenAI’s most powerful model, GPT-6 Astra, other people have used top offerings from rival US lab Anthropic instead.

Tomokiyo said that since mid-September, most of the ciphers on his list have been cracked using AI.

“There remain some tough problems” which could stay an enigma for years to come, because there is less relevant data available to help AI figure them out, the 58-year-old told AFP.

“I’m excited long-time problems are now solved, but on the other hand, I have mixed feelings, because AI seems to have solved these difficult problems so easily,” he said.

With technology draining the satisfaction of being first to crack a cipher, a fellow code-breaker told Tomokiyo: “I feel useless.”

AI is surpassing human abilities in pursuits from mathematics to computer programming, while threatening to alter or even eradicate many jobs.

The technology is transforming the work of historians not only by decoding documents, but also by analysing millions of medieval manuscripts or helping read ancient scrolls.

Too fragile to be unrolled without risking destruction, the Herculaneum Papyri — hundreds of papyrus scrolls carbonised in the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 AD — are now being X-rayed and analysed by AI to reveal the hidden writing inside.

Researchers in Italy announced in June the first complete virtual unrolling of a scroll, which turned out to be a treatise on ethics.

– ‘Facebook of the past’ –

AI is also being used to build a huge, searchable collection of previously inaccessible sources on Jewish history and culture by transcribing 10 million pages of Hebrew manuscripts.

“It’s gigantic. No human being could process such a quantity” of data, said project leader Daniel Stoekl Ben Ezra, of the Ecole Pratique des Hautes Etudes in Paris.

Researchers hope the databases created using the digitised text — which he likens to a kind of “huge Facebook of the past” — could help bring to light links between people, places and ideas.

And at the French capital’s Notre Dame Cathedral, an AI system has been trained to transcribe 14,600 Latin pages from the church’s medieval archives — a task not dissimilar to code-breaking.

“These are minutes drawn up by notaries who abbreviate their decisions. The script is highly administrative, very pragmatic… with rather technical vocabulary,” said historian Julie Claustre, who leads the e-NDP project.

With character recognition rates ranging between 88 and 94 percent, the project has revealed information about the cathedral’s daily life, its building work, its staff and the care of abandoned children.

Doing the same by hand would take “several decades”, said Claustre, but “it’s not just a time-saver”.

Automation enables “inquiries that were not previously possible; it transforms the conditions of research.”

Indian pilot Smit Machchhar who was attacked by his co-pilot aboard a Flydubai flight has recalled how a routine journey turned into a fight for survival, describing the repeated blows to his head, his attempts to call for help and the moments he lost consciousness as the aircraft went into a dive.after he was stabbed by his Omani copilot Hamam Al Hammami who was allegedly trying to crash the plane.In an exclusive 1st news interview after being stabbed, with Sky News Arabia, Captain Smith Machchhar said there had been nothing unusual about the flight until about two hours after take-off. He was carrying out routine checks in the cockpit when the attack began, initially mistaking the first blow to the back of his head for damage to the aircraft.Giving out details as he remembered he said, "when I was just in in the checking my computer for the timing and everything, uh suddenly there was a a very hard hit at the back of my head, right here. And uh it was quite hard and felt that it was something which was very strong."He said he initially thought something had broken off the aircraft's roof and hit him, causing catastrophic damage. Drawing on his training, he tried to regain his composure and check the aircraft's systems. âMy thought process went on that track, that oh, there is a big damage in the aircraft which has hit me at the back,â he said.But within seconds, he realised he was being attacked. âHe kept on hitting,â Machchhar said.He recalled turning around and realising what was happening, although the impact had severely restricted his field of vision.âImmediately, I would say in the next few seconds, my vision was restricted to like few inches,â he said, adding that he learnt about the extent of the impact from doctors later.His first response was to protect himself from further blows. He quickly unbuckled his seatbelt, turned around and tried to block the attack, sustaining an injury to his hand. âAt this point, it was very obvious what was going on,â he said.Machchhar said he immediately tried to get help from another captain who was on board and was expected to operate the return flight. âI was screaming his name and I was trying because the switch was very close to me to open the door. I was trying to just get help in,â he said.He lost consciousness amid the commotion but remembered managing to open the cockpit door. He could hear shouting as the other crew members confronted the co-pilot. âThe door shut immediately after that because he threatened to hit them as well,â Machchhar said.By then, he was struggling to stay conscious and could feel his strength fading because of blood loss. Soon afterwards, he heard the engine sounds change and felt the aircraft go into a dive. âSince Iâve been flying for such a long time, I donât have to see the instruments to figure out or hear the engine to know whatâs happening,â he said.Machchhar said he repeatedly drifted in and out of consciousness but realised he had to fight to survive. âThere was a moment where I realised and I told myself that, âSmith, do something. You canât die like this,ââ he said.His memories of what happened next remain fragmented. He recalled trying to reach the door, bracing his leg against something and pushing himself forward.âThe next memory that I have is the doorâs open and Iâm lying between the cockpit and the galley,â he said. He remembered being face down as panic and shouting continued around him.While Machchhar was fighting to survive, another captain took over the controls and helped save the aircraft. âThe other thing, how my other colleague who took over the controls and saved the day again is commendable. Itâs something that Iâll keep with me till I die,â he said.Asked what he wanted people to understand about the incident amid speculation over how the plane was saved, Machchhar said everyone on board had done what they could.âI think everyone in world everyone in world did the best in their capacity to save the day,â he said. The pilot said the first blow continued to haunt him in the days after the attack.âImmediately after the event, I used to get flashes of the first hit. And trust me, it shook me up for the first few days,â he said, describing how the memory would return suddenly and leave his heart racing.But what stayed with him most was the determination of those on board. âOne thing that I would take away from that day was the determination, the sheer determination of everyone to survive,â he said.Machchhar said he felt out of danger only when the aircraft touched down in Saudi Arabia. By then, a doctor was attending to him in the galley, while crew members worked to keep him conscious.Asked whom he thought of first, he replied: âMy son.â His two-year-old son, wife and daughter live with him in the UAE.Machchhar also expressed gratitude for the medical treatment he received in Saudi Arabia and after being brought back to the UAE. âFrom the first day onwards, the way I was taken care of, the way I was brought back to the UAE, even the care that I was given in Saudi is something I would never forget in my life,â he said.Still recovering from the traumatic incident, he said he felt grateful for the care and support he had received over the preceding two-and-a-half weeks.âGrateful is the word I would say right now,â he said.

World.title: 'Thoughts with those who have lost their loved ones': PM Modi on Kolkata stampede
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday expressed grief over the deaths of 17 people and injuries to 15 others in the Kolkata pandal incident, calling it âextremely distressingâ.

PM Modi also announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh from the Prime Ministerâs National Relief Fund (PMNRF) for the next of kin of each deceased person and Rs 50,000 for each injured person.

"The stampede in Kolkata is extremely distressing. My thoughts are with those who have lost their loved ones. May the injured recover at the earliest. The local administration is providing all possible assistance to those affected," PM Modi was quoted by PMO on X.

"The Prime Minister has announced an ex-gratia of Rs. 2 lakh from PMNRF would be given to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives. The injured would be given Rs. 50,000," the PMO wrote.

The incident occurred around 7.40 pm in the Girish Park police station area amid heavy crowds of pandal visitors and rainfall.

As rain began, people waiting outside the pandal rushed forward, causing some to fall on the road and triggering a stampede, a senior police officer told PTI.





All the injured were rescued and taken to Calcutta Medical College for treatment.

An eyewitness told ANI, âMany people lost consciousness; some were being taken on motorcycles. I witnessed this happening all aroundâwhen people fainted, they were taken away on bikes. All of this took place, and there was a massive crowd as well...â

World.title: Kolkata pandal stampede: Heavy rush amid rain led to deadly incident - top developments
World.content:
NEW DELHI: At least 17 died, and 15 were injured after a stampede-like situation errupted at the Sarada Park (Chor Bagan) Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata, officials said on Saturday.

The incident occurred around 7.40pm at the exit gate under Girish Park police station as heavy crowds gathered amid rainfall.

Earlier, police had said that around 35 people were taken to Calcutta Medical College and Hospital (MCH) for treatment.

Following the incident, authorities have issued two helpline numbers through the Lalbazar Control Room for assistance related to the incident: 18003455678 and 03322141310.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi's office announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh for the next of kin of the dead, while Rs 50,000 to be given to the injured victims of the pandal stampede.

"The Prime Minister has announced an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh from PMNRF would be given to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives. The injured would be given Rs 50,000," the statement said.

What happened at the pandal?

According to police, the crowd surge occurred as rain began to fall on Saturday evening.





People waiting outside the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal rushed forward, causing some to fall on the road and triggering a stampede-like situation.

Also Read:

West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said that at least 17 people lost their lives and 15 were injured, according to news agency PTI.

Earlier, in an official update, police said, "Today at around 7.40 pm, a stampede occurred at the exit gate of Sarada Park (Chor Bagan) Puja Pandal, under Girish Park Police Station, due to heavy crowds of pandal hoppers amid rainfall.

The Puja Pandal has now been closed to visitors. All injured persons were rescued and shifted to MCH for treatment. As per the information received so far, approximately 35 persons have been shifted to MCH.

"

Administration response

West Bengal health minister Sharadwat Mukherjee visited the injured at Calcutta Medical College and Hospital. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari and chief secretary Manoj Agarwal also visited the hospital to meet those receiving treatment.

Disaster management personnel were deployed at the site, police said. The pandal was closed to visitors following the incident.

Leaders' reaction

Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed his concerns over the distressing situation. He extended his thoughts and prayers to the kins and victims who lost their lives, while wished a speedy recovery to the injured.

World.title: NCB busts two synthetic drug labs in Greater Noida, seizes drugs worth Rs 50 crore
World.content:
A huge haul of Methamphetamine worth around Rs 50 crores, precursors and manufacturing equipment.

recovery of nearly 380 kg of amphetamine-containing materialâ encompassing crystalline, semi-crystalline, and liquid forms

The premises were heavily equipped with large-capacity heating mantles, glass reaction vessels, filtration machinery, and laboratory apparatus tailored for mass production.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a significant crackdown on illicit drugs network in Delhi-NCR, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has busted two clandestine synthetic-drug manufacturing laboratories in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, seizing a huge haul of Methamphetamine worth around Rs 50 crores, precursors and manufacturing equipment.Union home minister Amit Shah termed the operation as a 'major milestone'. "It is a remarkable example of intelligence-led enforcement and a testament to our commitment to eliminating drug cartels before December 2029," he said in a post on X.The raid, conducted under Op Crystal Hunt on Oct 16 2026 at village Jahanabad Kadalpur in Gautam Buddha Nagar, led to the recovery of nearly 380 kg of amphetamine-containing materialâ encompassing crystalline, semi-crystalline, and liquid forms â alongside 10 kg of pseudoephedrine and large quantities of precursor chemicals such as acetone, toluene, and hydrochloric acid.According to officials, the seized materials are projected to yield over 56 kg of finished crystalline amphetamine. The premises were heavily equipped with large-capacity heating mantles, glass reaction vessels, filtration machinery, and laboratory apparatus tailored for mass production.Two individuals have been arrested in connection with the operation. One suspect identified himself as Destiny Abraham Dumbiri, a Nigerian national.However, immigration checks revealed he entered India in January 2020 under the alias Francis Kalokoh using a tourist visa that expired in December of that year, underscoring the sophisticated tactics used by traffickers to evade law enforcement.The second accused, Ms Lallawmzuali, alias Olivia Lalchawimawii, a resident of Mizoram, was out on bail following an earlier arrest in March 2026 by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence in Goa for allegedly possessing a commercial quantity of heroin.This latest operation builds upon the NCB's ongoing efforts to dismantle organized cartels, echoing a previous October 2024 raid in the Kasna Industrial Area that exposed suspected ties to the Mexican cartel CÃ¡rtel de Jalisco Nueva GeneraciÃ³n.Investigators are tracing the financial trails, chemical procurement channels, and broader distribution networks associated with the arrested pair to uncover further interstate and international links.Beyond the direct threat of narcotics, authorities emphasized the severe environmental and public health hazards posed by such hidden facilities, noting that the untreated discharge of chemical waste severely contaminates local soil, drainage systems, and water bodies.The NCB has issued a strong public appeal urging landlords, property dealers, housing societies, and Resident Welfare Associations to remain vigilant. "Citizens are encouraged to report suspicious indicators such as unusual chemical odors, unexplained storage of drums, or heavy lab equipment to the National Narcotics Helpline MANAS at 1933, reinforcing the nation's collective stride toward a Nasha Mukt Bharat," the NCB said.

World.title: Man killed, four injured in suspected militant attack on Kuki village in Manipur
World.content:
Violence has been escalating in Manipur

A 36-year old man was killed and four others injured after suspected militants attacked Chassad village in Manipur's Kamjong district on Saturday, triggering an exchange of fire between the assailants and a local armed group, police said.Several rounds were fired at the Kuki village around 2.30 pm, and the gunfight was continuing in the evening, a senior police officer said, according to PTI."Village head Thangjahou Haokip (48), and four others - Khailun Haokip, Seikhohou, Hegin Haokip and Seipao Haokip - were injured after the suspected militants attacked the village. All the injured were taken to a hospital where Seikhohou succumbed to his injuries," the officer said."The gunfight is still underway in the evening," the officer added.The Committee on Tribal Unity condemned the attack and urged the state government to deploy central forces in the area.The latest violence comes amid broader reported cases of violence. The escalating clashes between Kuki-Zo and Naga communities, which have claimed more than 50 lives since February, with homes and shops torched and civilians caught in attacks across several districts.Last week, nine people, including six Nagas, two Kukis and a Gorkha farmer, were killed in a series of attacks across three districts in a 12-hour period. The violence included an attack on Chassad village and gunfights in Kangpokpi and Ukhrul districts. Houses and shops were also set on fire, prompting prohibitory orders in Kamjong and a shutdown call on National Highway 202.The situation remained tense on Thursday, when a Kuki-Zo woman, Hatneikim Haokip, was killed and her husband injured in an alleged ambush by suspected Naga militants on the road between Phaikoh and Aishu in Kamjong district. Two other people travelling with them were reported missing. The woman was reportedly travelling with the group to buy essential commodities.The violence has also affected Kamjong, Ukhrul, Kangpokpi, Tamenglong, Noney and other districts, raising concerns over security in the state and along the India-Myanmar border.

NEW DELHI: Congress workers vandalised the BJP office in Rajasthan's Ajmer on Saturday, pasting posters, smearing them with black ink and writing slogans on the walls to protest against state BJP president Madan Rathore's controversial remarks about Pakistan. World.title: Thane Police bust matrimonial fraud racket, arrest two men; ₹14.25 lakh cash, 311 grams of gold seized
World.content:
The Thane Police have arrested two men, including one on October 9, for allegedly cheating people through fake matrimonial profiles, promising marriage and persuading them to part with gold jewellery and cash. Police said the investigation has led to the detection of 19 cases registered across Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and Thane.

The accused have been identified as Dinesh Babu Manekar (39), a resident of Mahape in Navi Mumbai, and his alleged accomplice Suresh alias Babu Tanaji Mhatre (55), a resident of Chikhali in Raigad district.

According to police, the accused allegedly targeted unmarried women and men through matrimonial platforms. After establishing contact and gaining their trust, they would promise marriage and convince victims to hand over gold ornaments and cash before disappearing with the valuables.

The investigation began after a cheating case was registered at Badlapur West police station under Sections 318(4) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). During the investigation, police identified Manekar as a suspect and arrested him from Mahape, Navi Mumbai, on October 9.

Further investigation led police to Mr. Mhatre, who was subsequently arrested in Navi Mumbai. Police said the two accused were allegedly involved in similar offences across multiple jurisdictions.

During the operation, police recovered ₹14.25 lakh in cash and 311 grams of gold ornaments, collectively valued at approximately ₹24.24 lakh.

Police said the investigation has led to the detection of 19 offences, including 17 cases linked to the two arrested accused and two additional cases involving Manekar. These include cases registered at Badlapur West, Badlapur East, Ulhasnagar, Shivajinagar, Mulund, Panvel City and Koparkhairane police stations.

Investigators also found that Manekar had an extensive criminal record, with 29 serious offences, including robbery, theft, cheating and dacoity, registered against him across Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Mira-Bhayandar and Thane. Police said further investigation was underway to determine whether the accused were involved in additional offences.

The operation was carried out by the Ulhasnagar Crime Branch under the Thane Police Commissionerate, under the supervision of Thane Police Commissioner Ashutosh Dumbre and other senior officers.

World.title: Naga students’ body endorses tribe’s phased bar on ‘illegal immigrants’
World.content:
GUWAHATI

The Naga Students’ Federation (NSF) has backed the resolution adopted by the apex body of the Angami community to bar, in phases, “illegal immigrants” from working or renting property in areas under its jurisdiction.

The NSF has urged other Naga organisations to emulate the Angami Public Organisation (APO) in enforcing the Inner-Line Permit (ILP) and barring people of suspect nationality from working, offering services and renting houses.

Rooted in the Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, 1873, the ILP is a temporary travel document Indian citizens need to enter four frontier States (Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram, and Nagaland) in the north-eastern region.

An ILP-specific wing of the NSF said the APO’s phased approach would give indigenous and non-indigenous communities time to address illegal immigration and ensure that employment, services, documents and tenancy arrangements comply with the law.

“We are not opposed to non-indigenous people who enter, work, trade and reside in Nagaland legally. Our primary concern is illegal immigration and non-compliance with existing laws,” an NSF spokesperson said.

Announcing its phased bar on “illegal immigrants” on October 7, the APO said the decision was based on concerns over demographic changes and lax enforcement of existing regulations. It also asked Naga youth not to work for “illegal immigrants” as salespersons in shops or in any other capacity.

According to the APO resolution, Naga youth will not be permitted to work for “illegal immigrants” in any capacity from December 31, 2026. It also said that the Angami Youth Organisation has been tasked with enforcing this resolution after the deadline.

From March 31, 2027, the APO will prohibit the use of services of illegal immigrants as drivers, domestic workers or labourers. It has also directed that illegal immigrants must not use or operate any trade licence, PAN card, Aadhaar card, SIM card, permit or bank account issued in the name of an Angami individual.

The APO further said that Angami individuals will not be allowed to rent houses or lease land to “illegal immigrants” from July 31, 2027. It entrusted the Angami youth body with enforcing this restriction across the Angami areas in consultation with village councils.

The APO claimed the decadal growth rate of “illegal Bangladeshi immigrants” was 181.67%, while that of the indigenous communities was 20.44%.

World.title: Three compulsory P.T. periods a week for school students in Tamil Nadu: School Education Minister Rajmohan
World.content:
Schools in Tamil Nadu will now have three periods of physical education and two periods of extra curricular and co-curricular activities in a week, said School Education Minister Rajmohan while releasing a revised time table in Chennai on Tuesday (September 13, 2026).

Speaking to media persons, he said, “Now, there will be compulsory three periods of physical education, and the other two periods designated for extra curricular activities could also be converted to physical education periods, thereby ensuring that students can play all five days a week.” Mr. Rajmohan thanked the Chief Minister for the decision.

The Minister was holding a review meeting with all the District Education Officers on curriculum, hygiene and facilities of the schools in the districts.

Responding to a question about results of special Teacher Eligibility Tests, Mr. Rajmohan said that there are more attempts for the teachers to take up the exam, and they are working on providing a good support system for the teachers to take up the exam.

World.title: Visakhapatnam GVMC polls to use pink ballot for Mayor, white for corporator
World.content:
Voters in Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) elections will have to cast two separate votes – using a pink ballot paper to elect the Mayor and a white ballot paper to choose their ward corporator. Both ballot papers must be deposited in the same ballot box after voting, District Collector and Election Officer M. Abhishikth Kishore said on Saturday.

While polling for all 120 GVMC wards will be held from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. on October 28, counting of votes will begin at 8 a.m. on October 30. The district administration has made elaborate arrangements to ensure that the elections are conducted in a free, fair and peaceful manner, he said.

Addressing a press conference at the Collectorate in Visakhapatnam, Mr. Kishore said the GVMC has 18,37,901 voters. More than 10,000 polling personnel have been identified for election duty, and the first phase of training had been completed.

A total of 41 Returning Officers and 41 Assistant Returning Officers had been appointed. Polling personnel would be allocated duties through a randomisation process in accordance with the State Election Commission's guidelines, he said.

Ten distribution centres, one for each GVMC zone, had been established to facilitate the distribution of election materials. Nine buildings at Andhra University had been readied to accommodate strong rooms and counting halls. After polling, ballot boxes and other election materials would be shifted to the designated strong rooms and kept under security.

The administration had identified critical, sensitive and highly sensitive polling stations and was making additional security arrangements wherever necessary.

The Collector said the maximum election expenditure limit was fixed at ₹40 lakh for a Mayor candidate and ₹15 lakh for a corporator candidate.

Tight vigil

Police Commissioner Shankhabrata Bagchi said 6,607 police personnel would be deployed for the GVMC elections. Security arrangements would cover polling stations, strong rooms, distribution and reception centres, and other key locations.

The police would deploy route mobile teams, striking forces, checkposts, static pickets and shadow teams, besides establishing control rooms to monitor the election process. A total of 177 route mobile units and 16 static surveillance teams had been planned, he said.

Surveillance would be strengthened through photography, videography, CCTV cameras and drones. The police had identified potentially sensitive areas and were holding direct interactions with residents to prevent untoward incidents.

Three outreach programmes had already been conducted within the limits of the Two Town, Airport and Three Town police stations. More such meetings would be organised in the coming days to promote peaceful polling, the Commissioner added.

World.title: High-cost electricity to be purchased for 16 days to avoid unscheduled power cuts in Tamil Nadu: Energy Resources Minister
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Energy Resources Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) said a prolonged summer had led to a spurt in electricity demand in the State, and the Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL) had to resort to purchasing electricity at more than ₹30 per unit to avoid unscheduled power cuts.

Addressing the media, he said the current peak power demand was 21,000 MW when compared to 16,000 MW last year — a 30% increase due to the El Niño effect. He said the entire country was facing an energy shortage.

The Minister said that currently, gas power was the only source available, and it was being purchased at more than ₹30 per unit.

The expensive power was being purchased for managing the evening peak-hour demand for six hours from October 15 to 31, he added.

Mr. Nirmal Kumar said TNPDCL had to purchase expensive gas power owing to the central generating station at Neyveli Lignite Corporation reducing output by nearly 1,850 MW.

Also, despite the State having tied up with wind power generators to generate 3,500 MW of wind power, only 500 MW was being generated and supplied, he added.

Mr. Nirmal Kumar sought the setting up of a nationwide energy forecasting centre for alerts on power shortfall.

World.title: Two arrested for attacking security guard with knife in Besant Nagar
World.content:
Two youngsters were arrested for allegedly attacking a 39-year-old security guard with a knife after he questioned one of them for harassing his daughter in Besant Nagar.

The victim, Dilthamai, a native of Nepal, works as a security guard at a house in Oorur Alcott Kuppam and lives there with his family. One of the accused, Sujith Mukhiya, a native of Bihar who works as a cook at the same house, had allegedly been harassing Dilthamai’s daughter, asking her to be in a relationship with him.

On the night of October 12, the woman informed her father about the harassment. When Dilthamai questioned Sujith Mukhiya, an argument broke out. The accused allegedly abused and assaulted him before Sujith Mukhiya and his friend, Amarjit Amar, attacked him with a vegetable-cutting knife and fled.

Dilthamai sustained bleeding injuries and is undergoing treatment at a private hospital. Based on his complaint, the Shastri Nagar police registered a case and launched an investigation. The police arrested the two accused, both natives of Madhubani in Bihar, on October 13 and seized the knife allegedly used in the attack.

The police said interrogation revealed that both men worked as cooks at the house where Dilthamai was employed as a security guard. The accused were produced before a court on October 13 and remanded to judicial custody.

World.title: Residents seek probe into collapse of peepal tree
World.content:
Residents and green activists have sought an inquiry into the sudden collapse of a decades-old peepal tree (Ficus religiosa) behind Muthumariamman temple at the Nemilichery Main Road–Ramaswamy Cross Street junction in Bharathipuram, Chromepet. The tree fell a few days ago despite there being no rain or strong winds at the time.

People for the People’s Movement general secretary and green activist Karthik Kannan suspects that the tree could have been damaged deliberately, but said the matter needed to be investigated. He said some people might have considered the tree obstructing their “view” of nearby places.

According to Kannan, when he visited the spot along with members of Pasumai Thayagam and other activists, they noticed traces of powders and chemicals near the tree’s roots. He said the tree had provided shade to residents and served as a habitat for birds.

“The tree appears to have lost its support after its roots were cut. We have sought an inquiry to establish whether it fell naturally or whether there was any human intervention,” he said.

Scores of residents, including women, paid their “last respects” to the tree on October 5. “Apart from the green cover, a tree adds an emotional and spiritual connect to the people of this land,” said Parvathi, a resident of the locality.

Kannan has submitted a complaint to the Chief Minister’s special cell and the Tahsildar, seeking an inquiry and requesting that samples found near the tree be collected and sent for laboratory testing.

However, some local residents said the tree might have lost its support after its roots were inadvertently damaged when workers dug up the area for a stormwater drain.

A nearby trader said electricity department workers had also been pruning branches of trees in the vicinity that posed a threat to transformers and overhead cables ahead of the monsoon. “As far as any miscreant angle to the tree’s collapse is concerned, we are not sure,” he said.

Green activists, however, said the incident highlighted the need for greater care in protecting mature trees, particularly those with ecological value. They alleged that trees were sometimes removed without adequate attention to scientific methods or due process.

Senior social activist Santhanam recalled that a 50-year-old banyan tree was removed in 2023 by the Railway and Highways authorities during the construction of the Radha Nagar subway. He said compensatory plantation norms required saplings to be planted for trees removed for development projects, but questioned whether such plantations were being properly monitored or documented.

Activists also suggested that authorities explore tree transplantation or translocation, wherever technically feasible, before deciding to remove mature trees.

Residents of Bharathipuram said their demand for an inquiry was not intended to oppose development works, but to prevent a recurrence of such incidents and promote greater awareness about protecting trees.

World.title: Fazl clarifies he criticised policies, not institutions after ministers allege he sought 'share' in KP governance
World.content:
Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Saturday clarified that his party’s remarks regarding the country’s security situation were directed at policies, not institutions, and termed the allegations levelled against him by federal ministers as character assassination.

A day earlier, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, without naming anyone, had claimed that a “head of a party” was “extremely upset” about not being appointed the governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The remarks came after Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights and raised doubts over its reasoning behind imposing governor’s rule that there was a lack of cooperation on counterterrorism.

Earlier on Saturday, State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry also rebuked the JUI-F chief for reportedly seeking his “share” in KP’s governance following the imposition of governor’s rule and an emergency in the province. Other federal ministers have also taken exception to Fazl’s remarks.

Addressing a press conference in Lahore on Saturday, Fazl stressed that his party’s criticism was directed at policies, not institutions, and was intended to bring about corrective action rather than undermine the sacrifices made in the fight against terrorism.

The senior politician called for an in-camera session of Parliament to review the country’s security situation and formulate a consensus-based policy to combat terrorism.

“Our only question is why the country has failed to eliminate terrorism. Let us sit together and find out why. Parliament is the most appropriate forum to discuss the issue and make decisions. Instead of ridiculing politicians, the government should take them on board in this fight so that we can move forward together,” he said.

“If Parliament is supreme, why are decisions taken in Rawalpindi while Parliament is simply told to follow them?” he remarked. “The issue is that this government is powerless. Decisions are taken somewhere else, and it implements them obediently,” he alleged.

The JUI-F maintained that Parliament should review the security situation and that the nation should be taken into confidence. If the public was expected to support the fight against terrorism and those engaged in it, he argued, the government should explain its decisions rather than impose “unilateral measures”.

Fazl reiterated his objection to the imposition of emergency rule in KP or any other part of the country. Recalling his family’s opposition to emergency rule in Balochistan during the 1970s, he said his father had resigned when the government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto imposed it in the province.

He described the recurrence of such measures as unfortunate, pointing out that the PP had repeatedly been associated with their imposition.

Questioning the rationale behind the emergency, governor’s rule and deployment of troops in KP, Fazl asked why the province should face such treatment when Balochistan was also grappling with the same level of terrorist violence, if not more.

The JUI-F chief urged the government to develop a shared national narrative and a consensus-based counterterrorism strategy instead of questioning his party’s position.

He went on to ask why the government engaged in negotiations with the PTI, which had been in power in KP, if the party was accused of supporting terrorists. “On top of it, both (the PTI and the government) say that they had reached a consensus on all points.”

Fazl then highlighted that around 250 of his party workers had lost their lives in terrorist violence, arguing that their sacrifices should not be ridiculed or overlooked. “How can a party whose members have laid their lives be accused of supporting terrorists?” he asked.

He also questioned why he was being singled out for criticism when political leaders, including former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, had at various times disagreed with the military leadership.

Ministers assail Fazl

Earlier on Saturday, addressing the media in Jaranwala, Chaudhry said, “I am upset. We did not expect Maulana sahab […] to consider this as spoils of war and seek his share in the absence of a PTI government in the province.”

He emphasised that the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP was not a political move aimed at strengthening the PML-N’s presence in the province by dismissing the PTI-led government.

“This was an administrative setup,” he said, adding that it had been formed with a “one-point agenda: combating terrorism”, rather than with an intention of establishing a political setup.

“This is not spoils of war,” he reiterated, adding that the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule in KP was an “immensely responsible” decision taken after every other option had been considered.

“I am unable to understand why Maulana sahab says that he was forced to accept defeat [in elections],” he said, arguing that Fazl’s party had been defeated by the PTI in KP and the Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party in Balochistan.

Chaudhry said the JUI-F was worthy of respect only if it stood by Pakistan’s interests.

The state minister also rejected the impression that the imposition of an emergency and governor’s rule was aimed at taking control of KP’s natural resources.

He also criticised Fazl for bringing up the 1971 separation of East Pakistan — now Bangladesh — from Pakistan in his recent statements.

“You bring up 1971 after losing the 2024 elections,” Chaudhry said.

“This KP setup is not about distributing shares, forming coalitions and governments, or engaging in politics,” he stressed, clarifying that only one member of the KP Advisory Council has a political background, as she represents the families of martyrs.

Chaudhry again offered to implement the National Action Plan and combat terrorism jointly with all stakeholders. “Politics is possible only where there is peace,” he said.

At the outset of his address, Chaudhry alleged that there must be “a relationship or a mutual interest arrangement between the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and the PTI”.

“Since 2015, no PTI leader, gathering or member has been targeted by terrorists,” Chaudhry said. “On the other hand, over the past 11 years, no political or religious party, security force, public office, funeral or wedding has been spared terrorist attacks.”

He said the federal government had exhausted all avenues to bring together stakeholders and urge them to condemn terrorism by naming those involved, whether the TTP, the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), or groups funded by India or Afghanistan.

The state minister claimed that in 2013, when the government decided to hold talks with the TTP and representatives were proposed by both sides, the TTP had nominated PTI founder Imran Khan to its committee.

He also alleged that the PTI founder had allowed the TTP to open offices in Peshawar.

During his address, Chaudhry also criticised the PTI, showing a press release issued by the TTP that condemned the dismissal of the party’s government.

Meanwhile, speaking at a press conference in Sialkot, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif criticised the JUI-F chief for constantly “targeting” the country’s security forces.

He declared that the sacrifices made by the security forces, officers, and the public in the fight against terrorism were “matchless”.

The defence minister referred to Fazl’s accusations that the emergency and governor’s rule were imposed to capture KP’s mineral resources, saying that he had shared a full list of people who had the mining contracts in KP.

Asif maintained that the whole PTI and opposition leadership was engaged by the government before the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule.

“But it was fruitless,” he said.

“The situation will improve in KP […] parliament can roll back the decision of imposing the emergency only if the improvement of the situation in the province is guaranteed,” the defence minister said.

He said that some individuals in KP were expecting to get a share in the administrative changes in the province.

“We will ensure free and fair elections. Whenever the time comes, everybody can take part in it,” he said.

Fazl’s remarks also prompted a response from KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, who has now been tasked with running the province under governor’s rule.

Kundi, referring to the JUI-F chief, asked whether “your land in the land belonging to martyrs in DI Khan is halal”.

“What you get is halal, what the other gets is haram,” he remarked.

The governor reaffirmed that the new KP administration would continue to function properly.

Fazl, who was involved in reducing tensions between the Centre and the KP government, has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in KP. He also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the two parties.

Addressing a rally in Multan on Thursday, Fazl further recalled that his party had expressed reservations over the merger of tribal areas into KP after the 25th Constitutional Amendment in 2018.

“We were not against the merger, but we said that it was an issue of the political future of the people of tribal areas,” he said, alleging that the people of those areas were not consulted on the merger.

He alleged governor’s rule was not imposed in Balochistan because the province’s chief minister “praises you”.

The next day, during an interaction with journalists, the interior minister said, “The head of a party is extremely upset over being denied a role in the new setup in KP and not getting the governorship.”

This politician, Naqvi alleged, had remained “dependent on the establishment for decades to advance his political career”.

“These are the same politicians who remained in politics for decades with the support of the establishment, and this politician even relied on the establishment to arrange air tickets for the members of his party,” he further alleged.

He said such politicians had little justification for criticising others now, particularly after having benefitted from the same system they currently denounced.

The same day, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz also railed against Fazl in a post on X.

She said it was not expected of a senior politician such as him to support those who facilitate terrorism — an apparent reference to the PTI, which the Centre accuses of backing terrorism.

She also criticised Fazl for his remarks about Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, seemingly referring to his comments during the Multan address about the centralisation of power.

The Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

The move has drawn criticism from the opposition, including Fazl, as well as Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Raja Nasir Abbas of the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan.

In the days preceding the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI which was in power in KP — had remained high since jailed former prime minister Imran Khan’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release.

Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results, while Fazl was cast as the man who could defuse heightening tensions between the Centre and the PTI. Both sides had held separate meetings with Fazl, reportedly for his intervention to help break the deadlock in the negotiations.

World.title: Security forces respond to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban along Kurram border: state media
World.content:
Security forces have responded to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban forces along the Pakistan-Afghanistan border in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Upper Kurram, state broadcaster PTV News reported on Saturday.

PTV News and state-run Associated Press of Pakistan (APP), which cited security sources, said the Afghan Taliban forces opened fire to “facilitate terrorists” along the border in Taldah sector of Upper Kurram.

The army responded using heavy weapons, destroying several Afghan Taliban posts and forcing their personnel to flee from there, PTV News reported.

Meanwhile, APP quoted security sources as saying that several personnel of the Afghan Taliban were “reportedly killed during the Pakistan Army’s retaliatory action along the Ghuzgarhi border”.

The sources further said that in the Upper Kurram sector, the army targeted the Afghan Taliban’s Topsar post and Shipola base camp with artillery fire, reportedly completely destroying the latter.

The exchange of fire was still ongoing in the area, APP quoted security sources as saying.

The border skirmishes come a day after the Foreign Office (FO) said that talks with Afghanistan could not be unconditional, but also rejected suggestions that Islamabad was unwilling to engage with its neighbour and said it would welcome sincere efforts by friendly countries to help resolve the dispute.

“Pakistan is not shying away from discussions or dialogue, including with representatives of Afghanistan. Pakistan would welcome any sincere efforts by friendly countries that could help address our legitimate security concerns and promoting regional peace and stability,” FO spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said at the weekly media briefing.

The statement came after Russia recently renewed its readiness to mediate between the two countries, although Islamabad denied the existence of any such initiative.

“At present, I am not aware of any separate, formal Russian mediation initiative being under discussion,” Khan said.

Pak-Afghan tensions

Ties between the two neighbours have been strained in the past few years as Islamabad continues to voice its concern over cross-border terrorism.

September witnessed another bout of conflict between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

On Sept 21, in response to recent major terrorist attacks in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts, with the government saying more than 28 terrorists were killed.

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar described the action as part of Operation Ghazab lil Haq, which was launched on the night of Feb 26 in response to unprovoked cross-border firing by the Afghan Taliban.

Days later, Pakistan shot down eight drones launched from across the border that had entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat. It was also reported that the Afghan Taliban engaged in unprovoked firing the night before near Kurram as security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Pakistan.

In retaliation for the drone incursion, Pakistan conducted “precision aerial and drone strikes” in 10 locations across Afghanistan.

A demarche was also delivered to the Afghan side on Sept 26 on account of the Sept 23 airspace violation by drones, the Foreign Office said.

World.title: Indian airlines barred from using Pakistani airspace until Nov 24 as ban extended
World.content:
Pakistan has extended its airspace ban for Indian aircraft for another month, until Nov 24, according to a Notice to Airmen (Notam) issued by the Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA).

The previous extension of the ban was set to expire on Oct 24.

“Pakistan airspace not available for Indian registered aircraft and aircraft operated/owned or leased by Indian airlines/operators, including military flights,” the Notam said.

According to the notice, the extension came into effect at 7:45pm on Saturday and will remain until 04:59am on Nov 24, 2026.

The country’s airspace is divided into two flight information regions (FIRs) — Karachi and Lahore, according to a Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority (PCAA) document from 2022.

Saturday’s Notam applies to both the Karachi (OPKR) and Lahore (OPLR) FIRs.

India and Pakistan closed their airspaces to each other’s airlines in late April 2025, when tensions between them escalated in the wake of a deadly attack in India-occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam.

On April 24, Pakistan’s top brass had announced a series of measures , including the closure of its airspace to all India-owned or Indian-operated airlines with immediate effect, as it retaliated against New Delhi’s slew of aggressive measures against the country.

New Delhi, without evidence, had alleged that Islamabad backed the Pahalgam attack. However, Pakistan had strongly denied any involvement and offered a neutral probe . The nuclear powers had the fiercest air battle in May, in which Pakistan said it downed seven Indian fighter jets.

Since then, Pakistan has extended the airspace ban several times, forcing Indian carriers to use longer and costlier routes.

For Air India, the country’s only carrier with a major international network, fuel costs rose by as much as 29 per cent and journey times by up to three hours on some long-haul routes, according to a document submitted to Indian officials last October.

The airline, owned by Tata Group and Singapore Airlines, estimated the Pakistan airspace closure’s impact on its profit before tax at $455 million annually — a significant amount given its fiscal 2024-25 loss stood at $439m.

World.title: Looting, blazes and clashes in France amid nationwide protests
World.content:
Police and protesters clashed violently in Paris and other French cities on Saturday on the sidelines of nationwide marches against soaring inflation, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off, multiple blazes set, and looters breaking into dozens of stores to strip them bare.

With just months to go before the two-round elections in April and May to choose Macron’s successor, the demonstrations follow weeks of high-school student blockades demanding better learning conditions.

Macron and his government were criticised by many of the demonstrators, who numbered 500,000 across the country, according to the CGT union. Authorities did not immediately give their estimate of the numbers.

Police used tear gas and water cannon against masked protesters in Paris and other cities who were throwing projectiles and aiming fireworks. Several parked cars were torched in the capital, and more than 130 arrests were made.

In the southern city of Saint-Etienne, a male protester had his hand blown off by a police crowd-control grenade, a police source told AFP. His maiming came after a 15-year-old lost his hand on October 5 to a police stun grenade during another protest in the city of Lens.

Protesters stand amid tear gas smoke as clashes erupt ahead of a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, at Place de la Republique in Paris, France on October 17, 2026. — AFP

The protests geared up with a handful of gatherings nationwide on Saturday morning, AFP reporters said.

In Lyon, protesters set ablaze a tourist office in the city centre, and smashed their way into town halls in the cities of Marseille and Lille, where they vandalised the premises before leaving.

Dozens of shops were looted, including many in Marseille, among them a Hermes boutique, an Apple store in Lille, several shops in Nice and at least one mobile phone outlet in Paris, AFP journalists saw.

A crowd of more than 300 protesters tried to move up Paris’s Champs-Elysees, home to flagship luxury stores. As police firing tear gas blocked their way, they yelled, “All cops are bastards”.

In the western city of Rennes, around 20 people set up a barricade using trash bins and large pallets on the outskirts of a shopping mall.

Christophe, a 47-year-old carpenter and former Yellow Vest protester who did not give his surname, said he was indignant after seeing what he viewed as police brutality against teenagers in recent weeks.

“We’ve reached the point where the repression is targeting our own children,” he told AFP.

A French national police officer fires tear gas during clashes prior to the start of a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, in Marseille, southern France on October 17, 2026. — AFP

The looting and confrontations with police were being carried out by masked youths on the sidelines of marches that were largely peaceful and which attracted people of all ages, including families with children.

Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire stressed that “the overwhelming majority of demonstrators” wanted to “march calmly”, but “acts of vandalism” were tarnishing their protest.

In Paris, tens of thousands marched across the east and north of the city in one major march, some shouting “Everyone hates the police” and “Macron, resign”.

Protesters wearing yellow vests face police as clashes erupt ahead of a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, at Place de la Republique in Paris, France on October 17, 2026. — AFP

One demonstrator, Jules Petrichor, 47, who had brought his son, said: “There was a good atmosphere and then suddenly they (the police) started gassing us, even though nothing was happening. Naturally that worsened things and the hot-heads got hot-headed.”

Another protester who gave his first name as Louis, 19, complained that police were trigger-happy any time there was a demonstration.

“We can’t protest any more, it’s frightening,” he said.

The country’s Yellow Vest movement, which eight years ago staged street protests against Macron’s government over planned fuel tax hikes, has called Saturday’s “yellow and youth” demonstrations. It has appealed to teachers and students, workers, pensioners and farmers to take part in the protests on the first day of half-term holidays.

The principal grievance was the cost of living — pushed up in part by the war in the Middle East — that has helped send inflation soaring in Europe as elsewhere.

But there were other issues too.

A protestor with a gas mask holds a French flag in front of a fire at the Boulevard des Capucines during a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, in Paris, France on October 17, 2026. — AFP

High school student Kamil Alahyan, 18, said he was protesting “for so many reasons — the elections coming up in 2027, politicians who lie, the ultra-rich who’ve been taking more and more wealth over the past 10 years”.

“For years we’ve had climate, economy and equality problems but the government is not doing anything about it,” said Agnes, a 50-year-old actor who did not give her second name.

Anae, a 24-year-old student who did not give her surname, said she was protesting because she did not have a “sustainable future”.

“Our planet’s burning. And we’ve got a government that doesn’t give a toss,” she said.

Le Pen blames ‘rioters’

Opposition politicians vying to succeed Macron have seized upon the protests.

Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, who has sided with the police, said on X: “Looting, pillaging, attacking police — rioters have once again sullied the October 17 demonstrations over the cost of living.” She claimed that the protesters’ demands had been “hijacked by the far left”.

Her far-left rival Jean-Luc Melenchon, insisted early Saturday that “everything is passing off peacefully”, while accusing television news of “flooding us with images of violence in dozens of cities”.

Several protesters sought to draw parallels with the French Revolution of 1789.

“It’s the Revolution — we’re taking the Bastille!” some shouted in Marseille during the forced entry of the mayor’s offices.

In the western city of La Rochelle, marchers streamed behind a placard reading: “Revolution or death.” And in the southern city of Montpellier, a giant blue sign reading “The people will win” was unfurled above a central square.

“The government is trembling and it’s right to tremble because when the French people are angry, they never let up,” Ryad Rani, the head of the LSU high school student representative body, told journalists in Paris.

World.title: Centre was compelled to impose emergency in KP, PM reiterates
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday reiterated that the Centre was “compelled” to impose emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa due to the provincial government’s lack of cooperation in countering terrorism.

The Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were also endorsed by the Parliament this week amid protests by the opposition.

On Saturday, PM Shehbaz visited the residence of Rashid Bashir Virk in Gujranwala to offer condolences on the demise of his father, late MNA Mahmood Bashir Virk.

After recalling the late PML-N lawmaker’s services, the premier stressed that the Centre was compelled to impose emergency in KP.

He said the Centre made a “last attempt”, referring to the rounds of talks held by a joint delegation of the PPP and the government with the opposition.

The hours-long second round, held on Oct 3, had ended without a breakthrough.

“They had talks with them (PTI) day and night, for 48 hours, and sat with the intention to settle matters from every aspect,” PM Shehbaz said, adding that a draft was ready under which the PTI was to call off its long march.

The prime minister highlighted that he had held multiple meetings with Sohail Afridi, the KP chief minister whose role now stands non-functional, as well as with his predecessor Ali Amin Gandapur.

“In every meeting, I tried my best to convey to him from the depths of my heart and with seriousness that KP is an extremely beautiful province and has very brave and honourable people, […] and I am always present in every way for their development and prosperity,” PM Shehbaz said.

The premier added that he assured the KP government of the Centre’s support in fighting against terrorism together to face the security challenges in the province.

PM Shehbaz said he had assured the chief minister that he would make the decisions regarding the administration, resources and necessities in consultation with him.

“But, unfortunately, despite all these efforts, thousands of our law enforcement agencies personnel, soldiers, officers and officers of the armed forces were sacrificing their lives every day to defend the homeland.”

The prime minister stressed that the federal government “made many efforts” regarding the situation, but there were “threats and long marches every other day in response”.

“Their past history is very horrific,” he remarked, recalling the 2014 sit-ins staged by the PTI at Islamabad’s D-Chowk during the tenure of his brother, Nawaz Sharif.

“Last year as well, you saw how the entire country was jammed by staging a sit-in in Islamabad,” he added, ostensibly referring to the PTI’s November 2024 protest that had resulted in clashes.

“This time as well, they had an entire plan of bloodshed,” he alleged.

The Oct 11 imposition of emergency and governor’s rule followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

Federal ministers alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a “nexus” with terrorist groups and asserted that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there.

The Centre and the PTI have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy, which was one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their October 3 talks .

World.title: Iran backs 'political process' to resolve Saudi-Houthi conflict
World.content:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that Tehran supports a “political process” to resolve the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthi rebels.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets, including energy facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a major attack last week.

“We support an inclusive and comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve the issue,” Araghchi said in a speech at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation in Baghdad.

Araghchi repeated Iran’s offer to mediate between the two sides. Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh previously said Riyadh has not responded to Iran’s overture.

On Friday, Iran denied having anything to do with the Houthi attacks, after Saudi Arabia accused Tehran of encouraging the group’s escalation.

In his speech, Araghchi also said “either we build security together, or we will endure insecurity together,” adding that Tehran was willing “to cooperate with all its brothers and neighbours to achieve the first option”.

The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July.

On Wednesday, Yemen’s Houthi rebels said they had targeted facilities belonging to Saudi Aramco, after Saudi officials reported a strike on a building in Riyadh housing the energy giant’s operations centre.

Powerful explosions also rattled the Saudi capital, as the coalition fighting the Houthis said it had intercepted a missile fired by the group towards Riyadh.

On Tuesday, Saudi Arabia launched strikes on Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen, targeting fuel and energy facilities it said were being used to support missile and drone attacks, as the Yemeni group threatened a “harsh and painful” response against Saudi airports, refineries and oil installations.

Hours later, Saudi authorities issued warnings of potential hostile aerial threats in the kingdom’s eastern province and Riyadh.

Loud explosions were heard near Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran, according to witnesses. Later, a Saudi energy ministry official confirmed the attack. Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency said that four people — two women, a man and a child — were wounded by debris from two intercepted Houthi cruise missiles in the capital and that 15 homes were damaged.

World.title: India's 'cockroach' movement founder released from police custody
World.content:
India’s Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke was released from detention on Saturday, a day after he was detained during a police crackdown on protests against the election authority.

Dipke, 31, was detained on Friday in New Delhi as he headed to join a rally that the CJP protest movement had called in the capital’s central Connaught Place district. He was arrested to prevent a breach of the peace, broadcasters NDTV and ​India Today reported.

He walked out of a police station on Saturday afternoon, waving to the media and giving a thumbs up as he was driven away, an AFP photographer saw.

“Abhijeet Dipke released,” CJP legal affairs chief Ratna Singh said on social media.

Opposition parties and CJP activists have defied a security crackdown, rallying to demand the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar after accusing the poll body of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.

More than 130 million voters were deleted ​during the revision. The Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Student activist Neha ​Bora, a prominent face of the protests, who was also detained on Friday as she ​tried to reach central Delhi with dozens of supporters, was released earlier on Saturday as well.

“Please, spare the people of India. ‌Impeach ⁠Gyanesh Kumar and halt SIR (special intensive revision), so that the ordinary citizens of this country can breathe a sigh of relief, feel at ease, and have their voting rights ensured,” Bora told ANI news agency after she was released.

Two other senior CJP leaders, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, were arrested on Oct 14 after entering Jantar Mantar, a decades-old protest site that police have declared off-limits for demonstrations. They remain in custody.

Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighbouring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls.

Rights groups and critics, however, say Modi’s government has eroded democratic freedoms during more than a decade in power, citing pressure on journalists, civil society groups and political opponents — allegations the government rejects.

A weeks-long sit-in by supporters of the movement earlier this year forced then-education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation over ​exam paper leaks.

World.title: Islamabad ATC summons Islamabad police chief in security breach case against Imaan and Hadi
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Saturday summoned the Islamabad police chief and issued show-cause notices to two police officials over the continued failure to produce the case record in the security breach case against lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her spouse, Hadi Ali Chattha.

The case pertains to the alleged disruption of a security route of an international cricket team and incitement to public unrest. Imaan and her husband were accused of removing barriers from the route. The couple was indicted in the case on Oct 7.

During Saturday’s hearing, ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain directed the two police officials to whom notices were issued to explain their failure to ensure the production of the record. He warned that they could face imprisonment if it was not presented before the court.

During the proceedings, the court expressed displeasure over the continued absence of the investigating officer and raised questions about the whereabouts of the case record.

A court official informed the judge that the investigating officer had travelled to Gilgit-Baltistan and had not returned.

The judge immediately summoned the superintendent (investigation) to explain the situation.

Advocate Riasat Ali Azad, representing the accused, told the court that the bail application had been filed on October 29 last year and notices had already been issued, but the proceedings could not move forward because the investigating officer failed to appear with the record.

He argued that in similar cases, another police official usually appeared with the case record when the investigating officer was unavailable. Questioning how long the court was expected to wait, Azad urged the judge to make a decision in accordance with the law.

Advocate Asif Irfan, vice chairman of the Islamabad Bar Council, observed that the court was not powerless, but had so far been unable to ensure the production of the record.

Advocate Aleem Abbasi, meanwhile, urged the judge to exercise his authority and decide the matter on merit. He added that the legal fraternity stood with the judiciary in defending its independence, but questioned how lawyers could secure justice for their own children if the judicial system failed to deliver it.

Advocate Zafar Khokhar also questioned under which law an investigating officer could take the case record away and leave court proceedings stalled.

Judge Zulqarnain, however, expressed displeasure over the tone adopted by some lawyers, deeming such conduct inappropriate and remarking that he was not influenced by vlogs or commentary and always conducted proceedings impartially.

After a short break in the proceedings, SP Khurram Ashraf and Deputy Superintendent (DSP) Naeem Yousuf appeared before the court.

The SP informed the judge that the investigating officer had travelled to Khaplu and would appear after he returned. The judge questioned the arrangement and asked when the officer would return, observing that everyone was waiting while the court had a case to decide.

When pressed for a definite timeline, DSP Yousuf said the investigating officer could take another 10 to 15 days to return.

The judge criticised the police for causing prolonged hardship to PTI workers through delays in their cases.

Expressing frustration over the situation and the alleged harassment of workers, the judge ordered the discharge of several individuals arrested in connection with the PTI’s long march.

The court subsequently issued show-cause notices to the SP and DSP, warning that failure to produce the case record could lead to proceedings for their imprisonment.

Islamabad Inspector General of Police Muhammad Sohail Chaudhry was also summoned for the next hearing on November 3.

The case

The lawyer couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the Islamabad High Court (IHC) and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president.
